sleepers.name: Collin Murray-Boyles
sleepers.why: 8 creators (Locked On, Steve St-Pierre, Noah Rubin, RotoWire, The Roster Report, Old Man Squad, Adam King, SportsEthos). Locked On: Now going in round 8 in the 80s more and more; Lloyd says it is not the wrong area but you hope to get him later. Steve St-Pierre: Steve took him in the eighth round as a young upside big, for the same reason the others took Sharpe and Maluach. D-Mac likes the upside. Noah Rubin: Yahoo ADP 113.7; goes 90 to 100 in expert mocks. Rubin thinks top-100 is justified: backup four and five behind Scottie Barnes and Jakob Poeltl with starter-level minutes, 28 to maybe 30 a night. Not a good shooter. RotoWire: Per 36 last year was about 14 points, 8 rebounds, 3 assists and 3 stocks. At pick 90 and 28 minutes you are fine with zero improvement; with second-year growth the stat profile looks like Ausar Thompson, a 'prime Draymond' type of fantasy impact. Weak FT% and few threes. The Roster Report: In line for an expanded role: Keller expects about 30 minutes as backup power forward and center with a lot of run next to Jakob Poeltl. Per-36 was roughly 18 points, 8 rebounds, 4 assists with about 3 stocks; at 30 minutes that projects to about 14 points, 6 rebounds, 3 assists and 2 stocks. Old Man Squad: Favorite flier on the board and the only remaining five-airplane player, at Yahoo rank 102. Besbris expects him to finish ranked in the 60s, a 30 to 40 slot jump (three or more rounds of value). Adam King: King says he is one of his guys but left him off the list because Besbris has covered him at length on other shows. SportsEthos: Mark says his playoff output is close to a floor: roughly a block and a steal per game, low-to-mid teens points, FG% in the high 60s, good boards and some assists. Already pushed Jakob Poeltl for centre minutes in the playoffs and should share the floor with Scottie Barnes and Kawhi Leonard.

sleepers.name: Khaman Maluach
sleepers.why: 7 creators (RotoWire, Fantasy on Points, Old Man Squad, FSAN, Locked On, Number Two Sports, SportsEthos). RotoWire: Put him in your queue: Fantrax ADP is 162 but he goes around pick 100 in expert mocks since the Mark Williams injury. Fantasy on Points: Leo took him at the ninth pick of the eighth round, the highest any of them had seen. He is betting on talent to win the starting centre job from Oso Ighodaro, though probably not on opening night. D-Mac and Steve call it aggressive and a little high. Old Man Squad: Yahoo rank 113, two airplanes with wide upside and downside. With Mark Williams possibly out for the year, Besbris guesses he and Oso Ighodaro split center minutes; 24 minutes makes him top 100 with a Kel'el Ware style game, 20 minutes probably does not. FSAN: Going in the 12th round, often the last pick. Likely starting center with Mark Williams out; 7-foot-2 shot blocker who can stretch the floor, projected for about 25 minutes. Risk: he fouls a lot. Locked On: Fantrax 173-202. 'Almost locked in' as the Suns' starter with a ton of buzz; Lloyd takes him over Oso Ighodaro. Played nine minutes a game last season. Upside sketch: 12 points, 10 rebounds, two blocks, 52% shooting with decent free throws; at 28 minutes, 14 and 11 with 2.5 blocks is about top 75. Number Two Sports: Lottery ticket for the end of the draft or last pick. Barely played as a rookie after going 10th in the 2025 draft, but averaged 19.5 points, 12.8 rebounds and 3.3 steals plus blocks in summer league. SportsEthos: With Mark Williams out until at least January or February he is forced to step up. Mark projects at least 20 minutes as a rebound, lob and shot-block centre who may hit some threes, which is the classic 20-minute centre who falls into standard-league value; Oso Ighodaro is more of a mid-20s-minutes switchable big. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

sleepers.name: Ty Jerome
sleepers.why: 7 creators (Locked On, Fantasy on Points, Old Man Squad, League Winner Sports, NBA Fantasy Bible, RotoWire, Number Two Sports). Locked On: Taken at 74; Lloyd 'really, really' wanted him over Dylan Harper. Has forward eligibility but not point guard eligibility. Fantasy on Points: Leo's seventh-round upside pick; his preseason usage is spiking and he fits a points/assists/threes/free-throw build. Old Man Squad: Moved up to Yahoo rank 88 so no longer qualifies as a flier, but Besbris still loves him there and says he is going to have a monster season. League Winner Sports: 83rd on consensus, Yahoo ADP about 115 (biggest Yahoo gap), ESPN about 93. Projected 16 points, 5 assists, 2.2 threes, 1.2 steals over 60 games at 48% FG and 87% FT. Little in rebounds or blocks; emerging as a point guard option for Memphis. NBA Fantasy Bible: Yahoo ADP 115 ('insane', a no-brainer), Fantrax 91.2. DMac thinks he breaks into the top 60 comfortably with a secure role; he was top 40 in 15 games at 22.6 minutes and 33.5% usage last year, which will not repeat exactly. RotoWire: Over his last 85 games at 21 minutes a night he grades out about 85th in 8-cat, so it is hard to get burned around pick 100 aside from injury. Devil's advocate: Scotty Pippen Jr. and Cam Spencer could cut into minutes. Number Two Sports: Mentioned in passing: Chris thinks Jerome is locked into a starting role in Memphis, possibly at shooting guard, and says he will be in his breakout video. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

sleepers.name: Grayson Allen
sleepers.why: 7 creators (RotoWire, NBA Fantasy Bible, Steve St-Pierre, The Roster Report, Locked On, Old Man Squad, Adam King). RotoWire: Opportunity in Charlotte with Coby White (calf) and Kon Knueppel hurt; tends to find minutes even when the roster is healthy as a good three-point shooter who can play the one or two. NBA Fantasy Bible, Steve St-Pierre: D-Mac's twelfth-round pick: should start the season well with Coby White and Kon Knueppel injured. Steve calls him a very safe, 9-cat friendly roster filler. The Roster Report: Beneficiary of Kon Knueppel and Coby White being hurt to start the season. Elite threes with a usable points floor and a little rebounds and assists; a late-round or early waiver target. Locked On: In Lloyd's queue for round 11 before being sniped at about 128. Old Man Squad: Three 'burgers' (short-term streamer value) as a last-round pick. Charlotte is without Coby White and Kon Knueppel probably through the start of the season; when Allen gets real minutes and usage he has run at top 40. Good for a fast start in head-to-head, expect it to fade when others return. Adam King: Round 12 pick nobody is talking about. Charlotte's wing bench is thin (Royce O'Neale, Sion James, Tidjane Salaun, Buddy Hield), so King expects 25 to 27 minutes of threes and steals; a 3-and-D upside flyer.

sleepers.name: Austin Reaves
sleepers.why: 6 creators (Locked On, RotoWire, NBA Fantasy Bible, Old Man Squad, League Winner Sports, Adam King). Locked On: ESPN dropped him from 50 to 64 in its category re-rank, which Lloyd treats as absurd; he had already called 50 a steal. RotoWire, NBA Fantasy Bible: Labelled 'safe' but DMac ranks him 16 to 17 in 9-cat with ADP slightly after that: a really safe second-rounder with first-round upside. Only clear category weakness is blocks. Old Man Squad: Yahoo 21, bright green. About top 20 in 9-cat and maybe top 14 in 8-cat. Was 15th in 9-cat early last year on 18 shots; expects mid-to-high 20s scoring with steals falling from 1.4 to about 1.1. Much better than the players around him. League Winner Sports: D-Mac ranks him 16 in 9-cat and sees first-round potential: efficient, great FT%, hits threes, bigger role with no LeBron. Matt almost agrees a first-round finish is possible. James disagrees: defences will scheme for him without LeBron and 16 is 'too rich'. D-Mac would not touch him this early in points leagues. Adam King: In the second-round, early-third discussion with some upside. Similar skill set to Shai.

sleepers.name: Dejounte Murray
sleepers.why: 6 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, Steve St-Pierre, League Winner Sports, RotoWire, Old Man Squad, Locked On). NBA Fantasy Bible, Steve St-Pierre: D-Mac took him in the fifth and sees top-40 to top-50 upside as a steals guy, though he has not been fully healthy the last few seasons. Steve argues Murray may be better than Darius Garland in 9-cat because he is a bit more efficient. League Winner Sports: 44th on consensus, Yahoo ADP about 70, ESPN about 68. Projected 7.4 assists, 6.5 rebounds, 1.7 steals, 83% FT over 66 games. Cost is 3.6 turnovers (most in the video, counted on Yahoo) and 46% FG. RotoWire: Would be a massive steal in the 60s; assumes 30 minutes because the Pelicans are committed to him. Alex would draft him over Derrick White (Yahoo ADP 44) and says they should at least be closer. Old Man Squad: Pre-rank fell to 64 (early sixth). Dan thinks he is a second-rounder in 8-cat and a third-rounder in 9-cat, about 35th, and will take him at 48 or 49. His fifth-round pick from every draft slot. Locked On: Yahoo rank 64, ADP 67; Fantrax 55; ESPN rank 57. Was better than this last season in limited minutes off a torn Achilles; Lloyd calls him probably a top 30-35 player and does not expect him to sit back-to-backs. Trade and Jeremiah Fears are the wrinkles.

sleepers.name: Day'Ron Sharpe
sleepers.why: 5 creators (Locked On, NBA Fantasy Bible, Old Man Squad, Number Two Sports, RotoWire). Locked On: Lloyd's 'number one target' at pick 95; taken one pick before him at 94. NBA Fantasy Bible: D-Mac took him at the sixth pick of the eighth round, maybe slightly early, expecting a huge breakout as the Nets' centre. Old Man Squad: Yahoo rank 90, upgraded from zero to two airplanes (about even money). Started and played 18 minutes with the starters alongside Michael Porter Jr. and Julius Randle in the first preseason game with two blocks. Concerns are FG% and blocks; steals and rebounds are safe. Number Two Sports: Bonus pick, ADP in the 90s, and Chris's favorite center target for managers who wait on the position and miss Zach Edey and Kel'el Ware. Career per-30-minute line of 16.3 points, 13.8 rebounds and 1.5 blocks; in six starts last year he averaged 12.3 points, 8.3 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 2.0 steals and 1.2 blocks. RotoWire: Went around pick 100. Alex prefers him narrowly over Maluach because he has been an elite per-minute player for years, so he feels safer with similar upside.

sleepers.name: Jalen Suggs
sleepers.why: 5 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, Old Man Squad, League Winner Sports, Locked On, Number Two Sports). NBA Fantasy Bible: Fell to D-Mac in the ninth round; he still expects him to be solid. Steve nearly took him. Old Man Squad: Yahoo rank 95, four airplanes (cut from five live because of health). Besbris thinks he is near top 55 in straight 9-cat on a per-game basis, about 40 slots of value, but with more games-played risk than Josh Hart or Keegan Murray. League Winner Sports: 81st on consensus, ESPN ADP about 137, Yahoo about 109. Projected 1.7 steals, 2.2 threes, 5.2 assists over 58 games at 87% FT. Costs 43% FG and 2.7 turnovers, which hurts more on Yahoo where turnovers count. Locked On: Probably a top-70 player if he stayed healthy; always worth the late chance. Number Two Sports: ADP over 100 (ninth or tenth round) because he has played more than 58 games only once. Per game he was borderline top 50 last year: 13.8 points, 2.1 threes, 5.5 assists, 1.8 steals and 0.7 blocks in 27.6 minutes. Chris will actively target him as a bet on one healthy season. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Adam King.

sleepers.name: Dyson Daniels
sleepers.why: 5 creators (Locked On, Hustle Sports, League Winner Sports, Old Man Squad, Adam King). Locked On: Went at pick 43; Lloyd says he should go there (round 4) but usually falls to the fifth round. Hustle Sports: Steals specialist available late in drafts; elite defensive production with decent scoring. Shooting is not his strength, so pair him with scorers taken earlier. League Winner Sports: James would rather have him than Onyeka Okongwu to round out the top 50. Old Man Squad: Ranked in the 40s by Dan; fine around 50. Adam King: Seen as a one-category steals player but King stresses the rest: 6.8 rebounds last year (5.9 the year before) from a guard-eligible player, five to five and a half assists on a Hawks team without a high-assist guard, 13 to 14 points. Threes fell to 0.3 from 1.1 and FT% was barely 60. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

sleepers.name: John Collins
sleepers.why: 5 creators (Locked On, NBA Fantasy Bible, Old Man Squad, RotoWire, Number Two Sports). Locked On: 'Screaming at me at value' around pick 115, where he was taken. NBA Fantasy Bible: D-Mac likes him late in the eighth round in his new role in Detroit. Old Man Squad: Yahoo rank 97, three airplanes: should beat his slot by a little. Ranked just behind Wiggins and McDaniels and ahead of Jabari Smith Jr. RotoWire: Starts at the four with no real backup four (Ron Holland, Taurean Prince), so 32 to 33 minutes is possible. Detroit lacks reliable scorers beyond Cade Cunningham and Duren. Alex has taken him in the 80s and prefers him to Myles Turner in that range. Number Two Sports: ADP close to 120. Signed a three-year deal with the Pistons and should take the power forward spot Tobias Harris held. Chris sees him as the third scoring option behind Cade Cunningham and Jalen Duren with more lobs and spacing. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

sleepers.name: Kel'el Ware
sleepers.why: 5 creators (Hustle Sports, NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports, FSAN, Old Man Squad). Hustle Sports: One of T-Will's favourites. No Giannis and no Bobby Portis in Milwaukee, and Myles Turner is more perimeter-based. Averaged 11 points in about 25 to 27 minutes last year and is shooting more threes in preseason; at 30 to 35 minutes he could be a 17-point, 11-rebound player with blocks. Not an overspend in the 75 to 85 range. NBA Fantasy Bible: Went early in the sixth round (pick 63); D-Mac is 'loving Kel'el Ware for this season'. League Winner Sports: 54th on consensus, ESPN ADP about 108, Yahoo about 75. Center who shoots threes: projected 1.4 threes, 10.2 rebounds, 1.4 blocks over 73 games with under one turnover. Dents FT% slightly (70% on few attempts); listed second at center on Milwaukee's depth chart so minutes are the question. FSAN: ADP 76 (round 8). Averaged about 11 points and 9 rebounds with a steal, a block and a three last year. Clark sees a comfortable top-100 player pushing top 70 to 75 and would reach to about 70, especially if you skipped big men early. Old Man Squad: Pre-rank 69; could be top 50. Preferred sixth-round pick as the lightning-in-a-bottle choice for blocks and FG%, though he may not last to 72. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by League Winner Sports.

sleepers.name: Zach Edey
sleepers.why: 5 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, Fantasy on Points, Locked On, League Winner Sports, RotoWire). NBA Fantasy Bible, Fantasy on Points: Leo took him at the ninth pick of the sixth round; all three say it is not a reach. D-Mac sees top-30 upside if healthy, and Leo calls him a potential league winner if he plays 60-plus games. Locked On: ESPN rank 113 categories, 116 points. Top-50 upside in both formats. He barely played last season with a foot/ankle problem, but he was healthy through college and played 66 games as a rookie; 66 games at 26 minutes would be 'one of the biggest smashes you will see'. League Winner Sports: 60th on consensus, ESPN ADP about 124 (biggest gap in the video), Yahoo about 76. Projected 11 rebounds and 1.8 blocks on 62% FG; almost nothing in threes or steals, 78% FT is neutral. Projected for only 57 games. RotoWire: Alex is most comfortable taking him in the 70s (seventh or eighth round) because the centers after him are much riskier: Jusuf Nurkic becomes the best center on the board.

sleepers.name: Ajay Mitchell
sleepers.why: 5 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, Old Man Squad, FSAN, Locked On, RotoWire). NBA Fantasy Bible: D-Mac got him in the eleventh round after planning to take him in the tenth; says he is being overlooked relative to ADP. Old Man Squad: Two airplanes, last player in the 113 to 126 tier. Last year: 13.5 points, 1 three, 3 rebounds, 3.5 assists, 1.2 steals on good percentages in 25.5 minutes, finishing 106th. Minutes should rise with Lu Dort, Wiggins and Isaiah Joe gone; Besbris will drop him if usage falls. FSAN: Projected ADP about 115 (round 12). Was at 16 to 17 points before an injury last year and finished around 13 points, 3 rebounds, 3 assists and a steal. The only Thunder guard besides Shai who can run the offense; Caruso and Cason Wallace do not handle or facilitate. A top-100 season would be two to three rounds of profit. Locked On: ESPN rank 243. Lloyd does not think he starts and thinks his value gets overblown, but OKC lost Joe, Dort and Wiggins and wants Gilgeous-Alexander more off the ball. Value goes 'through the roof' if Shai is hurt. RotoWire: ADP around 115. Was top 100 last year while starting only 16 games, and the Thunder lost Lu Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins' minutes. Projects to about 15 points, 5 rebounds, 5 assists with a steal and a three, near 90% FT and close to 50% FG; seen as having a higher ceiling than Cason Wallace.

sleepers.name: Chet Holmgren
sleepers.why: 5 creators (Locked On, NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports, Old Man Squad, Adam King). Locked On: ESPN rank 71, which over-indexes on Chet hate; 'even easier' than Jaylen Brown in round 6 of an ESPN category league. Lloyd is against him at his Yahoo points price. NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports: D-Mac ranks him 22 while many have him outside the top 30 (Josh Lloyd criticised the pick). Does not hurt efficiency and brings blocks, threes and FT% from a big, a rare combination; not long ago he was viewed as close to a first-rounder in 9-cat. Matt and James are both fine with 22. Old Man Squad: Favorite of the realistic third-round options: easiest path to beating his pre-rank by average and totals. Adam King: ADP 25.4. Finished 18th last year, top 14 over the last three months and top 11 over the last two; people are off him after a poor playoffs. Blocks, rebounds, threes, near 55% FG and no damage at FT%. King thinks he can be top 15 again with mid-first-round upside; the one hole is points. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

sleepers.name: OG Anunoby
sleepers.why: 5 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, Steve St-Pierre, Hustle Sports, Old Man Squad, Locked On). NBA Fantasy Bible, Steve St-Pierre: Sixth-round pick described as 'safe as houses', used to offset the injury risk of Anthony Davis and Kyrie Irving on the same roster. Hustle Sports: The model balanced 9-cat wing: decent scoring, threes, rebounds, steals and blocks with low turnovers and good efficiency. The raw stats look 'mid' but he is very valuable in this format. Old Man Squad: Besbris likes him where he is being drafted: finished 35th last year on 17.5 points, 5 rebounds, 2 assists, 1.6 steals and 0.7 blocks with good percentages. His steals hold regardless of minutes. Locked On: Yahoo rank 71, ESPN rank 71. Lloyd would happily take him there. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

sleepers.name: Onyeka Okongwu
sleepers.why: 5 creators (Steve St-Pierre, Locked On, NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports, Old Man Squad). Steve St-Pierre: Steve's guy, taken in the fifth round as a safe pick that fills a centre slot in a two-centre league and balances a risky start. Locked On: Lloyd loves the player and took him at about pick 76 in a Yahoo points mock; the issue is only the rank of 49. NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports: Ranked 50 as a solid, safe centre, replacing the injured Kon Knueppel in the top 50. Matt agrees. James is lower, citing past frustration with Hawks rotation decisions, and would rather have Dyson Daniels at 50. Old Man Squad: Probably a 40s-ranked player; fine but a little boring in the late 40s. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

sleepers.name: Reed Sheppard
sleepers.why: 5 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, Steve St-Pierre, Old Man Squad, Locked On, Number Two Sports). NBA Fantasy Bible, Steve St-Pierre: Fell to the thirteenth round, which surprised D-Mac given his pedigree and clear role on Houston. Steve notes he and Fred VanVleet may cancel each other out when both are healthy. Old Man Squad: Yahoo pre-rank 141, three airplanes and Besbris's favorite of the deep three-airplane group. Role in Houston is unclear but 25 to 26 minutes puts him well inside the top 100, and his stat set looked translatable rather than inflated. Locked On: Clear skill set but 'probably hated by the coach'; Lloyd does not really believe in it. Number Two Sports: Late lottery ticket. Slow start last year after being thrown in by the VanVleet injury, then productive after the All-Star break with strong steals and a well-rounded line. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

sleepers.name: Yaxel Lendeborg
sleepers.why: 5 creators (RotoWire, Steve St-Pierre, Fantasy on Points, The Roster Report, Locked On). RotoWire: Minutes-and-opportunity flyer because nobody on the Warriors roster can be trusted to stay healthy (Curry, Draymond Green, Porzingis; Jimmy Butler out; Moses Moody not healthy to start). Alex believes in his talent. Steve St-Pierre, Fantasy on Points: Taken by Leo in the tenth round. Clear path to minutes because the Warriors are banged up: Leo doubts Steph Curry plays 70 games, Kristaps Porzingis returns soon, or Draymond Green plays 60. Steve says he is in the rotation whether Golden State competes or struggles. The Roster Report: ADP 142. Essentially already named a starter next to Stephen Curry, so 28 to 30 minutes is the working assumption. Preseason lines of 17 points, 9 rebounds, 2 assists, 1 block in 21 minutes (Oct 6) and 23 points, 10 rebounds, 6 assists, 2 steals, 1 block on 10-of-14 (Oct 10). Locked On: In Lloyd's queue; went 98 in round 9 after another great preseason game. Lloyd thinks he and Podziemski start.

sleepers.name: Darius Garland
sleepers.why: 5 creators (Noah Rubin, NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports, Adam King, Locked On). Noah Rubin: Rubin says he was better after the trade to the Clippers than he was in Cleveland, is fully healthy for the first time in a while after a multi-season toe issue, and now runs the team with Brandon Ingram out. Could average career highs. NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports: Ranked 44. James thinks he can give 21 points and 8 assists on decent efficiency and is happy to take the risk in the early 40s. D-Mac expects a very high-usage start to the season. Risks: a struggling Clippers organisation and trade rumours. Adam King: King took him at 49 and is pretty high on him there: the Clippers have no one other than Garland and Brandon Ingram, so he will do a lot. Locked On: Yahoo rank 61, ADP 58; Fantrax 54; ESPN rank 53, ADP 90. 'Probably a third round player'; Lloyd targets him in the 40s. Rookie Keaton Wagler is not a threat and Garland is the Clippers' best player.

sleepers.name: Ryan Rollins
sleepers.why: 4 creators (Locked On, Hustle Sports, Fantasy on Points, Old Man Squad). Locked On: Taken at 50. Lloyd is no longer worried about him losing his spot in Milwaukee. Hustle Sports: Named as an equally worthy fallback if you miss Tyler Herro, since Herro has competition for the lead role in Milwaukee. Fantasy on Points: Leo likes him at the end of the seventh as a surprise candidate, despite the guard logjam in Milwaukee. Old Man Squad: Aside while discussing the Bucks guards: Besbris loves Rollins in fantasy this year even though he is not great at creating his own shot.

sleepers.name: Kevin Porter Jr.
sleepers.why: 4 creators (Locked On, Hustle Sports, Old Man Squad, Number Two Sports). Locked On: Taken at about 143. Lloyd cannot figure out how Milwaukee uses him, but he has a real chance of landing well above his draft slot, unlike Anthony Black. Hustle Sports: Named alongside Ryan Rollins as an equally worthy fallback if you miss Tyler Herro. Old Man Squad: Yahoo rank 128, three airplanes for the most upside of the 18 deep fliers: he was a second-round value in 33 minutes last year. Came off the bench for 19 minutes in preseason behind a crowded guard group, but the Bucks lack shot creators besides Tyler Herro, so 25-plus minutes is plausible. Number Two Sports: ADP around 120, worth a tenth-round pick for the ceiling. In 38 games last year he ranked ninth per game in 9-cat: 17.4 points, 7.4 assists, 5.2 rebounds, 2.2 steals, 1.2 threes on 47% FG while Giannis missed time.

sleepers.name: Myles Turner
sleepers.why: 4 creators (Steve St-Pierre, Old Man Squad, Locked On, RotoWire). Steve St-Pierre: Fell to Steve in the ninth round; Steve expects a bounce-back season and thinks the pairing with Kel'el Ware may work, with a trade also possible. Old Man Squad: Yahoo rank 118, three airplanes, second favorite in the 113 to 126 tier. Expected to play about 27 to 28 minutes and supply a bunch of blocks. Locked On: ADP 128. Pretty bad last season, which Lloyd reads as single-season myopia; he does not think Kel'el Ware should replace him. 'Let's do it.' RotoWire: ADP around 87. Alex sees a possible bounce-back: the Bucks need him to play well to move him, and new coach Taylor Jenkins did well with another floor-spacing five in Jaren Jackson Jr. (Whalen fades Turner in the DO NOT DRAFT video.) Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by RotoWire.

sleepers.name: Paul Reed
sleepers.why: 4 creators (Locked On, NBA Fantasy Bible, Number Two Sports, RotoWire). Locked On: Lloyd dislikes him at 108, where he sometimes goes, but wants him at 140. NBA Fantasy Bible: Getting hype as a late-round pick 'for good reason' after a strong playoffs while Jalen Duren struggled and his contract is unresolved. Number Two Sports: Deep sleeper contingent on Jalen Duren's situation, which was unresolved when the video was recorded. In 11 starts last year he averaged 15.2 points, 7.6 rebounds, 3.2 assists and 3.9 steals plus blocks in 26.9 minutes. RotoWire: ADP around 140. Per-minute monster in the Day'Ron Sharpe mold; late upside play if Jalen Duren misses time or leaves Detroit.

sleepers.name: Trey Murphy III
sleepers.why: 4 creators (Locked On, League Winner Sports, NBA Fantasy Bible, Old Man Squad). Locked On: ESPN rank 46. Finished 11th in straight nine-cat rankings last season; Lloyd would not take him at 20 but calls 46 easy and does not buy the 'role instability' argument. League Winner Sports: 24th on consensus, ESPN ADP about 75, Yahoo about 39. Projected 3.4 threes, 21.4 points, 89% FT and 1.3 steals over 67 games. Soft spots are 46% FG and thin blocks. NBA Fantasy Bible: D-Mac ranks him 29 (consensus 23) and calls the per-game value a no-brainer; last year he smashed an ADP around 50. James is higher, around 19-20, citing threes, steals, blocks and efficiency plus Dejounte Murray running the offence. Matt sides with D-Mac's lower rank because of the Pelicans. Old Man Squad: Going late third; expected to beat pre-rank by average and totals. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

sleepers.name: Gui Santos
sleepers.why: 4 creators (RotoWire, Locked On, Fantasy on Points, Number Two Sports). RotoWire: Same Warriors opportunity play; was a legitimate must-roster 9-cat player for the last couple of months last season. Locked On: 'Going to start opening night, it looks like.' Went 121. Fantasy on Points: Leo's last pick; expects a lot of minutes whether or not he starts because Golden State is thin, and he doubles as a mini handcuff with Yaxel Lendeborg. Number Two Sports: Chris's favorite deep-league sleeper and a pick with one of his last two selections in nearly every draft (he admits a Warriors bias). Fits Steve Kerr's system, scores efficiently, rebounds, passes and adds a few steals; could reach the top 100 if he gets minutes and usage.

sleepers.name: Jaden McDaniels
sleepers.why: 4 creators (Hustle Sports, Locked On, Old Man Squad, League Winner Sports). Hustle Sports: Balanced wing whose value goes beyond scoring: decent points and rebounds, strong defensive nights, and he gets minutes. Locked On: Round-8 must-draft at Yahoo rank 92. He was about 84th last season and Lloyd thinks he has another step in him. Minnesota adds a full year of Ayo Dosunmu and Jonathan Kuminga but no longer has Naz Reid or Julius Randle. Old Man Squad: Yahoo rank 92, three airplanes. Projected around 75 with threes plus steals and blocks and slightly better percentages than Wiggins. League Winner Sports: 65th on consensus, Yahoo ADP about 91, ESPN about 100. Projected 1.2 steals, 1.1 blocks, 1.5 threes over 73 games at 51% FG and 81% FT; hurts you almost nowhere and played 73 games last season.

sleepers.name: Keegan Murray
sleepers.why: 4 creators (Old Man Squad, League Winner Sports, Locked On, Number Two Sports). Old Man Squad: Yahoo rank 99, four airplanes: expected to beat his slot by one to three rounds with a solid fantasy season and better games-played outlook than Suggs. League Winner Sports: 95th on consensus, Yahoo ADP about 120, ESPN about 124. Low-maintenance forward: projected 1.9 threes, 1.1 blocks, 6 rebounds over 72 games with 1.2 turnovers and 81% FT. Mild cost is 45% FG. Locked On: Yahoo rank 116, ADP 120; ESPN ADP 124. Sacramento cleared out DeRozan, Westbrook and Schroder. Lloyd expects about a top-100 season and is happy to take him in round 10; unsure last year's shot blocking holds. Number Two Sports: ADP 121. In 23 games last year he ranked 53rd per game in 9-cat with over 1 steal and 1.6 blocks. With DeRozan and Westbrook gone and Sabonis healthy, Chris projects 30-plus minutes and 14 to 15 shots with five or six threes. Floor about 100, ceiling top 60 to 70, with some regression expected in steals and blocks. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

sleepers.name: Neemias Queta
sleepers.why: 4 creators (Old Man Squad, League Winner Sports, Locked On, Adam King). Old Man Squad: Yahoo rank 107, three airplanes. Besbris sees him inside the top 90, at least a round of value, and close to four airplanes if he went half a round later. League Winner Sports: 90th on consensus, Yahoo ADP about 117 (second-biggest Yahoo gap), ESPN about 136. Projected 66% FG, 8.2 rebounds, 1.3 blocks over 73 games with about one turnover. No threes and 73% FT is a small dent; camp reports say he looks much improved on offense. Locked On: Lloyd says he 'really should have included' him on the main list of late targets. Adam King: Named as a really solid second-center target in the pick-100 range; DMac took him late in a FG%/rebounds/defense build. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

sleepers.name: Cason Wallace
sleepers.why: 4 creators (RotoWire, Old Man Squad, League Winner Sports, Locked On). RotoWire: Named again as a late-draft name the host is monitoring. Old Man Squad: Yahoo rank 123, three airplanes, third favorite in his tier. Likely starter for the Thunder and a big source of steals. League Winner Sports: 93rd on consensus, Yahoo ADP about 118, ESPN about 137. Steals specialist: projected 2.0 steals and 1.6 threes over 75 games with under one turnover. You give up scoring (10 points) and FG% (44%). Locked On: Fantrax ADP 115, Yahoo ADP 118, rank 128. Lloyd is fairly certain he starts; a steals source who could reach 31 minutes and pick up playmaking with Shai off the ball. 'Has to be drafted', but not too high. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

sleepers.name: Egor Demin
sleepers.why: 4 creators (Fantasy on Points, Number Two Sports, Locked On, SportsEthos). Fantasy on Points: Leo's twelfth-round pick; one of three young prospects he says to target late in real drafts. D-Mac also loves him. Number Two Sports: Deep-league breakout pick around ADP 120. Showed growth as a facilitator as a rookie with an improving three-point shot; Chris says camp clips show an expanded offensive game. Part of Brooklyn's young core, so minutes should not be a concern. Locked On: Year two after finishing outside the top 200 while managing a foot issue. Looks bigger and stronger. Lloyd projects about 120th with a wide band up to 80th: roughly 17 points, five rebounds, 4.5 assists, 1.4 steals, 2.5 threes on 45% shooting. SportsEthos: Clearly ahead of Brooklyn's other second-year players and most likely starting. Bankable three-point shooting, with assists, boards, steals and some points; added physicality in summer league and can play off Julius Randle.

sleepers.name: Moussa Diabate
sleepers.why: 4 creators (Noah Rubin, RotoWire, Old Man Squad, Locked On). Noah Rubin: Looks set to start at center for Charlotte and is going in the last round or undrafted. One of the best offensive rebounders in the league on a team that will fire a ton of threes; can average a double-double or at least double-digit rebounds with high FG% and few turnovers. RotoWire: Alex is less high but notes backup bigs who will play 18 minutes (Paul Reed, Maxime Raynaud) often go ahead of a starter who played 26 minutes last year. Rebounds and FG% specialist. Old Man Squad: One airplane. Has a reliable starting job to open the year, which gives him a shot at top 100 early, especially for teams punting points or FT%. Locked On: Expected to start; Lloyd prefers him to Hannes Steinbach about 90/10.

sleepers.name: Scotty Pippen Jr.
sleepers.why: 4 creators (The Roster Report, FSAN, Locked On, Number Two Sports). The Roster Report: Flagged in Keller's preseason role reports as an integral part of Memphis' rotation: 98th percentile steal rate, 93rd percentile defensive rating, 87th percentile deflection rate. Projects as a double-digit scorer with about 4 rebounds and 5 to 6 assists. FSAN: Honorable mention with a cheaper ADP than Ty Jerome. Proven points-and-assists guard with a steal who could play about 30 minutes, though he may be asked to do less with Jerome healthy. Locked On: Healthy 'defensive demon who can shoot'; unlikely to start over Ty Jerome but possible. Number Two Sports: Last-pick shot. Chris expects either Pippen or Cam Spencer to start at point guard for Memphis and prefers Pippen, whose scoring, playmaking, steals and threes are a better fantasy base. He was hurt most of last year, which Chris writes off.

sleepers.name: Jalen Williams
sleepers.why: 4 creators (Noah Rubin, NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports, SportsEthos). Noah Rubin: Yahoo rank 34 (was 43, then 38). Rubin says people are far too low: last year was derailed by a wrist injury that cost him the offseason and camp, then two hamstring injuries, and it was his worst statistical season. He was 24th in 9-cat the last time he was healthy; NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports: D-Mac ranks him 35 (consensus 37, ADP 38). James is higher: people are fading him for last season but he was All-NBA the year before, and James expects a big bounce-back and elite defensive versatility. SportsEthos: ADP about 41-42 after an 8-cat per-game rank of 81 in a lost season with a serious wrist injury. Dr. A calls 40 a steal if he is healthy.

sleepers.name: James Harden
sleepers.why: 4 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, Steve St-Pierre, Fantasy on Points, Old Man Squad). NBA Fantasy Bible, Steve St-Pierre, Fantasy on Points: Went at the fourth pick of the fourth round (pick 40), called fantastic, massive value. Steve had looked at him in the second round and Leo nearly took him in the third instead of Trae Young. Old Man Squad: Guard-build piece you should be able to get in the third round. Was number 8 last year in punt FG% plus punt TO. Stat profile like LaMelo with slightly better FG% and slightly lower steals. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Old Man Squad.

sleepers.name: Paul George
sleepers.why: 3 creators (Locked On, NBA Fantasy Bible, Old Man Squad). Locked On: Projected by Lloyd as a top-30 player available after pick 50. Went in round 5 here; 'in a lot of drafts you will not need to' reach that early. NBA Fantasy Bible: D-Mac took him in the seventh. He was a top-40 9-cat player last season, part of his missed time was a suspension and not health, and he looked great next to Jayson Tatum in preseason. Expect maintenance games. Old Man Squad: Besbris repeats that one of his two strongest takes of draft season is that Paul George is going to have a monster season (the other being the Jaylen Brown fade). No stats given in this episode. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Adam King, RotoWire.

sleepers.name: Brandin Podziemski
sleepers.why: 3 creators (RotoWire, Locked On, Number Two Sports). RotoWire: Worth rostering even though people dislike him: he will get usage and minutes because Steve Kerr likes him. Locked On: Taken at 98, preferred to Ja Morant. Number Two Sports: More breakout watch than sleeper; Chris sees a top 75 finish. Last year: 13.8 points, 5.1 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 1.1 steals, 2 threes on 45.5% FG, and he has improved every season. Golden State's backcourt is thin behind an aging Curry and injury-prone De'Anthony Melton, so usage is available. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On, Old Man Squad.

sleepers.name: Zach LaVine
sleepers.why: 3 creators (Locked On, Noah Rubin, Number Two Sports). Locked On: Was going around 120 in a lot of drafts; went 85 here as his price climbs. Noah Rubin: Rubin likes him more than his ADP, which is 'pretty low right now', though he may not be in Sacramento all season. Number Two Sports: ADP outside the top 100. Was terrible last year amid injuries and a tanking team, with dips in every meaningful stat, but he is 31, an unrestricted free agent after the season, and likely to be traded. Chris thinks 20-plus points with three to four assists and rebounds is realistic and that he can be a top 75 player again. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Old Man Squad.

sleepers.name: Brandon Miller
sleepers.why: 3 creators (Locked On, NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports). Locked On: Went 30, which Lloyd calls reasonable: 'going to have some pretty good numbers this season'. NBA Fantasy Bible: Second wild card. Yahoo ADP 45, ESPN 69; DMac ranks him in the 30s. Usage was 28% (27th in the league) alongside LaMelo Ball, Kon Knueppel and Miles Bridges and should clear 30% with Knueppel and Coby White hurt. A more complete fantasy player than Jalen Brunson because he adds steals. League Winner Sports: D-Mac ranks him 32 against consensus and Fantrax ADP of 43, so he may be available a round later. Number one option, more so with Kon Knueppel hurt. Matt is 'all in' at 32. James prefers 38-39 because of a lingering shoulder injury the Hornets have been opaque about, and D-Mac flags that FG% could get worse with usage. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by FSAN.

sleepers.name: Cameron Johnson
sleepers.why: 3 creators (RotoWire, Locked On, Number Two Sports). RotoWire: Alex does not love the pick, but he will hit threes efficiently. Expect about 55 games; fits some team builds. Locked On: Went 123; Lloyd is 'excited for a bit of a bounce back'. Number Two Sports: ADP around 114 to 120. Three-point attempts fell from 7.2 with Brooklyn to 4.7 in Denver last year but should rise with Tim Hardaway Jr. gone, and he closed the playoffs strongly (27 points in the elimination game). Contract year. Chris sees him cracking the top 100 and approaching top 75;

sleepers.name: Isaiah Hartenstein
sleepers.why: 3 creators (Locked On, League Winner Sports, RotoWire). Locked On: Round-9 must-draft for Yahoo categories at rank 104. Injured a lot last season but was top 40 early when Holmgren was out. A very low scorer who does not fit every team; Ousmane Dieng's preseason does not threaten his role. League Winner Sports: 85th on League Winner's consensus 9-cat board; ESPN ADP about 134, Yahoo about 105. Projected 10.3 rebounds and 3.6 assists over 67 games on 61% FG. Costs you FT% (64%) and threes. RotoWire: Around pick 100. Easy plug-and-play second center when you only drafted one; you know what you get. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On, Old Man Squad.

sleepers.name: Jakob Poeltl
sleepers.why: 3 creators (Locked On, Old Man Squad, RotoWire). Locked On: Best projection left on the board around pick 108; looks significantly better than last season and the back looks OK for now. Old Man Squad: Yahoo rank 117, four airplanes, favorite player in the 113 to 126 tier. Looks healthy, is the starting center, and Besbris expects 26 to 27 minutes, enough for top 60; he has been top 40 at 30 minutes. RotoWire: People are down on him, but Alex still views him as a relatively high-floor center in the round 8 to 11 range if healthy. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by RotoWire.

sleepers.name: Kevin Durant
sleepers.why: 3 creators (Locked On, Old Man Squad, Adam King). Locked On: ESPN rank 28 after finishing about 10th in category leagues last season. Lloyd does not believe Ime Udoka will actually cut his minutes dramatically. Old Man Squad: Yahoo 14. Was a first-rounder in 8-cat last year, played 78 of 82, 52/87 shooting splits, 1.7 steals plus blocks. Pairs with almost any first-rounder. Adam King: First-round upside but falling outside the first round to 16 or 17. Surprisingly durable the last few years.

sleepers.name: Andrew Wiggins
sleepers.why: 3 creators (Old Man Squad, Hustle Sports, Locked On). Old Man Squad: Yahoo rank 91, three airplanes (a safe round of value). Projected to finish around 75 with threes plus defensive stats, slightly more scoring and assists than Jaden McDaniels. Hustle Sports: One of three Heat players (with Giannis and Bam Adebayo) T-Will wants a share of after the Giannis trade, though he would not overspend on Wiggins. Locked On: Qualifies as a late pick on some sites. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

sleepers.name: Anthony Black
sleepers.why: 3 creators (RotoWire, FSAN, Number Two Sports). RotoWire: Talent bet: Orlando's rotation is not deep enough to keep him off the court. Pick 100 would be a reach but he keeps slipping in home leagues. Jalen Suggs' annual missed time bakes in a month or two of extra minutes. FSAN: ADP around 79 after going undrafted last year; Joiner would take him around round 7. Averaged about 8 points, 3 rebounds and a couple of assists in 21 minutes over the last 10 games, with frequent three and five-steal games; ten more minutes lifts every category. Number Two Sports: The hedge for managers who fade Suggs. Broke out in his third season with 15 points, 3.7 assists, 3.8 rebounds, 1.4 steals and 0.7 blocks in 29 minutes. Projects as sixth man leading the second unit, on a $10 million player option; upside if he reaches 30 minutes or starts when Suggs is out. Perimeter shooting needs to improve. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

sleepers.name: Daniel Gafford
sleepers.why: 3 creators (Old Man Squad, Locked On, RotoWire). Old Man Squad: One airplane. Probably a top 100 player to start the year if Dereck Lively II is out; a short-term 'burger board' candidate. Locked On: 'Last man standing': Lively, Santi Aldama and rookie Morez Johnson Jr. are all not healthy, so he may start opening night at about 25 minutes. Not the finisher or shot blocker he was, and his ankle is a constant issue; possibly top 100 for a month or two. RotoWire: ADP in the 200s on Fantrax, about 150 on some sites, closer to 100 on Yahoo. In 22 games last year with 25-plus minutes he averaged 12 points, 9 rebounds, 2.5 stocks on 67% FG. With Dereck Lively's status unknown the competition is Moussa Cisse, Santi Aldama and rookie Morez Johnson Jr.

sleepers.name: Derik Queen
sleepers.why: 3 creators (RotoWire, SportsEthos, Locked On). RotoWire: Going around the eighth round after finishing just outside the top 100 as a rookie. Had a 22-game stretch last year where he was top 50 punting turnovers in 28 minutes a game; needs consistent minutes more than extra minutes. Pelicans have a logjam but should be committed to him. SportsEthos: Watch-list or stash: better current fantasy skill set than Jeremiah Fears. At 25 minutes he is stashable, at 30 he gets exciting, but the Pelicans depth chart (Zion Williamson, Yves Missi, Saddiq Bey's extension) makes the minutes impossible to project. Locked On: Yahoo rank 92, Fantrax ADP 92, ESPN 96. Lloyd says Queen and Zion cannot play together but expects New Orleans to try, and Queen to play more minutes; he was already around this value last season so there is little downside. (By Oct 2-11 Lloyd had cooled on him.) Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Noah Rubin, RotoWire, Locked On, Old Man Squad.

sleepers.name: Domantas Sabonis
sleepers.why: 3 creators (Locked On, Noah Rubin, SportsEthos). Locked On: Yahoo rank 34. He was bad last season and played under 30 minutes, but minutes should rise and DeMar DeRozan, Russell Westbrook and Dennis Schroder are gone, so more touches. Third round is about right in categories with top-20 upside; trade risk exists but 'who's taking that contract?' Noah Rubin: Was ranked 22 on Yahoo before being bumped back down. Rubin thinks top 25 is fair: healthy after a 19-game season with a knee injury, the Kings are trying to win, he played 34 to 35 minutes when healthy, and the offense can run through him at the high post with dribble handoffs to rookie Darius Acuff Jr. SportsEthos: Bruski's contrarian buy at an ADP of about 34-35: comes in in great shape, knee issues probably fine, and Sacramento should run the offence through him early to rebuild trade value, so the first half should be good. The second half is uncertain (trade, Kings chaos). Dr. A is out, see busts. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Old Man Squad, NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports, Adam King, SportsEthos.

sleepers.name: Jaylen Brown
sleepers.why: 3 creators (Fantasy on Points, Locked On, Hustle Sports). Fantasy on Points: Leo took him in the fourth. Usage takes a hit on the 76ers but he expects better efficiency, making him more useful in 9-cat than in points; many drafters are avoiding him entirely, so there is value in rounds four to five. Leo describes it as a floor pick, not an upside pick. Locked On: ESPN rank 62. Lloyd is 'very happy' to take him in the 40s and says straight nine-cat rankings that put him in the hundreds are misused. Hustle Sports: T-Will likes the LeBron-to-Philadelphia move most for Brown and Tyrese Maxey: if LeBron facilitates they get easy looks and defences cannot double anyone. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Old Man Squad.

sleepers.name: Kyrie Irving
sleepers.why: 3 creators (Old Man Squad, RotoWire, Locked On). Old Man Squad: Besbris calls him a bona fide first-rounder with injury history who is going in the mid-to-late fourth round; one of only two players he takes ahead of Dejounte Murray in the 45 to 65 range. RotoWire: Alex is high on him in the fourth to early fifth round and could justify the late third if you are playing for upside; hard to find more upside in that range. Locked On: Fantrax ADP 52, ESPN ADP 98. Lloyd projects him top 20 per game, would consider him inside the top 40, and calls 52 'really, really easy'.

sleepers.name: Sandro Mamukelashvili
sleepers.why: 3 creators (Locked On, Noah Rubin, RotoWire). Locked On: Went about 136 here after going in round 9 in Lloyd's previous mock; called a good pick. Noah Rubin: Yahoo ADP 119.1 (10th round); Rubin is happy to take him there or a little earlier. Fantasy-friendly all-around game (passes, rebounds, defensive stats, shoots) and a chance to start at power forward for the Lakers next to Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves. RotoWire: Grades above average in every rate stat on RotoWire's advanced page. Scaling last year's 22 minutes up to 28 would make him roughly an 80th to 88th-ranked player, great value for a last or second-to-last pick.

sleepers.name: Ausar Thompson
sleepers.why: 3 creators (Hustle Sports, Adam King, Locked On). Hustle Sports: Named as a defensive-production type like Dyson Daniels; on the lower end offensively. Adam King: ADP 89.7, which King calls a no-brainer even without punting: defensive stats, out-of-position rebounds, FG% and low turnovers. Only 10 points a game and no threes. Averaged 26 minutes last year; King expects closer to 30 given the money Detroit invested and Tobias Harris leaving. Locked On: Yahoo rank 90, ADP 91; Fantrax 82; ESPN rank 78, ADP 110. At last season's 26 minutes he probably does not beat it; at 28-30 minutes he beats it easily, by a round or more.

sleepers.name: Fred VanVleet
sleepers.why: 3 creators (Locked On, NBA Fantasy Bible, Steve St-Pierre). Locked On: Fell to 122, which never happens; 'the first instance of Fred VanVleet this season for me'. NBA Fantasy Bible, Steve St-Pierre: Steve took him at the third pick of the eleventh round. Looked like he had not lost a beat in the Rockets' preseason game in Macau. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On, Number Two Sports.

sleepers.name: Ivica Zubac
sleepers.why: 3 creators (Noah Rubin, RotoWire, SportsEthos). Noah Rubin: Yahoo rank 57 (up from 68). Now the Pacers' center catching passes from Tyrese Haliburton, on a motivated team. Rubin sees more upside than a typical safe center: effective shot blocker and one of the best rebounders in the league. Besbris calls him a very safe play inside the 35 to 65 'Jarrett Allen corridor'. RotoWire: Pick 60 to 70. Underrated for how reliable he is and how good he could be in the Pacers' system; both hosts see value though the ADP is high for a sleeper label. SportsEthos: ADP 64 after a per-game rank of 104 in a small sample. Dr. A is okay with the ADP but wants him a little later than 60: he produces when he gets minutes and will get them as Indiana's centre, but it will be hard to exceed the price. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by SportsEthos.

sleepers.name: Jaime Jaquez Jr.
sleepers.why: 3 creators (Fantasy on Points, Locked On, RotoWire). Fantasy on Points: Leo's ninth-round safe pick: expects him to start and play 30-plus minutes. Locked On: Probably a starter and has to be drafted, though Lloyd is unconvinced: poor shooting and defensive stats, and Herro and Rollins will have the ball. RotoWire: Going in the 10th to 11th round after ranking 147th in 8-cat last year, which undersells roughly 15 points, 5 rebounds, 5 assists in just under 30 minutes for Miami.

sleepers.name: Jalen Duren
sleepers.why: 3 creators (Locked On, NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports). Locked On: Called 'falling way too far' at pick 49. Has not played in preseason yet. NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports: D-Mac has him 41 against consensus 34 because of unresolved contract talks and Paul Reed's strong playoffs. James buys him at 35-36 expecting the contract dispute to motivate him; Matt would be 'licking my lips' at 41, noting people forget his All-NBA-level regular season. Blocks are not great for a centre. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by RotoWire.

sleepers.name: LaMelo Ball
sleepers.why: 3 creators (Locked On, NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports). Locked On: Round-2 must-draft at Yahoo rank 23. Looks good in preseason, the fit next to Anthony Edwards no longer worries Lloyd, about half the time he missed was tanking-related rather than ankles, and he should play more minutes than last season. NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports: Ranked 23 and called almost a no-brainer: relatively healthy last season and now alongside Anthony Edwards. 'As long as he stays healthy, he smashes this value'; James thinks he could return a round of profit. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Old Man Squad, SportsEthos.

sleepers.name: Michael Porter Jr.
sleepers.why: 3 creators (Hustle Sports, Old Man Squad, Locked On). Hustle Sports: Threes plus scoring and close to 10 rebounds, a rare combination. Old Man Squad: Probably in the 40s for Dan; fine around 50. Locked On: Yahoo ADP 68. Usage comes down from a top-30 season, tanking incentives are lower this year, and his worst case if traded is about 75th.

sleepers.name: Quentin Grimes
sleepers.why: 3 creators (RotoWire, Locked On, Number Two Sports). RotoWire: Deep sleeper (pick 140-150 or later) whose ADP is lagging. Looks locked in to start for the Lakers with JJ Redick praising him; could see 33 to 34-plus minutes on many nights, giving threes, defensive stats and efficient scoring as the third to fifth option. Locked On: Feels certain to start at about 30 minutes; if Reaves or Doncic is hurt he becomes the number two with a usage and assist bump, possibly top 80. Number Two Sports: Deep-league last or second-to-last pick. 6'4 guard whose shooting and point-of-attack defense fit JJ Redick's lineups around Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler.

sleepers.name: Tre Jones
sleepers.why: 3 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, The Roster Report, Old Man Squad). NBA Fantasy Bible: Went at the eighth pick of the thirteenth round; D-Mac likes him in Chicago even off the bench. The Roster Report: Keller's favorite late pick for the 'beast mode' build: elite assist-to-turnover ratio, about 55% FG last year, good assists, about four rebounds. Old Man Squad: Two airplanes, preferred over Lendeborg among the deep two-airplane guys. The Bulls are thin at guard and his profile of FG%, assists and steals is a 'sweet combo'. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

sleepers.name: Tyrese Haliburton
sleepers.why: 3 creators (Old Man Squad, Adam King, Locked On). Old Man Squad: Moved up to Yahoo 10 from 12; Dan likes him there. Last full season: 18.5 points, 9.2 assists, 1.4 steals, 3 threes on 47/85 with 1.6 turnovers. A board-flipper for punt points. Adam King: King is fine taking him anywhere from about pick 8 and took him 12th in a draft, while many managers avoid him in round one. He has had a full 12 months off, the Pacers were woeful without him and need him to chase a top four to six seed, and they lack scoring beyond him and Pascal Siakam. Locked On: ESPN ADP 83 after missing last season. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On, RotoWire, NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports.

sleepers.name: VJ Edgecombe
sleepers.why: 3 creators (Adam King, RotoWire, Locked On). Adam King: Growing on King. Ranked 60th last year; best case now is about top 50 because of the pieces Philadelphia added, where he is the fourth or fifth option at full health. RotoWire: King is relatively high on him because the Sixers will ease Tyrese Maxey's load, manage LeBron, and Jaylen Brown has a history of soft-tissue and knee niggles, so Edgecombe plays the most games and minutes and steps up when others sit. Locked On: ESPN ADP 112. Lloyd is down on him this season, but he was top 70 last season and will not drop that far. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Hustle Sports, Old Man Squad, Locked On.

sleepers.name: Franz Wagner
sleepers.why: 3 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports, SportsEthos). NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports: Ranked 49 for a bounce-back season; Matt and James agree he is justifiable there if healthy. SportsEthos: ADP 55 after an 8-cat rank of 83 when on the floor. Bruski calls him almost a safe pick at 55, expecting Orlando to keep him healthy after last year's serious ankle injury. Dr. A disagrees and is out on Orlando entirely. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Old Man Squad.

sleepers.name: Jalen Johnson
sleepers.why: 3 creators (Adam King, RotoWire, Locked On). Adam King, RotoWire: Fell to pick 16 in this expert 9-cat draft when he is normally in the conversation at 6 or 7. Both speakers doubt he reaches the middle of round 2 in most leagues; at worst he is available at the 12/13 turn. Locked On: ESPN ADP 36 for a player going 7th-8th elsewhere who finished 7th per game in ESPN fantasy points last season. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On, Adam King, Old Man Squad.

sleepers.name: Jeremiah Fears
sleepers.why: 3 creators (Locked On, Adam King, RotoWire). Locked On: Outside the top 115 everywhere. At least a 50/50 chance he starts: a plugged-in Pelicans reporter says Joe Dumars wants him starting over Herb Jones.
