sleepers.name: Jake LaRavia
sleepers.why: 1 creator (Locked On). Locked On: If he starts: rebounds, assists, steals and blocks with iffy shooting.

sleepers.name: Jared McCain
sleepers.why: 1 creator (Number Two Sports). Number Two Sports: Yahoo rank 248 against an ADP around 110. Traded to the Thunder at last season's deadline and played better there: 10.4 points, 2.1 rebounds, 0.9 assists on 41% FG and 37% from three in 18.4 playoff minutes, with two starts in the Western Conference Finals. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

sleepers.name: Jayson Tatum
sleepers.why: 1 creator (Adam King). Adam King: King has him about 8th; at pick 10 he calls it a no-brainer. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Old Man Squad.

sleepers.name: Jerami Grant
sleepers.why: 1 creator (Locked On). Locked On: If he beats Jaylen Wells for a starting spot he is the better fantasy contributor, mostly for points; Lloyd is lukewarm.

sleepers.name: Joan Beringer
sleepers.why: 1 creator (Adam King). Adam King: Late-round flag plant at pick 120 to 130, taken with a last or second-to-last pick. King expects a pretty big role now that Naz Reid is gone and sees a young Rudy Gobert type: rim runner and good defender. At 20 minutes he projects 10 points, 7 rebounds and 1.5 blocks. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by SportsEthos.

sleepers.name: Joel Embiid
sleepers.why: 1 creator (Locked On). Locked On: ESPN rank 88. Lloyd will not draft him top 50 but says he should beat 88 comfortably, somewhere in the 60s: 'absolute thievery'. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On, RotoWire.

sleepers.name: Jrue Holiday
sleepers.why: 1 creator (Locked On). Locked On: Went undrafted; Lloyd 'would have been very OK with him' in the last round but needed a big.

sleepers.name: Karl-Anthony Towns
sleepers.why: 1 creator (Noah Rubin). Noah Rubin: ADP about 15 to 16; Rubin is comfortable taking him late first round. Rebounds are back up in New York, minutes dipped to 31 last year under Mike Brown for health preservation and could rise to about 33 with Mitchell Robinson gone and Andre Drummond the backup, and the Knicks leaned on him as a playmaker in the playoffs so... Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Old Man Squad, SportsEthos.

sleepers.name: Kasparas Jakucionis
sleepers.why: 1 creator (SportsEthos). SportsEthos: Now a Buck. Mark had him fifth in his dynasty rookie ranks and thinks he could push others out of the rotation with three-point shooting and passing, but will not project Milwaukee's depth chart. Dr. A does not like his path behind the other Bucks guards.

sleepers.name: Kawhi Leonard
sleepers.why: 1 creator (Locked On). Locked On: ESPN ADP 51. Lloyd will not take him inside the top 40, so 51 becomes value. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On, RotoWire, NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports, Adam King.

sleepers.name: Keaton Wagler
sleepers.why: 1 creator (Locked On). Locked On: Late-round pick around 153: 'that is upside. It probably doesn't work, but it is upside.' Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

sleepers.name: Kelly Oubre Jr.
sleepers.why: 1 creator (Locked On). Locked On: Needs an injury or odd rotation to matter.

sleepers.name: Klay Thompson
sleepers.why: 1 creator (Hustle Sports). Hustle Sports: Streaming candidate only: if he knocks down good looks consistently next to Giannis' playmaking, he is useful some weeks.

sleepers.name: Kon Knueppel
sleepers.why: 1 creator (Locked On). Locked On: ESPN rank 91. Lloyd is out at his Yahoo rank around 35 but takes him at 91. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by NBA Fantasy Bible, Old Man Squad, SportsEthos, Locked On.

sleepers.name: Kyle Filipowski
sleepers.why: 1 creator (RotoWire). RotoWire: On the list now that Jusuf Nurkic will miss time to begin the year.

sleepers.name: Matisse Thybulle
sleepers.why: 1 creator (Locked On). Locked On: Outside shot to start next to Doncic in the Dorian Finney-Smith role. At 28 minutes Lloyd floats three steals a game (steal rate above Dyson Daniels), a block, three threes on about nine points. Knees and ankles may cap him at 21 minutes, where he is a steals streamer.

sleepers.name: Max Christie
sleepers.why: 1 creator (RotoWire). RotoWire: Penciled in as the starting two-guard in Dallas.

sleepers.name: Mikal Bridges
sleepers.why: 1 creator (Hustle Sports). Hustle Sports: Balanced production plus availability: an iron man who does not miss games, which T-Will values highly in today's league. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by NBA Fantasy Bible, Locked On, RotoWire.

sleepers.name: Mikel Brown Jr.
sleepers.why: 1 creator (Locked On). Locked On: Presumed starting point guard next to Egor Demin, though Lloyd is not certain. Good steals and assists upside. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

sleepers.name: Miles Bridges
sleepers.why: 1 creator (Locked On). Locked On: Fell to about 141; Lloyd only objects to him around pick 90, and says he has to be taken at 140. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On, Old Man Squad.

sleepers.name: Mitchell Robinson
sleepers.why: 1 creator (Hustle Sports). Hustle Sports: FG% and rebounding big in the Gobert/Duren mould, a tier below them.

sleepers.name: Nikola Vucevic
sleepers.why: 1 creator (Locked On). Locked On: Round 13 flyer at 156. 'Could be completely washed', but if he plays 23-24 minutes he probably beats that price.

sleepers.name: Noah Penda
sleepers.why: 1 creator (SportsEthos). SportsEthos: Mark's deep-league pet: defensive playmaking, willing three-point shooter, quick decisions; he thinks Penda is better than Jonathan Isaac and could out-impact Tristan da Silva. Dr. A does not see a path to minutes unless Franz Wagner and Paolo Banchero miss time.

sleepers.name: Norman Powell
sleepers.why: 1 creator (Old Man Squad). Old Man Squad: Seventh-round alternative to Paul George if you already hold Kyrie. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

sleepers.name: Payton Pritchard
sleepers.why: 1 creator (Hustle Sports). Hustle Sports: One of the main beneficiaries of Jaylen Brown leaving Boston; shooter and playmaker who has improved each year. T-Will calls for a career year. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by NBA Fantasy Bible.

sleepers.name: Precious Achiuwa
sleepers.why: 1 creator (RotoWire). RotoWire: Usually has about a month of relevance; was easily top 100 over the last couple of months last year in Sacramento. A deep-league 'sicko' option. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

sleepers.name: RJ Barrett
sleepers.why: 1 creator (Locked On). Locked On: Will start and play 30-plus minutes; usage dips with Kawhi there but Toronto will manage Kawhi a lot.

sleepers.name: Robert Williams III
sleepers.why: 1 creator (Locked On). Locked On: Block specialist.

sleepers.name: Royce O'Neale
sleepers.why: 1 creator (RotoWire). RotoWire: Quietly top 20 in made threes last year and over a steal per game. Hornets have a lot of three-point shooting and minutes to replace. Boring but built for 9-cat: never turns it over, threes plus stocks.

sleepers.name: Saddiq Bey
sleepers.why: 1 creator (SportsEthos). SportsEthos: Has become a viable fantasy player over the last couple of years; new three-year, $55.5M extension. Mark sees him as at worst a sixth man or first forward off the bench. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

sleepers.name: Scoot Henderson
sleepers.why: 1 creator (Locked On). Locked On: Could reach 28 minutes if Lillard and Morant are in and out of the lineup.

sleepers.name: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
sleepers.why: 1 creator (Old Man Squad). Old Man Squad: At Yahoo 4 Dan calls him a deal for roto and very effective in H2H if you punt threes.

sleepers.name: Tari Eason
sleepers.why: 1 creator (Locked On). Locked On: 'A stashy sort of guy.'

sleepers.name: Walker Kessler
sleepers.why: 1 creator (Hustle Sports). Hustle Sports: Plays with an elite playmaker in Luka Doncic plus Austin Reaves and does not need post touches: lobs and quick finishes. The only worry is his injury history; if healthy, 'you better get him'. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

sleepers.name: Yanic Konan Niederhauser
sleepers.why: 1 creator (Locked On). Locked On: IL-stash idea: could have a top-70 run down the stretch after returning from his foot injury; Lloyd thinks the Clippers want to start him at 25 minutes.

busts.name: Jalen Brunson
busts.why: 7 creators (Locked On, NBA Fantasy Bible, Steve St-Pierre, RotoWire, Old Man Squad, League Winner Sports, SportsEthos). Locked On: Pick 29 in a category league is 'incredibly early'; 'too high for me'. NBA Fantasy Bible, Steve St-Pierre: Pick 24 is far too high for a 9-cat league; Steve agrees there are other guards he would take first in 9-cat. RotoWire: Has ranked between 29th and 53rd in 8-cat in four Knicks seasons with nothing set to change, and the Knicks may not push him to 35 minutes coming off a championship. Old Man Squad: Underperformer rather than outright bust. Pre-ranked in the late 20s (mid third round) but has 'Brunsonitis': steals, blocks and rebounds are exceptionally low and FG% is only middle of the pack, which people ignore because the points, assists, FT% and threes are good. League Winner Sports: James is not a buyer: great in points leagues, not as good in categories, coming off a long season with some lingering injury concern; he would take him around 44-45. D-Mac is higher at 39 because efficient high-volume scoring is hard to find later. SportsEthos: ADP 26 after ranking 47th per game in 8-cat. Dr. A does not think he gets better than 47 and calls the ADP way too high, driven by name recognition and the Knicks.

busts.name: Bam Adebayo
busts.why: 6 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, Steve St-Pierre, Locked On, Old Man Squad, Noah Rubin, SportsEthos). NBA Fantasy Bible, Steve St-Pierre: Went at 2.7, the highest any of them had seen, to a manager pairing him with Giannis. Called too early. Locked On: ESPN category rank 7 after finishing 41st last season, and he now plays with Giannis. Old Man Squad: Biggest riser near the top, 32 to 26, which is too early. 20 points, 10 rebounds, 1.2 steals, 1.7 threes on bad percentages; FG% was a big negative. Only rebounds make him a center in fantasy. Take him only on a guard-build team. Noah Rubin: Rubin says Bam 'isn't what we think Bam is': he lets you down in a different category each year, with assists and defensive stats fluctuating and the added threes last year dragging FG% down. Besbris calls his defensive stats last year a 'garbage fire'. SportsEthos: ADP 32-33 after ranking 54th. Dr. A is nervous that Giannis takes half his rebounds and some blocks and wants to see the fit first. Bruski expects the rebounding to suffer and thinks he finishes below ADP, though not by a lot. Disagreement: also named as a breakout by Hustle Sports.

busts.name: Stephon Castle
busts.why: 6 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, Noah Rubin, RotoWire, Locked On, Old Man Squad, FSAN). NBA Fantasy Bible: Sixth round is still too high in 9-cat; fine in points leagues. Noah Rubin: Mid-fifth-round Yahoo ADP 'blows my mind' in 9-cat. You get strong assists, decent guard rebounds, a steal and a three, but take a big hit in percentages (47% FG up from 42.8%, poor FT% on decent volume) and turnovers. RotoWire: Alex is more comfortable in points leagues; in 9-cat you have to build around him (some punt builds work) and he is a poor fit for balanced or roto teams. Agrees his ADP is less safe than people think. Locked On: Taking Castle over Dylan Harper in a nine-category league is 'probably a bad pick', especially at about pick 63. Old Man Squad: Going around 76 (seventh round) but finished 170th last year because of terrible turnovers, poor FT% and poor threes. Only reaches top 60 in a triple punt (threes, FT%, turnovers) on a Giannis-style big-man build that wants assists and steals from a guard. Otherwise a bust. FSAN: Joiner left him off his own list because the guard rotation is unclear: both De'Aaron Fox and Dylan Harper said at media day that they will start. (Clark has Castle as a breakout.) Disagreement: also named as a sleeper or value by Locked On, SportsEthos.

busts.name: Domantas Sabonis
busts.why: 5 creators (Old Man Squad, NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports, Adam King, SportsEthos). Old Man Squad: Besbris's counter to Rubin: 22 on Yahoo was too early. He does not expect a return to the De'Aaron Fox era when Sabonis had the ball at the high post every possession and was top 20 in 9-cat; expects something closer to the 40ish range, with a bump in 8-cat. Not worried about injury. NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports: Ranked 40 by D-Mac (consensus 38). No threes, turnovers, and few defensive stats for a big. James fades him to 45-46, expecting the Kings to lean into youth (Maxime Raynaud, Darius Acuff, Dylan Cardwell). D-Mac thinks a trade would be the best thing for his value. Adam King: ADP in the high 30s or low 40s. Taking him at 23 is a reach and a gamble given the uncertainty in Sacramento. SportsEthos: Dr. A is out even at ADP 34: a big who does not block shots, does not hit threes and has poor steals, three things he generally refuses to draft without. Bruski disagrees, see sleepers. Disagreement: also named as a sleeper or value by Locked On, Noah Rubin, SportsEthos.

busts.name: Kawhi Leonard
busts.why: 5 creators (Locked On, RotoWire, NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports, Adam King). Locked On: Went in round 3. 'Kawhi in a head-to-head league is after pick 40.' Lloyd will not touch him, Curry or Embiid in the round-2 area. RotoWire: ADP is early-to-mid third round and he goes in the second in expert drafts, too early for a player whose best case is about 60 games. Toronto has more talent and can manage him; he averaged under 24 points in the four seasons before last year's 28, so scoring regression is expected. NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports: D-Mac ranks him 31 against a consensus of 18 and has seen him go in the second round: 'I just don't trust his body' in head-to-head, fine in roto. He expects not to roster him anywhere. Matt is in the middle (early 20s). Adam King: Went 19th. Alex does not like drafting him there in general; King left him out of his punt-pairings show because a second-round pick on him is too risky for games played. Disagreement: also named as a sleeper or value by Locked On.

busts.name: Giannis Antetokounmpo
busts.why: 5 creators (Old Man Squad, NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports, Adam King, SportsEthos). Old Man Squad: Now Yahoo 6. Should not be drafted in the first round unless you punt FT%: about 30 attempts a week and 19 to 23 makes. NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports: Ranked 7 but D-Mac generally dislikes drafting him because he forces a punt from pick one; Matt prefers a balanced build and would take others in that range. Stronger in points leagues, where D-Mac sees top-four value. Adam King: King rarely drafts him: easy to build a punt around, but his defensive stats have fallen to about 1.5 to 2 combined steals and blocks, so King prefers Scottie Barnes (about 2.5) for the same style of build. SportsEthos: Sixth-highest ADP after an 8-cat per-game rank of 40 last season (free throws plus injuries). Bruski will never rank him high because he hurts you in multiple categories, will not chase him, and doubts the Giannis-Bam frontcourt works in many matchups; taking him sixth in roto is 'handing over your money'. Dr. Disagreement: also named as a sleeper or value by Locked On, Old Man Squad.

busts.name: Kon Knueppel
busts.why: 4 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, Old Man Squad, SportsEthos, Locked On). NBA Fantasy Bible: D-Mac is high on him for the full season but says to drop him in your draft order because of a hamstring injury that will likely cost him the start of the season; Charlotte will not push him if they start slowly. Old Man Squad: Pre-ranked 37th earlier, now 64th. Finished 66th last year on one of the best FG efficiency seasons ever for a rookie, but has 'Brunsonitis' in defensive stats and had 2 turnovers against only 3.5 assists. SportsEthos: Lost his point guard (LaMelo Ball). Mark expects only marginal improvement, not a leap, because he now has more primary creation duties and Charlotte lacks an initiator; warns against overdrafting him at an inflated price. Locked On: Lloyd is 'out' at his Yahoo rank of roughly 35. Disagreement: also named as a sleeper or value by Locked On.

busts.name: Alperen Sengun
busts.why: 4 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports, Old Man Squad, SportsEthos). NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports: D-Mac ranks him 30 on volume despite finishing 59th in 9-cat last season (29th the year before). James fades him to about 35: poor FT% and he needs more stocks; fine only if your build fits him. Old Man Squad: Yahoo 25; a punt player, not a straight value. SportsEthos: 16th-highest ADP after ranking 34th in 8-cat. Dr. A is done as his apologist: the lack of defensive stats is too much and he should go around 30th. Disagreement: also named as a sleeper or value by Old Man Squad.

busts.name: Derik Queen
busts.why: 4 creators (Noah Rubin, RotoWire, Locked On, Old Man Squad). Noah Rubin: Early-to-mid eighth-round Yahoo ADP. Rubin says he should not go inside the top 100 because Yves Missi looks like the starting center and the fit next to Zion Williamson is bad (lineups were worse with both on the floor). He played 22.8 minutes over the final two months last year after losing his starting job. RotoWire: Disagreement: Alex would take him around pick 90 and expects at least last year's 25 minutes, chasing the upside of 28 minutes plus improvement. He concedes Queen ranked 110th in 8-cat, had a terrible net rating, had five turnovers in about 18 preseason minutes and looks out of shape. Locked On: Went 105; Lloyd has 'no confidence in how they're going to play him and what his minutes are going to look like'. Old Man Squad: Yahoo rank 100. Will be okay but Besbris is not interested and skips him. Disagreement: also named as a sleeper or value by RotoWire, SportsEthos, Locked On.

busts.name: Tyrese Haliburton
busts.why: 4 creators (Locked On, RotoWire, NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports). Locked On: 'I don't love Haliburton' at the back of round 1; he fell to about pick 20 here. RotoWire: Usually drafted around the first/second-round turn but more likely a mid-to-late second-round value this year coming off the Achilles. Minutes could sit in the high 20s to low 30s early, with back-to-backs off and efficiency, rebounds, steals and blocks slow to return. NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports: D-Mac ranks him 17 against a consensus of 10. He has not played in over a year after the Achilles injury and has not been seen in game action; D-Mac expects a slow ramp-up with rest days (Indiana has 15 back-to-backs), which hurts in head-to-head where a fast start matters. Disagreement: also named as a sleeper or value by Old Man Squad, Adam King, Locked On.

busts.name: Alex Sarr
busts.why: 4 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, Locked On, FSAN, RotoWire). NBA Fantasy Bible: Too high in the sixth round for D-Mac, who also notes Sarr has never been known for staying on the court. Locked On: Yahoo rank 56. Anthony Davis's arrival means fewer rebounds, fewer rim contests and lower usage; Lloyd says Davis would have to play under 40 games for 56 to work. Sarr also comes in off a broken foot and surgery. FSAN: Honorable-mention breakout that Joiner would not pay for: if Anthony Davis plays more than half the games, Sarr's value is bad (blocks and steals only, rebounds down). He only feasts with Trae Young in pick-and-roll if Davis misses extended time. RotoWire: Typically a sixth-round pick. Rebounds and blocks rose last year when he mostly played center, but he now plays next to Anthony Davis, is the fifth option on offense and has only averaged 27 minutes for his career. Low-floor scenarios exist. Disagreement: also named as a sleeper or value by Hustle Sports.

busts.name: Paolo Banchero
busts.why: 4 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, RotoWire, Old Man Squad, SportsEthos). NBA Fantasy Bible: Went at the end of the fifth round; D-Mac says 'I'm not touching him in 9-cat'. RotoWire: Partial disagreement: Alex has taken him in the fourth round in 9-cat and thinks a third or fourth-round pick is fine in a committed multi-punt (blocks, steals, threes), but agrees he is a poor fit for balanced or roto builds. Old Man Squad: Going 52nd. Finished 129th in 9-cat last year (70s in 8-cat). Weak defensive stats (1.3 combined steals plus blocks), does not hit threes, and Besbris does not trust last year's FT% uptick to hold. Moved from bust to underperformer because one punt (punt FT% or punt FG%) can get him near his price; SportsEthos: ADP 41. Dr. A is completely out: no steals, no blocks, no threes, mediocre percentages and ordinary rebounding, and he expects him to be overdrafted every year. Disagreement: also named as a sleeper or value by Locked On.

busts.name: Tyrese Maxey
busts.why: 4 creators (Locked On, RotoWire, NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports). Locked On: 'Pretty low on Maxey compared to others'; Lloyd would not be surprised by a 15th-to-19th finish. Philadelphia has a lot of players who take the ball out of his hands, usage may drop, he has had injuries, and Lloyd doubts defensive stats carry him. RotoWire: With Jaylen Brown and LeBron James in Philadelphia he faces both less usage and fewer minutes after averaging 38 a game over three seasons. His per-36 numbers over that span rank only 18th in 8-cat. Considered around pick 6, he could return roughly 20th-ranked per-game value. NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports: Dropped to 9 in D-Mac's ranks because volume and usage come down with Joel Embiid, LeBron James and especially Jaylen Brown on the roster; still fine in 9-cat because of efficiency, but D-Mac would not take him in the first round of a points league. James disagrees and has him 6, ahead of Edwards. Disagreement: also named as a breakout by Hustle Sports.

busts.name: Devin Booker
busts.why: 3 creators (Locked On, Old Man Squad, SportsEthos). Locked On: Pick 27 'feels a bit early'. Old Man Squad: Yahoo 23, light red. Last year about 26 points, 4 rebounds, 6 assists, 2 threes, 1.1 steals plus blocks on 45.5% with high turnovers: 65th in 9-cat, 39th in 8-cat. No punt or build makes him a sure bet to return 23. SportsEthos: ADP 28 after ranking 39th. Dr. A expects him near 39 again: 'his name is bigger than his game'. Bruski adds that Jalen Green is in Phoenix and they just lost Mark Williams.

busts.name: Mikal Bridges
busts.why: 3 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, Locked On, RotoWire). NBA Fantasy Bible: Too high at the twelfth pick of the sixth round. Locked On: 'So boring' around pick 100; low likelihood he is significantly better than that price. RotoWire: Same no-upside type as Jabari Smith and Toumani Camara: will not walk into more minutes or usage. Games played is the only real selling point. Disagreement: also named as a sleeper or value by Hustle Sports.

busts.name: Jalen Johnson
busts.why: 3 creators (Locked On, Adam King, Old Man Squad). Locked On: Lloyd 'didn't feel good about' him at the 11-12 turn. Adam King: ADP 11; King has him more like 13 or 14. Taking him 5th or 6th is too high unless you are on a specific build. Defensive stats fell from about 1.6 steals and 1 block to about 1.1 steals as his offensive load grew, and his shooting efficiency slipped. Old Man Squad: Jokic's stat shape but worse everywhere except threes and turnovers, with no obvious punt to catch up. Steals fell to 1.2 and blocks to 0.4. Dan has him 9th. Disagreement: also named as a sleeper or value by Adam King, RotoWire, Locked On.

busts.name: Stephen Curry
busts.why: 3 creators (Locked On, Old Man Squad, RotoWire). Locked On: One of the per-game guys (with Kawhi and Embiid) Lloyd is 'not touching' in the round-2 area. Old Man Squad: Yahoo 25. Dan has fully soured: fears a Warriors gap year with Curry playing about 55 games on autopilot. RotoWire: Costs a second-round pick in category leagues and turns 39 in March after playing 43 games last year. Still elite in threes and FT% with near 27 points, but assists and rebounds have fallen and steals could dip under one. Whalen expects similar health issues this season. Disagreement: also named as a sleeper or value by Adam King, Locked On.

busts.name: Trae Young
busts.why: 3 creators (Locked On, Old Man Squad, SportsEthos). Locked On: Went right after James Harden in round 3: 'I cannot get behind that.' Old Man Squad: In full 9-cat he ranks outside the top 35 or 40. Do not draft him unless you are punting FG% and/or turnovers; never in roto at this price. SportsEthos: ADP about 25 (23rd highest) after a per-game rank of 84. Bruski is out at that price because of a shots problem in Washington with Anthony Davis, Alex Sarr and first overall pick AJ Dybantsa. Dr. A is not fully out but says a second-round pick on him will feel like 'God, I hope this works out'. Disagreement: also named as a sleeper or value by Old Man Squad.

busts.name: Amen Thompson
busts.why: 3 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports, Old Man Squad). NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports: D-Mac ranks him 26 against a consensus of 21 and Adam King's 15: until the outside shot is consistent he is not reaching first-round value, and Fred VanVleet and Marcus Smart add more facilitators. A League Winner host was burned last year and prefers the 24-25 range. Old Man Squad: Yahoo 21. Dan likes him but does not see top 20 with the Houston logjam changing his role. Fine if you treat the pick as a mid-third. Disagreement: also named as a sleeper or value by Adam King, Locked On.

busts.name: Deni Avdija
busts.why: 3 creators (Locked On, NBA Fantasy Bible, RotoWire). Locked On: ESPN category rank 5. He was 35th in Lloyd's head-to-head ranking last season, and Portland now gets Damian Lillard back, adds Ja Morant and has a full season of Scoot Henderson. NBA Fantasy Bible: Yahoo ADP 40.8, Fantrax 35.1. Top-25 usage (about 30%) last year should fall dramatically with Ja Morant, Damian Lillard, Scoot Henderson and Jrue Holiday there. DMac sees him well outside the top 50 in 9-cat (still top 50 in points). RotoWire: Was 33rd per game in 8-cat last year and 75th the year before; Alex expects something in between, around 50th, with a high floor but no path to first-round value. Disagreement: also named as a sleeper or value by Locked On.

busts.name: Ja Morant
busts.why: 3 creators (Locked On, Old Man Squad, RotoWire). Locked On: Lloyd considered him at 98 and decided 'not really'; he went 99. Old Man Squad: Yahoo rank 94, two airplanes and 'impossible to rank'. Will take and miss a lot of shots in Portland and is always hurt. Could be a four-airplane value only if you are punting FG%. RotoWire: Always better in real life than in fantasy, and the Portland situation is muddled. ADP is not punitive but Whalen is still out. Disagreement: also named as a sleeper or value by Locked On, Old Man Squad.

busts.name: Jabari Smith Jr.
busts.why: 3 creators (Locked On, Old Man Squad, RotoWire). Locked On: 'So boring' around pick 99; low likelihood he is significantly better than that price. Old Man Squad: Yahoo rank 96, two airplanes: almost exactly even money, startable but with no value baked in. Besbris would take John Collins over him. RotoWire: Alex never drafts him: almost no upside because his role is cemented, and it could get worse with Fred VanVleet returning. Prefers upside swings in rounds 7 to 9. Disagreement: also named as a sleeper or value by Locked On.

busts.name: LeBron James
busts.why: 3 creators (Steve St-Pierre, Hustle Sports, RotoWire). Steve St-Pierre: Steve is not high on him: expects him to be in and out of the lineup, a year older with declining stats, on a loaded Philadelphia team. Acceptable only as a sixth-round forward fill. Hustle Sports: 'Tread lightly' on whatever price drafts put on him: year 24, turning 42 in December, and Nick Nurse reportedly wants him as more of a point guard facilitator. T-Will personally would not draft him. RotoWire: ADP 35 ESPN, 37 Yahoo, 39 Underdog is higher than Whalen expected. He no longer has to be a first or second option and the Sixers should be aggressive resting him on back-to-backs. Little upside, though he should be a good assists source. Disagreement: also named as a sleeper or value by Adam King, RotoWire, Locked On.

busts.name: VJ Edgecombe
busts.why: 3 creators (Hustle Sports, Old Man Squad, Locked On). Hustle Sports: Expected to take more of a back seat than last season with LeBron James, Jaylen Brown, Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey all in Philadelphia. breakouts.name: Cooper Flagg
breakouts.why: 7 creators (Steve St-Pierre, Fantasy on Points, Locked On, Old Man Squad, FSAN, Adam King, SportsEthos). Steve St-Pierre, Fantasy on Points: Fell to pick 11 here but is climbing to seventh or eighth in real drafts. Steve thinks new coach Dusty May gets even more out of Flagg and Kyrie Irving. Locked On: Rookie of the Year who Lloyd expects to get better this season. Old Man Squad: Very young with 19 to 20 shots a game. Three categories could each tick up: a point or two, half a three, a point or two of FG%. That could push him to the edge of the first round. FSAN: Joiner's number five. ADP about 27 after roughly 40 as a rookie; he thinks Flagg could finish top five because he contributes in every category, with Kyrie Irving back, more shooting and hopefully Dereck Lively. Clark calls 27 'disrespectful' and expects at least top 20. Adam King: Went 7th overall. King expects him to settle in the 7 to 9 range of drafts on hype and notes a report that he has grown to 6-foot-10. SportsEthos: Came on in the last third of last season during his Rookie of the Year push. Dr. A thinks Dallas hands him the car keys and the league wants to make him a face of the league starting this year. Bruski allows he 'might just go nuts'. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports, SportsEthos.

breakouts.name: Collin Murray-Boyles
breakouts.why: 7 creators (RotoWire, The Roster Report, NBA Fantasy Bible, Number Two Sports, Old Man Squad, Locked On, SportsEthos). RotoWire: Second-year players typically improve rebound, free-throw and stock rates; a 10% across-the-board gain at 28 minutes makes him an Ausar Thompson-like line. The Roster Report: Stock is rising and will keep rising into the season as the expanded role becomes visible. NBA Fantasy Bible: Big playoff series and the flexibility to play power forward or centre; still expected to come off the bench. Projected 27.5 minutes (from 21.9) with more rebounds, assists, steals and blocks. High-volume defensive stocks; threes are not his game. Number Two Sports: ADP 115, which Chris calls his floor, with a top 70 ceiling. Over the final three months last year he was about a top 100 player in 23.6 minutes: 10 points, 5.1 rebounds, 1.9 assists, a combined 2 steals and blocks, 63% FG, 68.3% FT. Old Man Squad: Yahoo pre-rank 111, honorable-mention breakout with top 60 potential at 27 to 28 minutes and third-round value if Poeltl misses time. Raptors said he will play the four and the five: about 14 backup power forward minutes behind Scottie Barnes plus about 20 backup center minutes. Locked On: Outside the top 150 as a rookie; Lloyd sets top 100 as the baseline this year. SportsEthos: Mark thinks he is talented enough to 'really explode in year two' if he gets the minutes at centre and forward that the playoffs suggested.

breakouts.name: Matas Buzelis
breakouts.why: 6 creators (Locked On, NBA Fantasy Bible, Fantasy on Points, Hustle Sports, Number Two Sports, League Winner Sports). Locked On: Year three with a minutes bump expected from 29 a game; Lloyd has him top 50. NBA Fantasy Bible, Fantasy on Points: Leo took him in the fifth for upside. D-Mac is very high on him and says the preseason hype means you cannot wait until the sixth. Hustle Sports: Middle-to-late-round multi-category upside: scoring, threes, rebounds and some shot-blocking, compared loosely to a modern Andrei Kirilenko. Young players can be inconsistent and inefficient, so do not pay for the breakout before it happens. Number Two Sports: ADP 65; Chris sees a possible second or third round outcome. Played close to 30 minutes as a sophomore with almost 1.5 blocks and 0.7 steals and averaged 19 points after the All-Star break. Added 12 pounds of muscle and is working on a midrange game. League Winner Sports: Ranked 47 (consensus 47). D-Mac expects another breakout season; Matt has him inside the top 50 in both points and categories, citing blocks and continued improvement. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Noah Rubin, RotoWire, Old Man Squad.

breakouts.name: Dylan Harper
breakouts.why: 6 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, Fantasy on Points, Noah Rubin, RotoWire, Locked On, SportsEthos). NBA Fantasy Bible, Fantasy on Points: Went with the first pick of the seventh round and is rising because he may start in three-guard lineups. Gives points and assists but is not efficient. Noah Rubin, RotoWire: Alex 'loves Dylan Harper this year'; Rubin says he is emerging and is the Spurs' number two long-term priority behind Wembanyama, ahead of Castle and Fox. Locked On: Expected to start and to be San Antonio's second-best player by the end of the season. SportsEthos: Dr. A's view: a Sixth Man of the Year candidate who could reach about 15 points, 5 rebounds, 5 assists, 1.5 steals and 1.5 threes in 28-plus minutes. Mark calls that line the peak, not the expectation. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by SportsEthos.

breakouts.name: Brandon Miller
breakouts.why: 5 creators (Locked On, NBA Fantasy Bible, RotoWire, Number Two Sports, League Winner Sports). Locked On: Lloyd expects 'pretty good numbers this season'; reasonable at pick 30. NBA Fantasy Bible: Fourth-year leap as the number one option with LaMelo Ball gone, and Kon Knueppel and Coby White missing the start of the season. Projected 31.5 minutes, 24 points, 5.1 rebounds, 3.6 assists, 1.1 steals, 0.8 blocks and about 3 threes. Efficiency has hurt him in the past; he has added physicality to finish at the rim. RotoWire: Posted per-minute career highs in points, rebounds, assists, steals and FT% in only 30 minutes last year while dealing with injuries. Career-high usage plus 33 to 34 minutes could lift him into the top 30; Alex has drafted him as early as 29th. Number Two Sports: ADP 46 is still too low: top 30 upside with a top 50 floor, a no-brainer in the fourth round. With LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges gone he becomes the lead option with close to 20 shots a game. Chris's baseline is 20 points, 5 rebounds, 4 assists, over 1.5 steals plus blocks and multiple threes on average-to-below-average FG%. League Winner Sports: D-Mac and Matt both call for a breakout as Charlotte's number one option; D-Mac compares the path to a 'Paul George lite' and floats All-NBA contention. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by FSAN.

breakouts.name: Khaman Maluach
breakouts.why: 5 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, FSAN, Locked On, RotoWire, Number Two Sports). NBA Fantasy Bible: Mark Williams is injured and will miss a lot of time. Oso Ighodaro is starting and is expected to start opening night, but Maluach is projected at 24.9 minutes off the bench with 10 points, 8.5 rebounds and 1.7 blocks. Host expects him to take the starting job later in the season. FSAN: Joiner's number three. Great summer league and G League; the Suns let him bulk up last year (about 3 points and 2 rebounds in 46 games). Gives everything Mark Williams would, maybe more, if he is allowed to shoot. Locked On: Second-year center going from nine minutes a game to a likely starting job. RotoWire: Looked amazing in summer league; at 28 to 29 minutes plus development he could look like Kel'el Ware statistically. Number Two Sports: Chris sees a big second year possible if Phoenix lets him win the starting job; 7'1, 250 pounds with elite defensive potential and a possible outside shot. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

breakouts.name: Ausar Thompson
breakouts.why: 5 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, Number Two Sports, Old Man Squad, Adam King, Locked On). NBA Fantasy Bible: Preseason hype around a developing mid-range shot that would keep him on the floor. Coach has said he will get more minutes; projected from 26 to just under 29 with an increase in every category. Could be the best perimeter defender in the league and can act as secondary playmaker behind Cade Cunningham. Number Two Sports: ADP close to 90; Chris sees a top 50 to 60 profile if minutes pass 30. Elite multi-category defender, but shoots 25% from three on under one attempt, which hurt Detroit in the playoffs and makes 30-plus minutes hard to sustain. Old Man Squad: Yahoo pre-rank 77 (seventh round); Besbris sees a fourth or fifth round finish. Ranked around 211th through the new year last season at 25 minutes with four free throw attempts at 55%, then top 60 in the second half: 2.3 steals and 1.2 blocks over his last 25 games, 56% FG, 4 assists, free throw attempts down to two. Adam King: King has more faith in a minutes jump from 26 toward 30 this year because of Detroit's financial commitment and Tobias Harris's departure, though his lack of spacing next to Jalen Duren is a concern and John Collins has been added. Locked On: Breakout hinges on a minutes jump from 26 to 28-30.

breakouts.name: Kel'el Ware
breakouts.why: 4 creators (Hustle Sports, NBA Fantasy Bible, Old Man Squad, FSAN). Hustle Sports: 'The time is now': projected jump from 11 points to about 17 points and 11 rebounds if he gets 30 to 35 minutes, with added three-point volume. NBA Fantasy Bible: Started at the four alongside Myles Turner in the last preseason game after being expected to back him up. Projected 28 minutes (from 22.1, when he averaged 11.1 points and 9 rebounds), about 11 rebounds and up to 1.4 blocks, plus outside shooting as a stretch four/five. Old Man Squad: Sixth-round pick with fourth-round or better upside. Last year: 22 minutes, 11 points, 9 rebounds, 0.8 steals, 1.1 blocks, 53% FG, 1 three, 75% FT, ranked 59th helped by 0.8 turnovers. Now in Milwaukee, expected to reach 25 minutes as backup center and alongside Myles Turner, which Besbris calls a top 50 floor; FSAN: Clark's number one. Expects him to become Milwaukee's starting center over Myles Turner, if not in week one then eventually, on a mostly rebuilding team with ex-Heat teammates Tyler Herro and Jaime Jaquez and coach Taylor Jenkins. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by League Winner Sports.

breakouts.name: Cedric Coward
breakouts.why: 4 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, Number Two Sports, FSAN, Locked On). NBA Fantasy Bible: Projected 28.9 minutes (from 25.8). High-upside two-way wing who is an efficient shooter, with slight increases in rebounds, assists, steals, blocks and threes. Number Two Sports: Sophomore leap candidate; Chris would 'smash' him in the late 80s or early 90s and sees a top 70 finish. As a rookie: 13.6 points, 5.9 rebounds, 2.8 assists, 0.6 steals on 47% FG in 26 minutes, with seven 20-point games. FSAN: Clark's number two. Second-year wing who scores, defends and passes; more minutes alone should lift scoring and roughly double his defensive stats. Locked On: Second-year starter with minutes and usage rising. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

breakouts.name: Darius Garland
breakouts.why: 3 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, Number Two Sports, Noah Rubin). Number Two Sports: ADP 66 with top 40 upside. Finished outside the top 100 in totals last year after a midseason trade and injuries, but over his final 14 games averaged 20.6 points, 6.6 assists, 1.2 steals and 3.3 threes in 30.4 minutes. Noah Rubin: Rubin expects career highs as the lone creator on the Clippers; the last time he played a full season without Donovan Mitchell he was an All-Star.

breakouts.name: Egor Demin
breakouts.why: 3 creators (Locked On, NBA Fantasy Bible, SportsEthos). Locked On: Taken at 109 as a round-10 flyer. Lloyd goes back and forth on how excited he is; 'a little bit all over the place'. NBA Fantasy Bible: Has the coaching staff's trust and has added strength. Projected 29.8 minutes (from 25.2), 13.3 points, 3.6 rebounds, 4 assists, 1.0 steals, 0.4 blocks and 2.8 threes. Will play off the ball a lot but can be primary playmaker. SportsEthos: A focal point for Brooklyn along with rookie Mikel Brown Jr.; Mark expects complementary passing and possibly more on-ball reps on top of the threes.

breakouts.name: Ajay Mitchell
breakouts.why: 3 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, FSAN, RotoWire). NBA Fantasy Bible: Aaron Wiggins, Lu Dort and Isaiah Joe all left the Thunder, opening minutes. Projected 30 minutes off the bench, 14.7 points, 3.8 rebounds, 4 assists, 1.4 steals, 0.4 blocks, 1.3 threes. Sixth Man and Most Improved candidate; Daigneault called his defence the foundation of his game. FSAN: Clark's number four. More natural scorer and passer than Caruso or Wallace, with more minutes available now that Lu Dort and Isaiah Joe are gone; takes over when Shai rests. RotoWire: Described as lying in the weeds ready to burst out, with a higher potential than Cason Wallace.

breakouts.name: Day'Ron Sharpe
breakouts.why: 3 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, Number Two Sports, RotoWire). NBA Fantasy Bible: Starting centre for Brooklyn now that Nic Claxton is in Chicago; a per-minute beast with a clear path to heavy minutes all season. Host projects about 28 minutes after offseason conditioning work, with elite rebounding and underrated passing. Called a Most Improved Player favourite. Number Two Sports: Bonus eleventh name. Per-minute production (16.3 points, 13.8 rebounds, 1.5 blocks per 30 for his career) meets a starting job with Claxton gone; Chris expects double-digit points plus rebounds and steals and blocks without needing touches next to Michael Porter Jr. and Julius Randle. RotoWire: One of the best per-minute bigs in the NBA: top 20 in total rebound rate, top 10 in offensive rebound rate, 2.9% steal rate (would have ranked fifth in the league) and an assist rate tied for fifth among centers. Could fly up draft boards once preseason minutes are visible.

breakouts.name: Naz Reid
breakouts.why: 3 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, FSAN, SportsEthos). NBA Fantasy Bible: Now the starting power forward in Charlotte with some small-ball five; starter minutes for a proven per-minute producer. Projected up in points, rebounds, assists, steals, blocks and threes, with extra usage early because Kon Knueppel and Coby White will miss the start of the season. FSAN: Joiner's number one. ADP about 52 (round 6), up from about 88. Goes from sixth man (about 13 points, 6 rebounds) to probably Charlotte's number one scorer and best player with better point-guard play than he had in Minnesota. Will not be a 10-rebound, double-double player. SportsEthos: First real chance at a full starter role after years of about 20 minutes in Minnesota; advanced handle, shooting and athleticism for a big. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Noah Rubin, RotoWire, The Roster Report.

breakouts.name: Ty Jerome
breakouts.why: 3 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, Number Two Sports, Old Man Squad). Last year was only 15 games at 22.6 minutes with very high usage; usage should fall but minutes rise. Elite FG%, 3PT and FT% efficiency, healthy preseason, pick-and-roll with Zach Edey and Cameron Boozer. Number Two Sports: ADP north of 114. Chris believes he starts at point guard with Ja Morant gone and could get upwards of 30 minutes. Last year: 19.7 points, 5.7 assists, 2.8 rebounds, 2.8 threes on 14.3 shots at 47.4%, over a steal and only 1.8 turnovers. Top 80 on average across his last 85 games; Old Man Squad: Yahoo pre-rank has fallen from 87 to 114 (10th round); Besbris sees possible fourth-round value. Ranked 38th in 9-cat last year in just 22.5 minutes: 20 points on 14 shots, 6 assists, 1 steal, almost 3 threes, 47% FG, 88% FT. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

breakouts.name: Anthony Edwards
breakouts.why: 2 creators (Adam King, Old Man Squad). Adam King: King thinks this is the year he has been building toward with a different-looking Minnesota squad that lost depth. Old Man Squad: Probably outscores Maxey this year because of personnel changes in both Minnesota and Philadelphia. Dan expects him to play the most games of the Maxey/Tatum/Edwards group. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports.

breakouts.name: Brandin Podziemski
breakouts.why: 2 creators (Number Two Sports, Locked On). Number Two Sports: ADP north of 117; Chris projects top 75. Last year: 13.8 points, 5.1 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 1.1 steals, 2 threes on 45.5% FG, and he has improved every season. Warriors backcourt is thin behind Curry and Melton, Butler is still recovering and Porzingis will miss a large chunk of games, so minutes and usage are secure. Locked On: Top-100 season 'probably coming' as a starter with more minutes. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On, Old Man Squad.

breakouts.name: Dejounte Murray
breakouts.why: 2 creators (Number Two Sports, Old Man Squad). Number Two Sports: ADP 71; Chris expects him to crush it and finish at or near top 50. Returned late last season from a major injury and looked good, and now has his first normal offseason in two years. Over 1.5 steals at his best (led the league in 2022), 20-plus points in three of his last five seasons. Old Man Squad: Projected around top 30 per game; Besbris takes him with any pick from 45 to 65 (fifth round). Almost two years removed from the injury he suffered 30 games into 2024-25, played 14 games at 28 minutes late last season and looked good, and should return to about 33 minutes as the Pelicans' point guard.

breakouts.name: Austin Reaves
breakouts.why: 2 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, Locked On). NBA Fantasy Bible: Steps into a larger offensive role with LeBron James no longer on the Lakers; looked like the alpha last season in games Luka and LeBron sat. Only played 51 games last season, so health is the condition. Host projects All-Star, possibly All-NBA level. Locked On: Usage clearly going up with LeBron gone; could be the 12th or 13th best player.

breakouts.name: Jaden McDaniels
breakouts.why: 2 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, Locked On). NBA Fantasy Bible: Departures of Naz Reid and Julius Randle raise his usage and move him to the four more often, which should lift rebounds and blocks. Projected to 15.7 points per game while keeping the defensive stats, playing with LaMelo Ball and Anthony Edwards. Locked On: Lloyd thinks 'he's probably got another step in him this season' with Naz Reid and Julius Randle gone.

breakouts.name: Ryan Rollins
breakouts.why: 2 creators (Old Man Squad, Locked On). Old Man Squad: Blossoming point guard job in Milwaukee; could be top 50. Locked On: Pushing top 50 if he starts over Kevin Porter Jr.

breakouts.name: Trae Young
breakouts.why: 2 creators (Locked On, Old Man Squad). Locked On: Minutes could rise by about seven a night from under 26, so he should beat last season's 85th; Lloyd still fades the price. Old Man Squad: Expected to bounce back into the top turnover group this season, meaning a full workload. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On, Old Man Squad, SportsEthos.

breakouts.name: Tyler Herro
breakouts.why: 2 creators (Hustle Sports, NBA Fantasy Bible). Hustle Sports: Career year possible as Milwaukee's lead option when healthy. NBA Fantasy Bible: D-Mac took him in the sixth as the expected number one usage player on the Bucks. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

breakouts.why: 2 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, FSAN). NBA Fantasy Bible: New Lakers centre next to Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves, critical to JJ Redick's defence. Hit 1.2 threes per game in a five-game sample last season. Comes in with a clean bill of health, which matters given his injury history. FSAN: Joiner's number two. ADP about 38, up from about 60. Averaged about 14 points, 10 rebounds, 3 assists, 1.5 steals and 2 blocks in five games last year and started making a three a game; now gets the 'Luka bump' as the Lakers' center. Clark is comfortable around pick 30 and can see 16 points and 12 rebounds with the same defense. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

breakouts.why: 2 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports). NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports: Ranked 6. With Jaylen Brown gone he takes on more facilitation and usage; James notes he averaged about 6 assists with triple-doubles late last season and sees a potential MVP season. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Old Man Squad.

breakouts.why: 2 creators (Adam King, RotoWire). Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Hustle Sports, Old Man Squad, Locked On.

breakouts.name: Alperen Sengun
breakouts.why: 1 creator (NBA Fantasy Bible). NBA Fantasy Bible: D-Mac thinks he has another step to take at age 24 if the defensive stats come. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports, Old Man Squad, SportsEthos.

breakouts.why: 1 creator (FSAN). FSAN: Joiner's number four. Role expands with Jalen Suggs' injury history and Cole Anthony gone; produced when he was the sole starting guard last year. Well-rounded: cuts, distributes, shoots threes, elite steals. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

breakouts.name: Bam Adebayo
breakouts.why: 1 creator (Hustle Sports). Hustle Sports: T-Will thinks Giannis and Adebayo are 'about to go crazy' together for fantasy, with Miami a possible top-four seed. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by NBA Fantasy Bible, Steve St-Pierre, Locked On, Old Man Squad, Noah Rubin, SportsEthos.

breakouts.why: 1 creator (NBA Fantasy Bible). NBA Fantasy Bible: Steps into a starting role after the Thunder's departures. Elite point-of-attack defence (steals) plus expanded on-ball usage as a secondary playmaker; shot threes and created well when SGA missed games. His game is not high-usage. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On.

breakouts.name: Coby White
breakouts.why: 1 creator (Number Two Sports). Number Two Sports: Chris's favorite breakout. ADP 89 with top 50 upside. Played a career-low 50 games last year and finished coming off the bench in Charlotte at 17.4 points, 3.4 rebounds, 4.0 assists and 2.3 threes. Charlotte moved on from LaMelo Ball and gave White a three-year, $74 million deal; Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On, FSAN.

breakouts.name: Derik Queen
breakouts.why: 1 creator (RotoWire). RotoWire: Already flirting with triple-doubles with more assist upside; if the three-ball comes along it is a massive breakout. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Noah Rubin, RotoWire, Locked On, Old Man Squad.

breakouts.name: Jalen Williams
breakouts.why: 1 creator (Noah Rubin). Noah Rubin: Bounce-back call after an injury-ruined year. Rubin had him top 20 in his mid-August 9-cat ranks and thinks he can finish as a second-round producer.

breakouts.name: Jeremiah Fears

breakouts.name: LaMelo Ball

breakouts.name: Oso Ighodaro

breakouts.name: Payton Pritchard

breakouts.name: Tyrese Maxey
breakouts.why: 1 creator (Hustle Sports). Hustle Sports: Benefits from LeBron as a facilitator creating easy looks. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade by Locked On, RotoWire, NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports.

breakouts.name: Victor Wembanyama

breakouts.name: Zach Edey

Rebounds projected slightly down because Cameron Boozer will take some. The entire question is health.

rookies.name: AJ Dybantsa
rookies.outlook: 9 creators (Hustle Sports, NBA Fantasy Bible, Steve St-Pierre, Noah Rubin, RotoWire, Locked On, Old Man Squad, League Winner Sports, SportsEthos). Hustle Sports: On the draft board as a patient, long-term play. Number one pick who averaged 25.5 points, almost 7 rebounds, 4 assists and 1 steal at BYU. Trae Young shares the ball and should not hurt him much; Anthony Davis is the concern for his usage. If Davis is hurt, as he typically is, or traded, Dybantsa's stock jumps. NBA Fantasy Bible, Steve St-Pierre: Went at the end of the eighth round. Putting on a show in preseason alongside Anthony Davis and Trae Young. Noah Rubin, RotoWire: Rubin would take him over Acuff in redraft. Alex calls Peterson more polished and safer than Dybantsa. Can defer to the talent around him in Washington. Locked On: Went about 112 in the flyer range of this mock; Lloyd offered no detail beyond 'let's do it' on the pick. Old Man Squad: Yahoo rank 93, one airplane. Besbris thinks around 100 is fair and does not see much upside 'with all the other stuff going on in Washington'; unlikely to land on his teams at that price. League Winner Sports: James does not expect an amazing rookie fantasy season because of the mouths to feed in Washington (Trae Young, Anthony Davis, Alex Sarr), though it is a good development spot. No round range given. SportsEthos: DRAFT in the later rounds, for points. Mark thinks he should be Washington's go-to scorer and can be relied on for points on acceptable FG% all season, with only base-level production in other categories, unlike Boozer or Wilson. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade at his price by Locked On.

rookies.name: Yaxel Lendeborg
rookies.outlook: 9 creators (RotoWire, Locked On, NBA Fantasy Bible, Steve St-Pierre, Fantasy on Points, The Roster Report, Old Man Squad, Number Two Sports, SportsEthos). RotoWire: Late-round flyer on Warriors minutes opening up through injuries; ADP has climbed a little. Locked On: Went about 107 at the end of round 9. NBA Fantasy Bible, Steve St-Pierre, Fantasy on Points: Tenth-round pick by Leo after a strong preseason with heavy usage; clear path to minutes on an injured Warriors roster. D-Mac passed four picks earlier, thinking the tenth was too early. The Roster Report: Rookie out of Michigan, ADP 142 (14th round of a 10-team draft), essentially named a Warriors starter. Helps points, rebounds, FG% with some stocks based on two preseason games. Meyer says the upside may be higher than any other player going that late. Old Man Squad: Two airplanes as a deep flier outside the top 125 (last-round pick). Well-rounded, fantasy-friendly game: 82% from the line at Michigan, rebounds, passes, hits threes, but steals and blocks will be modest. 6'9 and wide, will play power forward and some center; Number Two Sports: Noted only as the Warriors' one notable roster change via the draft. No projection given. SportsEthos: LATE FLYER. A 24-year-old rookie who should be a positive defender immediately and fits the Warriors system. Clear opportunity at forward with Jimmy Butler out, Kristaps Porzingis' health uncertain, and Draymond Green and Al Horford limited; Gui Santos is the only other forward.

rookies.name: Cameron Boozer
rookies.outlook: 8 creators (RotoWire, Locked On, Hustle Sports, NBA Fantasy Bible, Noah Rubin, The Roster Report, Number Two Sports, SportsEthos). RotoWire: Only mentioned in passing: host does not think Memphis wants to play him at center often. Locked On: Lloyd debated him at pick 50 and was surprised he lasted; he went in the mid-50s. Hustle Sports: T-Will rarely drafts rookies but makes an exception here: one of the few rookies without a major veteran ahead of him, so it is his team from day one. Averaged 22.5 points, 10 rebounds, 4 assists and 1 steal on 55% shooting at Duke, and 18 points, 7 rebounds, almost 4 assists and 1.5 steals in summer league. NBA Fantasy Bible: Went at the tenth pick of the fifth round (pick 58) in this 12-team Yahoo mock. No analysis given. Noah Rubin: Third overall pick and Rubin's top fantasy rookie; starts immediately for Memphis. Yahoo ADP 55.4 (fifth round) and both speakers say that is worth it; the 40s start to feel early though he could finish top 40. RotoWire projects about 17 points, 8 rebounds, 3 assists. Efficient across categories; The Roster Report: Mentioned only as part of a healthy Memphis lineup alongside Zach Edey. Number Two Sports: Named with Cedric Coward as the top of Memphis's youth-development priority list and expected to draw most of the attention there. No stats or round range given. SportsEthos: DRAFT. The safest rookie and the only one who is not a flyer: clearest role, focal point of the Grizzlies, about 30 minutes per game from the start, and he chips in every category. Helps rebounds, assists, threes, steals and blocks; the weak spot would be scoring efficiency. Rookie of the Year favourite at +300.

rookies.name: Darius Acuff Jr.
rookies.outlook: 7 creators (Locked On, Fantasy on Points, Noah Rubin, Old Man Squad, FSAN, League Winner Sports, SportsEthos). Locked On: Taken by Lloyd at 119 as a flyer. Fantasy on Points: Leo took him in the eleventh round: 'moving like a vet' in preseason, looks like the guy in Sacramento and should get good usage. Leo says to target him late in real drafts. Noah Rubin: Will start and have the ball constantly, running two-man game with Domantas Sabonis; points and assists with 'off the charts' usage. Expect bad efficiency: FG% around 40%, above 43% would shock Rubin, plus turnovers. Better in points leagues; a great later-round pick if you punt FG%, turnovers or both. Old Man Squad: The most interesting of the one-airplane deep fliers ranked outside the top 125 (11th to 13th round range). No stats or role detail given in this episode. FSAN: The Kings are publicly committed to him as their centerpiece (media-day footage of him shooting with eight development coaches). The hosts excluded rookies from the breakout list by rule. League Winner Sports: Named only as part of a Kings youth movement James expects them to lean into, alongside Maxime Raynaud and Dylan Cardwell. SportsEthos: LATE FLYER, early-to-mid 100s. Sixth overall pick and the most natural point guard on the Kings, expected to start from the opener. Helps points, threes and assists. Hurts FG% and turnovers and gives no defensive stats, so he will grade badly in rankings.

rookies.name: Darryn Peterson
rookies.outlook: 6 creators (Locked On, Noah Rubin, RotoWire, Hustle Sports, Number Two Sports, SportsEthos). Locked On: Went about 117 in 'flyer territory'. Noah Rubin, RotoWire: Rubin's number two rookie in redraft and dynasty. Looks set to start right away for Utah alongside Keyonte George, Jaren Jackson Jr., Lauri Markkanen and Jusuf Nurkic, with Ace Bailey to the bench. Elite off-ball shooter in Will Hardy's curl-heavy system; Hustle Sports: 'A little iffy': hard to see him coming in and doing his thing on a loaded Utah roster. A risk pick; watch his preseason role. Number Two Sports: Only a passing mention: Chris expects Peterson and Ace Bailey to form 'a monster one-two punch' for years, though maybe not this year. No fantasy projection given. SportsEthos: DRAFT only at a discount; both hosts have cooled. Probably fourth in the shot pecking order behind Keyonte George, Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr., with Isaiah Collier, Ace Bailey, Brice Sensabaugh and Kyle Filipowski also needing minutes. Excellent target for threes off the ball; Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade at his price by Hustle Sports, SportsEthos.

rookies.name: Keaton Wagler
rookies.outlook: 6 creators (Locked On, Steve St-Pierre, Noah Rubin, Old Man Squad, Number Two Sports, SportsEthos). Locked On: Went 154. Steve St-Pierre: Steve's twelfth-round flyer: huge opportunity because the Clippers are running out of bodies and have every incentive to play him. Noah Rubin: Probably not starting, though with more of a chance than Flemings. Old Man Squad: Only a passing mention: took 15 shots in the Clippers' first preseason game, which Besbris says to take with a grain of salt. Number Two Sports: Deep-league breakout pick at ADP around 120. Fifth overall pick out of Illinois, a polished shot maker and creator. Chris was not sold until the Brandon Ingram injury news; now thinks he can step in as the Clippers' second scoring option behind Darius Garland with heavy usage available from the start of the season. SportsEthos: LATE FLYER, borderline stash. The Clippers did not bring back Bennedict Mathurin, which helps, but Darius Garland, Kris Dunn, Bradley Beal, Gradey Dick, Max Strus and Brandon Ingram are all there. If the usage is there early he gives threes with some points and assists; if Beal is ahead of him, cut and move on. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade at his price by Locked On.

rookies.name: Caleb Wilson
rookies.outlook: 6 creators (Locked On, NBA Fantasy Bible, Noah Rubin, Number Two Sports, Hustle Sports, SportsEthos). NBA Fantasy Bible: Went in the first half of the eighth round. No analysis given. Noah Rubin: Rubin would take him over Acuff in redraft; named as a threat to Matas Buzelis' touches if he is good right away. Number Two Sports: Drafted by the Bulls. Chris expects rookie growing pains at points during the year and does not think he threatens Matas Buzelis's starting job; no round range given. Hustle Sports: Grouped with Boozer as a rookie with a lot of opportunity as one of the main players on Chicago's roster; should give a good season if you can get him. SportsEthos: DRAFT. Dr. A's guy and his Rookie of the Year pick at +330; he is 'going in'. Mark says he will get minutes on the Bulls and 'do stuff' across categories, which translates to fantasy, but scoring and on-ball play will be uneven night to night and the summer league three-point accuracy should not be expected to hold (the volume...

rookies.name: Mikel Brown Jr.
rookies.outlook: 6 creators (RotoWire, Steve St-Pierre, Noah Rubin, Locked On, Adam King, SportsEthos). RotoWire: Flyer on the Nets; has not played in preseason because of an ankle injury. Alex is not worried about Julius Randle and Michael Porter Jr. icing him out since Brooklyn is moving the ball in preseason. Steve St-Pierre: Steve considered him with his thirteenth-round pick and had him queued, but passed because he already had enough guards. Noah Rubin: May or may not start; had not yet played in preseason. Locked On: Went 138. Not seen in preseason yet; Lloyd fears he is not ready to start the season. Adam King: Named as one of the risky late-round swings other teams took. SportsEthos: STASH, arguably a late-round sleeper. Mark expects him to start for Brooklyn, with the question being how fast Jordi Fernandez hands him the offence next to Julius Randle, Michael Porter Jr. and Egor Demin. Assists and threes early, with a role that grows into standard-league impact later. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade at his price by Locked On.

rookies.name: Brayden Burries
rookies.outlook: 5 creators (RotoWire, Old Man Squad, Locked On, Number Two Sports, SportsEthos). RotoWire: Looked very comfortable in Las Vegas and in preseason. Stuck in a Bucks logjam for now, but the host thinks Milwaukee will struggle to keep him off the floor as the season goes on; value rises if Tyler Herro is hurt or Kevin Porter Jr. is moved. Last-pick flyer. Old Man Squad: Only a passing mention: the Bucks are going to try to get him action at a guard spot, which is part of the minutes squeeze on Kevin Porter Jr. Locked On: Not starting; four other guards ahead of him. Deeper-league long shot. Number Two Sports: Only noted as a new addition to the Bucks backcourt that crowds Kevin Porter Jr.'s role. No fantasy projection given. SportsEthos: LATE FLYER, last or second-to-last pick. Milwaukee's first pick, but the guard rotation with Tyler Herro and Ryan Rollins is unclear. If he gets starter minutes he is a Brandin Podziemski-type glue guy: some assists, rebounds, steals and points for back-end standard-league value. Disagreement: also named as a bust or fade at his price by Locked On.

rookies.name: Hannes Steinbach
rookies.outlook: 3 creators (Noah Rubin, Locked On, RotoWire). Noah Rubin: Replaces Mason Plumlee in Charlotte's three-center rotation with Diabate and Kalkbrenner. Good rebounder who got defensive stats but is not a great defensive big; more of a threat to Diabate's minutes than Kalkbrenner is. Locked On: Expected backup center who may also get minutes behind Naz Reid. Lloyd thinks he would out-produce Moussa Diabate at equal minutes but prefers Diabate 90/10 on role. RotoWire: Alex assumes he is Charlotte's fifth starter alongside Coby White, Kon Knueppel, Brandon Miller and Naz Reid. (The later Noah Rubin episode has Moussa Diabate starting instead.)

rookies.name: Morez Johnson Jr.
rookies.outlook: 3 creators (Locked On, RotoWire, SportsEthos). Locked On: Undersized rookie big who is injured and missing training camp; moves up Lloyd's list if he plays in preseason. RotoWire: Rookie in the Dallas center mix; unclear how many center minutes he can handle right away. SportsEthos: STASH, arguable late pick. Ninth overall pick with his college coach Dusty May now coaching the Mavericks; can play power forward or centre. Early on expect rebounds, blocks and FG% help and not much else, in a crowded frontcourt with Daniel Gafford, Dereck Lively II, P.J. Washington, Naji Marshall and Santi Aldama. Dr.

rookies.name: Kingston Flemings
rookies.outlook: 3 creators (Noah Rubin, RotoWire, SportsEthos). Noah Rubin: Probably not starting. RotoWire: Lottery pick mentioned only as part of Atlanta's crowded backcourt. SportsEthos: STASH, watch list only. First or second guard off the bench behind CJ McCollum, Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Dyson Daniels and Lu Dort. Do not trust him in week one or month one; if he adapts he could reach 25 minutes later and add points, assists, threes and steals.

rookies.name: Aday Mara
rookies.outlook: 1 creator (RotoWire). RotoWire: Through two preseason games he was 15-of-15 from the field in 43 minutes with 34 points, 15 rebounds, 5 assists and 4 blocks.

rookies.name: Allen Graves
rookies.outlook: 1 creator (SportsEthos). SportsEthos: STASH. Forward-sized bench piece who adds three-point shooting, defensive versatility and some passing; strong per-minute producer who could matter at 18 to 20-plus minutes late in the season. Kyle Anderson likely gets the minutes first. Becomes a pickup if Kawhi Leonard misses time. Not in players.json; team per transcript.

rookies.name: Bennett Stirtz
rookies.outlook: 1 creator (SportsEthos). SportsEthos: STASH, more of a 14-team name. Mark thinks he could beat Jared McCain for the Thunder's backup guard minutes as a better shooter and ball mover, adding assists, threes, some points and steals later in the season. Has been falling in dynasty rookie drafts. Not in players.json; team per transcript.

rookies.name: Cameron Carr
rookies.outlook: 1 creator (SportsEthos). SportsEthos: AVOID in drafts, remember the name. Three-point shooting with a knack for blocks and steals, but he needs to bulk up and is unlikely to see rotation minutes early; possible spot minutes from December to February. Not in players.json; team per transcript.

rookies.name: Nate Ament
rookies.outlook: 1 creator (SportsEthos). SportsEthos: AVOID in drafts, watch only. Relevant only if the Bucks go full youth and play him 30 minutes with Kyle Kuzma out of the rotation. Mark does not love his fantasy profile and would not draft him even as a sleeper. Not in players.json; team per transcript.

FSAN: Probable starting center with Mark Williams out; shares the position with Oso Ighodaro. Locked On: Almost locked in as the starting center. SportsEthos: Now Minnesota's lead guard alongside Anthony Edwards.

SportsEthos: Moved to Charlotte and should start at power forward; Miles Bridges is gone from the Hornets.

role_changes.name: Kawhi Leonard
role_changes.change: 7 creators (Old Man Squad, Noah Rubin, RotoWire, NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports, Adam King, SportsEthos). role_changes.name: Collin Murray-Boyles

strategy_notes.point: Locked On: Yahoo's single rank list blends several rankers and every format, so category drafters should fade points-flavoured names near their rank (Brunson at 29) and points drafters should fade category names (Anunoby at 69, Trey Murphy at 28).
Locked On: Straight nine-cat rankings (Kessler 28th, Banchero outside the top 100, Giannis outside the top 50) should not drive category draft decisions.
Locked On: Injured stars: Lloyd will not take Ingram inside the top 120 with a partially torn Achilles, and discounts Haliburton for early-season restrictions rather than for re-injury.
Locked On: Do not pay for small-sample spikes: Kessler's five-game steal, assist and three-point jump is 'absolute best case randomness'.
Locked On: Mid-round veterans on bad teams carry trade risk at the worst time: a deadline move to a better team can crater usage in the fantasy playoffs (Norman Powell).
Locked On: Round 9 is your second-worst starter and should not be a bench player who needs injuries (Dosunmu, Sexton). Round 10 flyers are acceptable; round 11 suits them better.
Locked On: Do not over-index on games played: Mikal Bridges plays every night and was still unrosterable per game.
Locked On: Be sceptical of 'NBA-ready' older rookies; being old is not the same as being good. Lloyd reserves aggressive rookie ranks for players who are good at 19.

Locked On: ESPN's October 9 category re-rank (Avdija 5, Adebayo 7, Booker 8, Giddey 11, Jerome 13, Reaves 64) is unusable; Lloyd is dropping ESPN coverage and tells people to play on Yahoo or Fantrax.
Old Man Squad: H2H each-category is not roto: it pays to be very strong in five to seven categories even if you are weak in one to four others. Roto is about balance.
Old Man Squad: Second-round targets must be realistic: stay within about three picks of your actual second-round slot on the Yahoo board (pick 1 comes back at 24, pick 5 at 20, pick 12 at 13).
Old Man Squad: With a top-four pick you have such a big advantage that the main job in round 2 is not to mess it up. Avoid risk and ADP underperformers.

Old Man Squad: Wembanyama: do not ruin his free throw percentage by doubling up on a low-70s-or-worse FT% shot-blocking big (Kessler, Clingan, Mobley, Sabonis). You do not need more blocks on top of him. Get points and guard stats early; blocks and rebounds come later.
Old Man Squad: Wembanyama no longer forces a guard build: 51% FG and almost 83% FT now. He still lags other early centers in FG% impact, so tilting toward lower-FG% guards is the H2H play.

Old Man Squad: Jokic: the only mistake is trying to fix blocks (0.8). Avoid Chet Holmgren and Evan Mobley in round 2, avoid risk (Kawhi, LaMelo, Curry) and ADP underperformers. Anyone who beats their 9-cat ADP fits. Punting blocks and/or turnovers both work.

Old Man Squad: Luka: your second-round pick chooses the punt. Trae Young means punt FG% and TO; Giddey means punt TO and probably FT%. Then the third-round pick gets harder because you have to commit quickly. Keep the scoring lead: no low scorers, so no Chet and no Sabonis.

Old Man Squad: Luka's margin for error is smaller than SGA's even though his second-round options are more numerous, because Luka's percentages are a negative and you cannot sacrifice his points or threes.

Old Man Squad: SGA: easiest punts are threes (1.7 per game, lowest in the first round) or assists (6.5). You can even punt points with him because he is the best in the NBA in aggregate at the two percentages on huge volume. Dan prefers going well-rounded and deciding later.
Old Man Squad: SGA: never put a hole in his percentages without a matching big win elsewhere. LaMelo and Sengun fail that test; Trae Young passes it.

Old Man Squad: Guard build (punt FG% plus punt TO) finally works this year because Trae, Harden and LaMelo fall to rounds 2 and 3 instead of all going by pick 13 or 14. You can get three of them on one team, and only one or two teams are trying it instead of four.
Old Man Squad: Guard build downside: steals. Cade is pretty good, Harden meh, Trae poor, LaMelo okay. Fix steals by about round 5 after you take a big, or you will only be great at four categories.
Old Man Squad: In a Cade guard build the second-round pick must score around 25 a game (or 20-plus from a big). Do not take a punt-points type like Amen Thompson or Chet Holmgren.

Old Man Squad: Maxey, Tatum, Edwards and Mitchell are the 'Spider-Man meme' group: all high-points, high-threes players who want the same second-rounders. This part of the board is a pain in H2H. Take a well-rounded ADP-beater (Murray, Reaves, Durant) and pick the punt later, even retooling in December.

Old Man Squad: Dan takes Giannis at 6 (Yahoo has him 9), right after Cade: this is the year to punt something hard before you reach the Spider-Man group, because it flips the board and you stop competing for the same players.

Old Man Squad: Giannis build: definitely punt FT%, maybe turnovers too. Get points, assists and steals from guards or a scoring big early; rebounds, blocks and FG% are plentiful later from punt-FT bigs who shoot 62%. Do not take a traditional big like Jalen Duren early.

Old Man Squad: Jalen Johnson is 'the crappy version of Jokic'. A punt-blocks build with him loses 8-1 to the Jokic team, so go the other way: beat Jokic teams in rebounds, assists, steals, blocks and turnovers.

Old Man Squad: Haliburton: best move is punt points. Elite threes, assists, FT% and an extremely low turnover number for an assist guard. If you punt points you need one volume-efficiency player by round 3, and those are nearly gone after round 2 (Kawhi in round 3 is the risky option, Kyrie in round 4 does not help FG% enough).

Old Man Squad: If you miss your two favorites among Maxey, Tatum, Edwards and Mitchell, there is a good H2H case for Jalen Johnson (punt blocks or points) or Haliburton (punt points) simply to change which players you are fighting for.
Old Man Squad: Dan likes to get his big man in the third round.
Old Man Squad: Tatum: do not dent his rebounding edge and do not try to fix his steals and blocks in one swing. If you kill one defensive stat make it steals; one big fixes blocks.
Old Man Squad: Edwards: do not chase assists (3.7 per game, lowest of the group). Likely a punt-assists team, so skip Ball, Trae, Sengun and Sabonis.

Adam King/RotoWire: In an expert 12-team 9-cat draft the first-round shuffle was unusual: Cooper Flagg 7th, Scottie Barnes 9th, Tyrese Haliburton 12th, Anthony Edwards 13th, Jalen Johnson 16th, Kawhi Leonard 19th, Lauri Markkanen 26th.

Adam King/RotoWire: Center supply: there is a run of usable centers around pick 100 (Day'Ron Sharpe, Myles Turner, Derik Queen, Jarrett Allen, Kristaps Porzingis, Khaman Maluach, Jusuf Nurkic, Nic Claxton, Neemias Queta). In a one-center league you can reach round 6 to 8 with no center and be fine.
RotoWire: In a TWO-center league, reaching round 8 without a center means trouble, because the same players will not be on waivers either.

Adam King/RotoWire: Find sleepers by reading thin depth charts for the player who absorbs minutes when anyone is hurt: VJ Edgecombe (PHI), Anthony Black (ORL), Ajay Mitchell (OKC), Dylan Harper (SAS), Grayson Allen (CHA), Josh Hart (NYK) as the template.

Adam King: A three or four-category punt will almost certainly not finish first in the regular-season standings. The aim is to beat every opponent in five or six categories, sit safely in the top four to six, then roll through the playoffs.
Adam King: Giannis is the easiest star to learn punting with because threes and FT% are obvious punts. The swing category in that build is steals, so you need a Dyson Daniels or Cason Wallace type.

Adam King/RotoWire: Punting assists is rarely a hard punt if your bigs and wings pass (Sengun, Sabonis, Barnes, Jalen Johnson, Josh Hart); it becomes a swing category. There are few assists available late in drafts.

RotoWire: Late steals specialists tend to also be good three-point and FT% shooters, value that is wasted in a punt-threes/FT% build. That is an argument to reach a round early for the pure defensive players (Dyson Daniels, Ausar Thompson) before a like-minded drafter snipes them.
Adam King: With picks at the turn, reach for your guy (Markkanen at 26) because he will not survive the 20-plus picks until you are up again.
RotoWire: Use your last two picks on upside flyers in a normal league where you can drop them; Alex went safe late only because this league allowed no roster moves.
Adam King: Tanking rules changed, so Brooklyn and Utah players carry less shutdown risk than in prior years, though long 'rest' absences after minor injuries are still a risk on non-contenders.
Adam King: People are either on or off Tyrese Haliburton depending on how long they expect early-season limitations to last.

Old Man Squad: Dan's H2H first round: 1 Jokic, 2 Wembanyama, 3 Gilgeous-Alexander, 4 Doncic, 5 and 6 Cunningham and Giannis, 7 and 8 Maxey and Edwards, 9 Jalen Johnson, 10 Mitchell, 11 Tatum, 12 Haliburton, then Flagg at 13 followed by Durant, Jamal Murray, Scottie Barnes and Reaves.
Old Man Squad: There is a clear drop-off after the top 17 (first round plus Flagg, Durant, Murray, Barnes, Reaves).

Old Man Squad: Jokic over Wembanyama because he is hyper elite in assists, rebounds and FG% with one small hole (0.8 blocks) that a 0.6-to-0.7 block guard cancels. Wemby has more value tied to one category, blocks at 3.1.
Old Man Squad: Threes are one of the easiest categories to find later: the first three picks (Jokic 1.7, Wemby 1.9, Shai 1.7) are not three-point players.

Old Man Squad: Shai over Luka for Dan. Shai supports punt threes, punt assists or even punt points because his FG% and FT% on volume are the hardest things to find for a punt-points team. Never build punt FT% around Shai.

Old Man Squad: Luka's best categories are counting stats (points, threes, rebounds, assists), which are less volatile week to week than percentages and defensive stats. That is the H2H case for Luka; in roto Shai runs away with it. Punting turnovers lifts Luka from 6th to 4th.
Old Man Squad: With the fifth pick, 14 selections pass before your next one, and this year almost none of those teams want your guard-build or punt-FT players. Cade and Giannis flip the board.
Old Man Squad: Cade is the safer punt anchor of the two: if the punt fails he is still a good player, while a failed Giannis punt leaves a first-rounder worth about 65th.

Old Man Squad: Giannis build options: win rebounds, FG%, blocks and turnovers and add one guard category, or give up turnovers, win rebounds, FG% and blocks and add two guard categories (points plus steals or assists).
Old Man Squad: For the Maxey, Edwards, Mitchell, Tatum group, all within about eight per-game slots, rank them by who plays the most games.
Old Man Squad: Punt points is harder this year: mid-round favorites are gone and big men are being overdrafted, so the percentages bigs with steals and blocks are not there later.
Old Man Squad: Well-rounded second-rounders with upside pair with every first-rounder and let you delay the punt decision, which matters most with the Spider-Man group.
Old Man Squad: Turnovers: only Cade, Jokic, Luka and Trae sit near 3.5 to 4 a game now. Most first-rounders are 2.2 to 2.9, so a 3.7 really costs you in 9-cat.

NBA Fantasy Bible: This mock is Yahoo, 12-team, 9-category, 13 rounds, default two centre slots, 30-second picks. First round went Wembanyama, Jokic, Gilgeous-Alexander, Doncic, Cunningham, Antetokounmpo, Tatum, Jalen Johnson, Maxey, Edwards, Flagg, Mitchell.
Steve St-Pierre: Get guards early and often: the elite guards go fast and guards 'run dry' in the middle rounds (rounds five to seven).
