NBA Fantasy Bible/Steve St-Pierre/Fantasy on Points: Bigs also go early, and in Yahoo's two-centre format reliable centres are gone by round eight, where all three hosts were taking upside bigs (Day'Ron Sharpe, Khaman Maluach, Collin Murray-Boyles). 'There's not many reliable, 100% safe picks' at centre by then.
Steve St-Pierre: For 9-cat, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is preferred over Luka Doncic at pick three because he is more balanced; Doncic is better in points formats.
NBA Fantasy Bible: Trae Young in 9-cat: target the back of the second round or the third to lock down assists, then build FG% back up later.

Steve St-Pierre: Mix risk and safety. Steve took Curry, Davis, Irving and Embiid, then balanced with Okongwu and Anunoby; he would only draft that many injury risks in a real league with a handful of IL spots. With one or two IL spots it is a very risky draft, so go safer and healthier.

Steve St-Pierre: A last-round injured stash (Jimmy Butler) can go straight to IL so you can pick up or stream a healthy player in that slot; the comparison was stashing Jayson Tatum last year, who won leagues when he returned late.
NBA Fantasy Bible: Around pick 100 (round eight on) switch to flyer picks on players you believe in from preseason.

NBA Fantasy Bible/Steve St-Pierre: Yahoo ADP differs from Fantrax and ESPN, so adjust expectations by platform; set your queue with 30-second picks, and note Yahoo does not let you move players between slots during the draft, so positional eligibility matters.
NBA Fantasy Bible: Giannis Antetokounmpo is valued more in points leagues; D-Mac finds Jayson Tatum easier to build a 9-cat team around at pick seven.
Noah Rubin: Seven or eight rookies should have redraft value this year; most go around pick 100, only Cameron Boozer costs a top-60 pick.
Noah Rubin: Take one thing from preseason: who is starting. Do not overreact to box scores.
Noah Rubin: A 'sleeper' can simply be a last-round pick who finishes around top 100 (Diabate); that kind of value matters as much as the top-50 lottery tickets.
RotoWire: Value built on defensive stats is fragile: a small drop in block rate (Buzelis from 1.8 to 1.4 per 36) moves 9-cat rank a lot.
RotoWire: For young bigs like Derik Queen and Kel'el Ware the real fantasy problem last year was inconsistent minutes (random 11 to 12 minute nights), not their season-long rank.
RotoWire: Poor-FT%, high-turnover, low-threes guards like Stephon Castle only make sense at ADP inside specific punt builds, not balanced or roto teams.
Number Two Sports: Chris never weighs turnovers when valuing a player in 9-cat: he usually ends up punting the category, or looks at it only after the draft shows he can compete in it.

Number Two Sports: Prioritize players with a defensive floor of about one steal and one block per game, since that holds value regardless of what happens on offense (Murray-Boyles, Buzelis, Ausar Thompson, Sharpe).
Number Two Sports: More minutes and touches only matter if the player has a fantasy-friendly, well-rounded skill set to convert them.
Number Two Sports: Center plan: if you wait on the position and miss the earlier options like Zach Edey and Kel'el Ware, Day'Ron Sharpe in the 90s is the target.
Number Two Sports: Wings who cannot shoot from outside struggle to hold 30-plus minutes regardless of defense, which caps players like Ausar Thompson.
Hustle Sports: In head-to-head 9-cat the goal is to win at least five categories a week; plan to win six because 'five is too close to four'. You do not need to dominate everything.

Hustle Sports: Take Victor Wembanyama over anyone in a 9-cat first round: elite blocks are the scarce foundation. Scoring and three-point shooting are easier to find later in the draft and during the season; shot-blocking centres are not.

Hustle Sports: Second building block is a playmaking frontcourt player (Jalen Johnson, or Scottie Barnes or Alperen Sengun) so assists come from a non-point guard on top of scoring and rebounds. The trade-off is more turnovers from ball handling.

Hustle Sports: Threes are everywhere, so target efficient shooters who do not hurt elsewhere: Collin Gillespie late; Desmond Bane, Kon Knueppel or Michael Porter Jr. mid-draft when you want threes plus something else.

Hustle Sports: Identify your steals source early in planning even though players like Dyson Daniels come late; defensive production wins categories, and this is where 9-cat ranks diverge most from points ranks.
Hustle Sports: Re-evaluate roster strengths and weaknesses after every round from round three onward.
Hustle Sports: T-Will prefers balanced builds over punts: balance makes you hard to beat top to bottom. He explicitly says do not punt or sleep on bigs.

Hustle Sports: Percentage categories are volume-weighted: a 90% shooter on two free throws moves FT% less than a 65% big taking seven or eight. High-FG% bigs (Clingan, Gobert, Duren, Mitchell Robinson) are the fix for FG% damage from high-volume guards.
Hustle Sports: 'The big man might be on the way back': do not sleep on centres for FG%, rebounds and blocks.
Hustle Sports: Never overspend, and do not pay for a breakout before it happens; a small reach on a specific need (Clingan) is the exception.

Hustle Sports: Pre-draft checklist: know your format; what did your first-round pick establish; where are steals, assists and blocks coming from; are you ignoring turnovers; are your players efficient (high usage trades off against efficiency); the highest-ranked player is not always the best fit for your roster.
Hustle Sports: Availability is a skill: players who do not miss games (Mikal Bridges, Collin Gillespie at 80 games) make a roster hard to beat.
Number Two Sports: Three kinds of sleepers: players who improved late last season, players with a role or team change, and players who were bad or hurt last year and are discounted by recency bias.

Number Two Sports: On injury-prone players: injuries cannot be predicted, and discounted injury-label players paid off last year (he cites LaMelo Ball and Kawhi Leonard). Take one, maybe two, at a discount, but do not stack Anthony Davis, Kawhi Leonard, LaMelo Ball, Joel Embiid and Zion Williamson on one team. Avoiding them entirely and betting on the backup (Anthony Black for Suggs) is also a fair strategy.

Number Two Sports: Late in drafts, target players who could move into the starting unit with a usage bump and who have a well-rounded stat set or are dominant in two or three categories. A new starter who gives 12 points, 2 rebounds and 1 assist is not useful.
Number Two Sports: Avoid late picks whose value depends mainly on a high FG% with limited defensive stats (Christian Braun, Cam Spencer), because shooting percentages vary year to year.
Number Two Sports: Contract-year motivation is real in Chris's view; he applies it to Zach LaVine, Cameron Johnson and Anthony Black.
Number Two Sports: Dislike of the Kings' roster has swung too far, creating value on Sacramento players.
Number Two Sports: Past ADP 100 to 120, look for players with the foundation to jump 30 to 40 spots.
Old Man Squad: Dan's top four in order: Jokic, Wembanyama, Gilgeous-Alexander, Doncic. In H2H flipping Luka over Shai is fine.

Old Man Squad: With a top-four pick, treat the pick at 21 to 24 as a third-round pick. The end of the second round is full of punt-only players (LaMelo, Booker, Sengun, Sabonis), so think 'who would I take mid-third' and the answer gets simpler.
Old Man Squad: In H2H the end-of-second pick is a fit pick that chooses your punt. With Jokic: either a big who does not block shots or an assists guard with turnovers thrown away.
Old Man Squad: You get two picks together at the 2-3 turn. If one is a big, make the other a guard. Do not take too much risk here after a great first-round pick.
Old Man Squad: Round 4 (pick 48) is where to take the first risk: Kyrie Irving or Anthony Davis. If neither is there, treat it like a fifth-round pick and reach for a player you like.
Old Man Squad: At the front-end turns you have to reach half a round to a round. Taking a 55 to 60 player at 50 is still value.

Old Man Squad: Two risk-reward players through seven rounds is fine if the rest are safe and the second-rounder is someone who will play. After two risks take a high-floor player in round 8 (Wiggins) instead of another swing.
Old Man Squad: By pick 95 in sharper drafts the reliable part of the board is gone; ignore pre-ranks and take whoever you want. Jerome, Hart, Turner and Suggs are already off the board by then.

Old Man Squad: Late-round upside does not have to mean a player who has never done it. Prefer the one who needs nothing to change (Keegan Murray, Queta, Suggs) over the one who needs several things to break right (Lendeborg). Go by the odds of a top-100 finish.
Old Man Squad: Hardest spots with an early pick: end of round 2, then end of round 8, then end of round 4. The round 6-7 turn is the easy one with real value.
Old Man Squad: Holmgren fits lower-scoring anchors (Haliburton, Jalen Johnson, Cade) and Shai. He makes no H2H sense with Jokic and is redundant with Wembanyama.
Old Man Squad: $250 Yahoo leagues are effectively all experts. In $20, $50 and some $100 leagues players like Ty Jerome slide a round or two.
Locked On: 'There is no such thing as a must-draft player.' Every name is relative to its current site rank; do not take a 50th-best player at 20 because he was called a must-draft.

Locked On: Yahoo's pre-ranks are format-agnostic, one list for points and categories, so category drafters get value on players the blended list drags down (Davis at 45, Daniels at 62, Alexander-Walker at 58) and should avoid points-flavoured names.
Locked On: Injured or risky stars: price decides. Anthony Davis at 45 and Kawhi at 45 are fine; Kawhi in the teens or 20s is not. 'I wouldn't stack the risk players on top of each other.'
Locked On: Do not build analysis on imagined motives (for example 'Davis faked injuries because he did not want to be in Dallas'). Lloyd also says contract years are proven not to lift performance.

Locked On: Straight nine-cat rankings are 'incorrectly used' in category formats: they had Giannis about 70th, Banchero 125th and Trey Murphy 11th last season. Lloyd prefers a head-to-head ranking and discounts turnover and percentage penalties on high-usage stars.
Locked On: League winners are players taken outside the top 100 who return top-50 numbers; his named candidates are Ryan Rollins, Paul George (at ESPN's rank) and Zach Edey.
Locked On: Rounds 11 and later are 'real flyer zone'; round 10 is borderline.

Locked On: Yahoo's third round by rank (25-36) is Curry, Adebayo, Mobley, Trey Murphy, Brunson, Markkanen, Holmgren, Duren, Harden, Sabonis, Brandon Miller, Kawhi; Lloyd sees nothing egregious there, with Sabonis the best value.

Old Man Squad: Yahoo board 4 (October 1): 1 Jokic, 2 Wembanyama, 3 Doncic, 4 Gilgeous-Alexander, 5 Cunningham, 6 Giannis, 7 Tatum, 8 Edwards, 9 Maxey, 10 Haliburton, 11 Jalen Johnson, 12 Mitchell, 13 Flagg, 14 Durant, 15 Barnes, 16 Towns, 17 Murray, 18 Trae Young, 19 Giddey, 20 Amen Thompson, 21 Reaves, 22 Sengun, 23 Booker, 24 LaMelo Ball, 25 Curry, 26 Adebayo.
Old Man Squad: Jokic is Dan's number one because no single punt drops him below top three or four. Only soft spots are turnovers (ignorable with almost 11 assists) and 0.8 blocks.

Old Man Squad: Points, rebounds and assists are the most predictable categories week to week; percentages and low-volume defensive stats swing. That is why H2H players and Yahoo put Luka ahead of Shai.

Old Man Squad: Cade at 5: fine either way, much better if you ignore turnovers and go guard build. He is still a 30 to 40% shot at turnovers if you do not punt, and one 1.5-turnover player in the first three rounds catches you up.
Old Man Squad: Giannis is different: nobody can fix his FT% single-handedly. Drafting normally leaves about a 15% chance at the category, so commit to the punt.
Old Man Squad: Punting with Cade, Giannis or Haliburton is valuable mainly because it changes who you draft and when, so you stop competing with the rest of the league for the same players.

Old Man Squad: Dan has never felt as strongly about the advantage of the punt as this season. To beat the top-four teams in five categories in a playoff week the other eight teams need to get creative.

Old Man Squad: Tatum, Edwards, Maxey, Mitchell, Flagg and Durant are six near-identical builds (punt assists or punt one defensive stat). If you sit in the middle of them you get sniped every round unless you flip the board.

Old Man Squad: Tatum, Edwards and Maxey should all land near 12th per game; the winner is whoever plays the most games, a coin flip. Likely punts: Edwards assists, Tatum steals, Maxey nothing obvious (so he is the roto pick and gets Dan's nod).
Old Man Squad: In a punt-points build you must draft the volume-percentages players early; steals, blocks, assists and rebounds can be found later.
Old Man Squad: Do not get so caught up in build theory that you draft a player who is just not good.
Old Man Squad: Guard build bigs should score and block or hit threes rather than rebound, like Jaren Jackson Jr. Try not to hard punt four categories.
Old Man Squad: A bad-health pick in the second round loses the season out of the gate.
Old Man Squad: Dan likes getting a center in the third round.
Old Man Squad: If you run several H2H teams and do guard builds in two, take LaMelo Ball in one of them.
Adam King: Turnovers are one of the four weakest categories for every top-12 player by Yahoo ADP because they all handle the ball so much.
Adam King: Threes from big men are worth less than three or five years ago because almost every center shoots them now (Clingan, Okongwu), so threes are a reasonable punt next to Wembanyama or Jokic.
Adam King: There is a pretty significant drop-off after pick 4. Cade's overall stat set is not that loaded: points and assists, few threes, middling percentages.
Adam King: First multi-category punt? Use the guard build: target points, threes, assists, steals and FT%, ignore rebounds, blocks, FG% and turnovers. Maxey is the easiest anchor for it.

Adam King: King's favorite build is the big-man build: punt points, threes and FT% (he also lists turnovers among the four, though the build ends up good in turnovers); target rebounds, blocks, FG%, steals and low turnovers. Across 11 leagues last season it made the playoffs in 10 and won four.

Adam King: In the big-man build steals are the swing category, so take elite steals players early (Barnes, Amen Thompson, Dyson Daniels, Ausar Thompson) and stack non-center shot blockers before taking late centers.
Adam King: There are almost no shot blockers in the first round besides Wembanyama, so Barnes's blocks are enough of a head start.
Adam King: Starting Barnes plus Amen Thompson gives you a forward and a guard-eligible player, so you do not have to scramble for a guard in rounds 5 to 7.
Adam King: If you punt points with Giannis, the later targets (Ausar Thompson, Walker Kessler, Dyson Daniels, Amen Thompson) are all below-average scorers, which wastes Giannis's scoring.
Adam King: You can offset an injury-risk second-rounder (Curry) by pairing him with a durable first-rounder (Cade, Tatum).
Adam King: Wembanyama and Jokic do not need a punt at all; these are options, and you can punt one or two of the four listed categories instead of all four.
RotoWire: After about pick 100 ADP is nebulous: if you really believe in a player, just take him rather than worrying about reaching.
RotoWire: Finding sleepers this late is partly about knowing who is simply a good 9-cat player: low turnovers, threes and some stocks (Royce O'Neale is the example).
RotoWire: A backup big who gets 20 to 25 minutes can be streamed in on four-game weeks (Isaiah Stewart).
RotoWire: Late-round wings who only shoot threes (Ja'Kobe Walter, Duncan Robinson, Sam Merrill types) are four-game-week streamers for the 3PM category.

Old Man Squad: Blanket rule: if a player is out on opening night, do not draft him. Besbris says it works out about 12% of the time and lists last year's failures who started the year hurt: Coby White, Paul George, Darius Garland, LeBron James (fine per game but only 60 games), Tyler Herro, Keegan Murray, Zach Edey, Jalen Green; De'Aaron Fox (72 games) was the closest thing to a success. Soft-tissue injuries are the worst kind, and missing preseason makes it messier.

Old Man Squad: Distinguish 'risky but healthy on night one' from 'out'. He will take risky players who are available on day one (Kawhi Leonard, Joel Embiid, Anthony Davis, Kyrie Irving, maybe Zach Edey, Damian Lillard) but not players who are out to start. The four known to be hurt to start the year as of this episode: Kon Knueppel, Brandon Ingram, Kristaps Porzingis, Jimmy Butler.

Old Man Squad: 'Brunsonitis': when you expect a player to be bad at a category you stop noticing how bad. Low steals, blocks and rebounds from a scoring guard quietly sink the 9-cat rank, so do not pay a third-round price for a known profile.

Old Man Squad: Punt-build players (Giannis Antetokounmpo, LaMelo Ball, Alperen Sengun) are excluded from the bust list: they will not hit their 9-cat rank but the reason is known and you adjust the build around it.
Old Man Squad: Finals hangover: players on a team coming off a deep title run (the Knicks here) tend to show slight mental fatigue from late November or early December, plus a shorter offseason.
Locked On: Second-round players are 'relatively interchangeable' in Lloyd's view.

Locked On: After pick 50, Damian Lillard and Paul George are the two players Lloyd sees as top-30 talents; he wanted one or both in rounds 5-6 and both were taken one to two rounds earlier than usual.

Locked On: The penultimate-turn problem: at pick 11 you line up two targets and cannot control what the drafter with back-to-back picks does. The drafter one spot ahead of Lloyd took Lillard, Harper, Day'Ron Sharpe and Maluach and ended with the best projected record.
Locked On: If a player you like starts going earlier, do not chase: 'just get somebody different later', because earlier reaches push other players back.
Locked On: Late rounds: choose the player with a small chance of finishing well above his slot (Kevin Porter Jr.) over the safer player who will probably finish ahead (Anthony Black).
Locked On: Pick 119 onward is flyer territory, and many of the usual flyers now go earlier.
Locked On: Position labels can mislead: Anthony Davis and Jaren Jackson Jr. were not labelled as centers in this room, so check eligibility before deciding you need a center.
Locked On: He ended up short on rebounds and bigs after starting Maxey, Barnes, Davis and guards, and used his last two late picks on Isaiah Jackson and Jalen Smith to patch it.

Old Man Squad: Towns is a 'guard build center': points, threes, FT%, more steals than blocks, plus elite rebounding. Treat him as a guard build plus one big-man category rather than a traditional big; he fits punt blocks and does not hurt FG%.

Old Man Squad: Sabonis and Towns are 'wine pairing' players rather than single-punt players: neither forces a specific punt. Sabonis is mediocre but not ruinous at FT%, has highish turnovers, and gives about one defensive stat per game.

Old Man Squad: The 'Jarrett Allen corridor': quality big men reliably finish between 35 and 65, so centers drafted in that window are safe. Rubin's distinction is that Zubac has more ceiling than Allen within it.

Old Man Squad/Noah Rubin: Disagreement on finals hangover: Besbris says players coming off a title run tend to have a letdown the next season; Rubin calls that a narrative without statistical backing and notes the Knicks deliberately managed minutes.

Noah Rubin: Rubin says the league's new rules mean teams have little reason to bench healthy veterans late in the year, and which teams might do it cannot be predicted in preseason, so do not discount players like LaVine or Sabonis for shutdown risk.
Noah Rubin: High-variance scorers who can produce 40 points and 8 threes in a night are useful in head-to-head leagues.
Old Man Squad: Besbris says you cannot ignore the rookies this season because the top three or four names in the draft were fantasy-game ready.
Old Man Squad: Sabonis gets a bump in 8-cat relative to 9-cat because of turnovers.

Adam King: Steals are such a low-volume category that small gains swing value: Daniels going from 2.0 to 2.2 or 2.3 steals is a 10 to 15% jump, comparable to a 20-point scorer becoming a 23-point scorer.

Adam King: King's signature head-to-head build is a quadruple punt of points, threes, assists and FT%, winning FG%, rebounds, steals, blocks and turnovers. Besbris: once you have your main four or five players it is very hard for opponents to beat you in those five categories, and you can reach rounds early for fits like Ausar Thompson without hurting the team.
Adam King: A Haliburton guard build targets points, threes, assists, steals and FT%, but Haliburton only scores around 20 a game, so you have to load up on points with the next picks.
Old Man Squad: Guard builds often end up with too many assists and not enough steals; Dyson Daniels is the fix.

Old Man Squad: Chet Holmgren's low scoring makes him a hard sell in round two of head-to-head unless paired with one of the lower-scoring first-rounders; Besbris is more comfortable with him in roto. His neutral FT% is what lets him pair with FT%-driven guards.

Old Man Squad: Besbris notes that in the season Haliburton got hurt he ranked around 60th after the first four or five weeks and still finished fifth in 9-cat, so a slow start after a layoff is not disqualifying.
Adam King: King says there is not much value at the top of the draft this year; Holmgren at an early-second-round price with mid-first-round value is one of the few spots.

SportsEthos: Four rookies should be drafted in every league: Cameron Boozer, Caleb Wilson, Darryn Peterson and AJ Dybantsa (all +300 to +400 for Rookie of the Year; everyone else is +1500 or longer). Everything after that is a last-two-rounds flyer or a stash.

SportsEthos: Late-round rookie choice depends on your build and earlier risk: take Darius Acuff if you run a counting-stats build needing points, assists and threes and can absorb FG% and turnover damage; take Brayden Burries if you are balanced and want a pick you can cut without regret.
SportsEthos: Target late picks who can beat their ADP; a pick in the 140s who can only return 130th to 140th value has no excess value.

SportsEthos: Mark is not worried about tanking this year because of lottery reforms: teams will play their guys, so you can trust players on bad teams (Wizards) through the fantasy playoffs, with injured veterans the exception.
SportsEthos: Rookies and second-year players carry a wide range of outcomes; a second-year player priced at his peak (Dylan Harper at 79.2) is a fade on price even if you love the talent.
Old Man Squad: In expert drafts the really good players run out in the 80s, so everything after about pick 89 on Yahoo is flier territory.

Old Man Squad: Round-by-round late approach: in the 10th round still take a reliable top-90 type; rounds 11, 12 and 13 are for big swings (Kevin Porter Jr., Reed Sheppard, Khaman Maluach) or short-term 'burger board' plays like Grayson Allen that you expect to cut.
Old Man Squad: Using a last-round pick on a player with a two-week window of heavy usage is fine in any format; in head-to-head it gets you off to a quick start.

Old Man Squad: Per-game value versus games played: among equally graded players (Suggs versus Hart versus Keegan Murray) pick by what the roster needs. Suggs has the higher per-game value, Hart and Murray the better games-played outlook.

Old Man Squad: Among the deep one-airplane names, the ones with the best shot at top 100 early are those with reliable starting jobs on opening night (Moussa Diabate, Daniel Gafford if Lively is out, Cameron Johnson).

Old Man Squad: Tier order of the flier pool on Yahoo's fifth board: Murray-Boyles first; then Keegan Murray, Jalen Suggs, Josh Hart, Jakob Poeltl; then safe plays Wiggins, McDaniels, John Collins, Neemias Queta, Myles Turner; then choose your risk among Sheppard, DeRozan, Porter Jr., Allen, Maluach.
Hustle Sports: Rankings show where players are expected to go, not their value; championships are won by who you identify in the middle rounds, not the first round.

Hustle Sports: All seven targets (White, Kessler, Ware, Boozer, Dybantsa, Pritchard, Herro) are mid-round players; taking them anywhere in rounds five to eight is not an overspend, and several will not last to the ninth. Do not let ADP alone dictate where you take them.
Hustle Sports: T-Will generally avoids overspending on rookies unless the rookie walks into a team with no major veteran ahead of him (Boozer).
FSAN | Fantasy Basketball Advice: Caveat for a 9-cat reader: this show quotes fantasy points per game projections, so its rankings lean points-league. Category-specific claims are noted per player.
FSAN: Breakouts are judged against ADP: the goal is one to two rounds of profit per pick stacked across the roster, not finding a first-rounder in round five.
FSAN: Stop using the last pick on boring floor players (the 'Herb Jones of the world'); take breakout candidates like Cedric Coward that cost nothing and can simply be dropped if they miss.
FSAN: Few players contribute in every category; Cooper Flagg is one, which is the case for paying a first-round price.
FSAN: A guard who gives nearly 2.5 combined steals and blocks (Stephon Castle) is rare and valuable for defensive categories.
FSAN: If you skip big men early, Kel'el Ware around pick 70 to 76 is a good later-round center.
FSAN: Oso Ighodaro is power-forward eligible, so he adds big-man stats without using a center slot.

Locked On: Late flyers cover all your bench slots and can start as early as round 10, your last starter spot: 'there's no point grabbing a guy at 110 who's going to be 110th', because that value is on the waiver wire.
Locked On: Lloyd is moving toward treating round 10 as flyer territory; rounds 11-13 are all swings. In the very last round a stable 110th-ranked player at pick 150 becomes value again.
Locked On: Do not wait on upside players because their ADP is 170-200. Take Maluach in round 10, since most teams drop their round 10-13 picks anyway.
Locked On: Projection is the median, so pick by range: Demin and a Harrison Barnes or Tobias Harris type can both project 120th, but only Demin can finish 80th.
Locked On: Conditional flyers: take Fears while he might start and drop the idea if you learn he will not.
Locked On: Starting centers are scarce late in drafts. The late names Lloyd gives are Nurkic, Maluach, Missi, Isaiah Jackson, Gafford, Diabate, Poeltl, Queta, Paul Reed and Day'Ron Sharpe.
Locked On: Lloyd accepts losing week one or two: he does not draft for the week-one schedule or stream for early games, and holds flyers such as Gillespie to see how roles settle.
Locked On: Stash plays depend on format: Porzingis is close to unusable in daily-lineup leagues with short benches; Konan Niederhauser needs an IL slot.
Locked On: His dislike of a player is about price versus consensus; he drafted John Collins late when he needed a big.
Locked On: Do not weight player quotes about teammates (for example comparisons of Darryn Peterson to Kawhi or Kobe): players 'are the worst evaluators of talent'.

Locked On: 'The major part of winning fantasy is getting value picks.' Drafting someone at 80 who finishes 40th matters more than builds or pairings; the rest is in-season activity, waivers and streaming.
Locked On: The gap needed to call something value widens as you go down the board; 22 versus 20 is nothing.

Locked On: Giannis does not force a three-category punt. Punt free throws, treat turnovers as punted by default if you are collecting high-usage players, and recover threes easily. Get guard stats (assists, threes, steals) early even from good free-throw shooters, and do not just stack bad free-throw shooters.
Locked On: Turnovers 'should just be punted anyway by anyone who's paying any attention' because high-value, high-usage players make them unavoidable.
Locked On: ADP is an average, so about half of drafts take the player later than the number. When Yahoo moves a rank back (Davis to 44), ADP drifts later afterward.

Locked On: The real value band this year is picks 51-100, where Lloyd sees many players who can beat their price by 10 to 40 spots; inside the top 50 he sees only a few per-game values (Kawhi, Kyrie, Davis).
Locked On: Picks 100-120 are still starters on a 12-team roster, not flyers.
Locked On: Steals are highly variable year to year; do not pay for a three-steal season, and do not assume a down year sticks either.
Locked On: Injury-risk veterans are fine at the right price: Lloyd passes on Kawhi inside the top 40 and Embiid inside the top 50 but buys both later, plus Porzingis around 100 and Suggs around 105.
Locked On: Games-played totals need context: LaMelo's missed games were at least 40% tanking-related.
Locked On: ESPN ADPs are unreliable and its default is 10-team, 8-category; Lloyd does not play there. Sleeper does not offer category leagues.
RotoWire: There are not many intriguing centers at the end of drafts; after pick 100 Gafford and Maluach are about as good as the center options get.
RotoWire: Centers who average a double-double, hit threes, block shots and shoot a high FG% (the Kel'el Ware profile) always look great in category leagues.
League Winner Sports: ADP mixes points and categories drafts, so it is not a categories price. Compare a 9-cat ranking against ADP one platform at a time.

League Winner Sports: ESPN standard categories is 8-cat with no turnovers while Yahoo is 9-cat, so high-turnover players (Dejounte Murray at 3.6, Jalen Suggs at 2.7) are worth less on Yahoo than on ESPN.
League Winner Sports: Biggest Yahoo value gaps versus their consensus: Ty Jerome (83rd vs ADP 115) and Neemias Queta (90th vs ADP 117). Yahoo also undervalues Jaren Jackson Jr. (29th vs ADP 49).

NBA Fantasy Bible: Yahoo ADP blends 9-cat, 8-cat and Yahoo high-score (points) drafts, so 9-cat specialists (Ty Jerome 115, John Collins 116, Dejounte Murray 68.9, Zach Edey 76) fall further on Yahoo than on Fantrax.
NBA Fantasy Bible: You do not have to smash every pick; gaining one or two rounds of value on a few picks goes a long way to winning the league.

RotoWire/NBA Fantasy Bible: 'Popcorn stats' players (high points, highlights) such as Paolo Banchero and Jalen Brunson are overdrafted in 9-cat; players whose value comes from stocks and efficiency (Derrick White, OG Anunoby) slip relative to real value.
RotoWire/NBA Fantasy Bible: Drafting safe players early is what lets you take upside swings like Zach Edey later; if you took risk early, gravitate to White and Anunoby types.
NBA Fantasy Bible: Punt blocks is a very viable build this year because players like Victor Wembanyama prop up the category for whoever has them; DMac is considering going hard at it.
NBA Fantasy Bible: DMac does not like punting from the first pick; Giannis is elite but forces a multi-punt build, which he finds undesirable.
RotoWire: Center cliff: if you pass on Zach Edey in round 7 or 8, the remaining centers are much riskier, with Jusuf Nurkic the best left.
Hustle Sports: Do not draft off last year's situations: usage and roles changed for about a dozen players off single moves (LeBron to Philadelphia, Giannis to Miami, LaMelo Ball to Minnesota).

Hustle Sports: For rookies in redraft, weigh opportunity over hype: minutes, starting role and how they get their looks in preseason matter more than box scores. Boozer and Wilson have the roles; Dybantsa and Peterson are the talent-versus-crowded-roster risks. Ace Bailey started slowly last year and was a hold by the All-Star break, so timing matters.
Hustle Sports: Never overspend on anybody; T-Will wants one of the main players from Miami and from Minnesota at a fair price.
RotoWire: All of these center targets go around or after pick 100 (Sharpe 101, Claxton 99, Queen about 92, Maluach about 100, Nurkic 120), so a two-center roster can wait on its second center.
RotoWire: There are not many viable centers left by pick 120 who still give high-volume rebounds and assists; Nurkic is the pick there, and he jumps to about top 55 in a punt-FT% build.
RotoWire: Price sets the floor: at pick 100 a per-minute big like Sharpe or Queen only burns you if he plays about 20 minutes.
RotoWire: Edey's injury risk is baked into an ADP around 70, so he will not make or break your season (Whalen is more nervous than Alex).

The Roster Report: 'Beast mode' build (Keller): focus on FG%, rebounds, blocks, steals and low turnovers, and punt the rest. In H2H each-category leagues a 5-4 win counts the same as 9-0, so locking five categories every week is the goal.

The Roster Report: Three rules: (1) playing time and availability first, (2) know your format because points and category leagues value players differently (a player with 8 points, 5 rebounds, 5 assists and 3 turnovers is decent in categories and atrocious in points), (3) go in with a plan.
The Roster Report: Keep a do-not-draft list as well as a target list; knowing who you are avoiding matters more when your targets get sniped and stops panic picks.
The Roster Report: Keep a watch list of late-round players (Grayson Allen type) to put at the top of your waiver list if they produce early.
The Roster Report: Adam Waldo's projections are tuned for points leagues (fantasy points per minute); that metric does not help in 9-cat.

NBA Fantasy Bible: D-Mac's 9-cat top 50 (ranked for end-of-season finish, not draft slot): 1 Wembanyama, 2 Jokic, 3 Gilgeous-Alexander, 4 Doncic, 5 Cunningham, 6 Tatum, 7 Antetokounmpo, 8 Edwards, 9 Maxey, 10 Flagg, 11 Mitchell, 12 Barnes, 13 Jalen Johnson, 14 Durant, 15 Jamal Murray, 16 Reaves, 17 Haliburton, 18 Towns, 19 Curry, 20 Trae Young, 21 Harden, 22 Holmgren, 23 LaMelo Ball, 24 Giddey, 25 Mobley, 26 Amen Thompson, 27 Markkanen, 28 Anthony Davis, 29 Trey Murphy, 30 Sengun, 31 Kawhi Leonard, 32 Brandon Miller, 33 Derrick White, 34 Booker, 35 Jalen Williams, 36 Adebayo, 37 Kessler, 38 Jaren Jackson Jr., 39 Brunson, 40 Sabonis, 41 Duren, 42 Bane, 43 Kyrie Irving, 44 Garland, 45 Dejounte Murray, 46 Clingan, 47 Buzelis, 48 Ware, 49 Franz Wagner, 50 Okongwu.
NBA Fantasy Bible: D-Mac ignores turnovers and treats 9-cat as 8-cat, effectively punting TO. That is why he ranks Cade Cunningham 5 despite the turnovers.

NBA Fantasy Bible: Get assists early: 'You've got to get your assists early' on statistical and positional scarcity grounds, which is why Trae Young (20) and James Harden (21) sit in his second round.
NBA Fantasy Bible/League Winner Sports: Do not commit to a punt at pick one; D-Mac starts leaning into a punt around rounds 3 to 4 and prefers balance before that. Matt also prefers balanced builds.

NBA Fantasy Bible: In head-to-head, fade injury-prone stars more than in roto, because a fast start matters and you cannot bank games; in roto with a games cap they can be plugged back in. D-Mac says he is deliberately avoiding the more injury-prone players this year (Haliburton 17, Davis 28, Leonard 31, Irving 43).

NBA Fantasy Bible/League Winner Sports: Wembanyama vs Jokic at 1: D-Mac takes Wembanyama for upside and League Winner's per-game 9-cat projections have him ahead, but Jokic is the safest pick in any format. Risk on Wembanyama: the Spurs sit him when they blow teams out. Pick two is a great spot because you get whoever is left.
NBA Fantasy Bible/League Winner Sports: Gilgeous-Alexander over Doncic at 3 in 9-cat on volume plus efficiency, with nearly two steals and a block per game from a guard.

NBA Fantasy Bible: Rank is not draft slot: check ADP for your platform and do not pay a player's ceiling if he is likely to come back to you at your next pick. Fantrax ADP is the sharpest; ESPN and Yahoo are softer.
NBA Fantasy Bible: Picks 5 to 12 are close enough that you can argue any order; variation between rankers grows the later you go.
NBA Fantasy Bible: Do not rank purely off last year's 9-cat finish; ask what a player gives that others cannot and whether he fits the build (the Sengun case).
NBA Fantasy Bible: Efficient high-volume scoring is hard to find later in drafts, which is D-Mac's reason for holding Jalen Brunson at 39.

NBA Fantasy Bible: Kyrie Irving, Darius Garland and Dejounte Murray are ranked 43, 44, 45 with almost nothing between them: Irving has the highest per-game upside (second round, possibly first) but the games-played risk.

SportsEthos: The whole episode compares current ADP to last season's 8-category per-game rank (turnovers excluded). Published site ADPs (ESPN, Yahoo) are 'all over the place', so SportsEthos uses its own ADP tool built from competitive drafts.
SportsEthos: Dr. A would almost prefer the 12th pick if he cannot get first overall for Wembanyama: the turn should offer players like Cooper Flagg, LaMelo Ball and possibly Trae Young.
SportsEthos: Premium picks at the turn carry thin profit margins even when they hit.
SportsEthos: Dr. A does not weigh FT% or turnovers much when drafting head-to-head.
SportsEthos: Dr. A generally will not draft a big who does not block shots, hit threes or get steals (Sabonis, Banchero).
SportsEthos: Centres: by rounds six to eight only a certain number are left, so make sure you get one or two of them in that window; Rudy Gobert qualifies.

SportsEthos: Players who hurt you in two or three categories (Giannis) cannot be ranked high just because they are good in six; you can build a strategy around them but it is limiting. Exotic punt builds have won high-stakes roto, but Bruski does not think Giannis is the player to do it with.
SportsEthos: Fourth-round picks tend to be boom-or-bust; Jalen Williams has a better floor than most in that range.

Locked On: Lloyd's first-round order for 9-cat H2H: Jokic 1, Wembanyama 2, then Doncic and Gilgeous-Alexander in either order, Giannis 5, Tatum 6. He is lower than consensus on Cade Cunningham but says taking Cade anywhere from 5 to 8 is neither league-winning nor league-losing.
Locked On: Picks 8 through 12 are 'a rough sort of spot': Cooper Flagg, Anthony Edwards, Durant, Maxey, Haliburton, Jalen Johnson. He would take Kevin Durant and Maxey ahead of Jalen Johnson.

Locked On: Perfect builds do not exist and Lloyd hates over-reliance on pairings. Example: you do not need to pair a bad free-throw shooter like Sengun with Giannis; Sengun gives assists but does not help threes or steals.
Locked On: Do not stack injury-risk veterans. After taking Anthony Davis he refused to add Paul George, Embiid or LeBron: 'I don't want to combine those players with Anthony Davis.'

Locked On: With two centers already (Jokic, Davis) he did not push for more centers through the middle rounds, then took Jarrett Allen at about 85 as 'another center option'. He chose Allen over Gobert because his free throws were 'a little precarious' and Allen's are bad but not as bad as Gobert's.
Locked On: Round 8 (picks 85-96) is not flyer territory; round 10 onward is, especially at the turn, because by your next pick most people will have taken their flyers.
Locked On: Red injury flags on Fantrax in preseason should not scare you off players like Brandon Miller.
Locked On: A backup's value does not pass down a chain: Raynaud was only a play as Sabonis's backup, so his injury does not make Dylan Cardwell or the next man worth drafting.
Locked On: Late-round picks are about short-term chances you will not hold all season (example: Jackson Hayes as a possible opening-night starter for blocks and field goal percentage).
Locked On: Lloyd pushed up Cameron Boozer, Ty Jerome and Dylan Harper on preseason evidence.
Locked On: His round-9 need check on the Jokic team: 'my threes are bad', and he looked for an assist source late (considered Jeremiah Fears, took Zach LaVine and Egor Demin).
Locked On: Players who normally fall (Hartenstein, CJ McCollum, Pritchard, Suggs, Norman Powell) did not fall in this room; if a target goes early, take someone else later rather than chasing.

Old Man Squad: Suggested round map to land all six breakouts on one roster: Dejounte Murray in the fifth, Kel'el Ware in the sixth, Ausar Thompson in the seventh, then two or three of Ty Jerome, Collin Murray-Boyles and Keegan Murray in rounds nine to eleven. With an early ninth-round pick take Jerome first; Keegan Murray has slid to the eleventh before.

Old Man Squad: After the start of the ninth round on Yahoo's board there are few players Besbris likes other than his three breakouts ranked 111 to 116, so plan those picks rather than hoping for value.

Old Man Squad: Extremely low turnovers inflate 9-cat rank more than they should: Ware's 0.8 turnovers and Keegan Murray's low turnovers pushed both to 59th. At 1.3 turnovers Ware's rank would have been much lower.

Old Man Squad: More minutes mainly add rebounds and defensive stats; points, assists and threes follow usage rate, which tends to dip as minutes rise. So high-usage bench scorers like Ty Jerome have a flat value curve across minutes.
Old Man Squad: Players usually need to score to climb far up the board; Ausar Thompson may stay at 9 to 10 points, which is why his breakout is strongest in punt points, punt threes or punt FT%.

Old Man Squad: Recovery-time ranking of players who suffered major leg injuries in 2024-25: Dejounte Murray and Kyrie Irving have had the longest recoveries, then Jayson Tatum and Damian Lillard, with Tyrese Haliburton the shortest. Besbris argues it is inconsistent to trust Tatum and Haliburton but fear Murray.
Old Man Squad: Players in the 100 to 120 range are tightly bunched, so a jump from the 10th round to the seventh or eighth is smaller in real value than it sounds.
RotoWire: Tanking is expected to be far less widespread this season, so you can no longer blanket-fade whole rosters like Utah or Brooklyn.
RotoWire: ADP composites blend points leagues and category leagues, so do not treat them as gospel for 9-cat.

RotoWire: The big-name injury risks (Embiid, Kawhi Leonard, Anthony Davis) are worse bets than in past years because they are in their mid 30s AND their team situations got worse, while the draft-day discount has shrunk.
RotoWire: Embiid-type risk is tolerable in daily-lineup or best-ball formats and a non-starter in weekly-lineup leagues.
RotoWire: In rounds 7 to 9 take players with upside (Dylan Harper, Derrick White named) over cemented-role, no-upside wings like Mikal Bridges and Jabari Smith Jr.

Injury watch: Anthony Davis (WAS). 9 creators (Locked On, Hustle Sports, Steve St-Pierre, Old Man Squad, FSAN, RotoWire, NBA Fantasy Bible, Adam King, SportsEthos). Locked On: 'Has been looking pretty good so far' in preseason. Hustle Sports: Described as typically not healthy; T-Will also raises the possibility he gets traded. Steve St-Pierre: Long injury history; so far so good, playing in preseason and looking good. Taken in the third round as a dice roll. Old Man Squad: Listed among risky players who are healthy enough to play on opening night. FSAN: Joiner does not expect him to play more than half the games: 'he gets hurt every year'. RotoWire: Has played more than 56 games only twice since 2017-18; turns 34 in March. NBA Fantasy Bible: 'Day-to-day Davis': D-Mac wants to see 60-plus games. Davis has said he wants to play all 82, which D-Mac says will not happen. Adam King: Higher risk than Kessler because of sustained injuries; going around pick 25. SportsEthos: Mark does not expect him to play enough to dent AJ Dybantsa's usage. Dr. A's counter: if Davis somehow plays 72 to 78 games he wins people leagues, though Dr. A is not going in on him.

Injury watch: Stephen Curry (GSW). 9 creators (RotoWire, NBA Fantasy Bible, Steve St-Pierre, Fantasy on Points, Locked On, Old Man Squad, Number Two Sports, League Winner Sports, Adam King). RotoWire: Alex does not trust Curry, Draymond Green or Kristaps Porzingis to stay healthy; Moses Moody is not starting the year healthy either. NBA Fantasy Bible, Steve St-Pierre, Fantasy on Points: Falling in drafts; not at 100% in preseason. Steve calls him a dice roll on how long he stays healthy, and Leo does not think he plays 70-plus games. Locked On: A Curry absence would raise Podziemski's value. Old Man Squad: Healthy now, per Besbris. Number Two Sports: Age and injury history flagged. League Winner Sports: Concerns about his knees and age; signed a two-year extension, which cools trade rumours. Adam King: Injury concerns centered on his knee and age.

Injury watch: Zach Edey (MEM). 9 creators (RotoWire, NBA Fantasy Bible, Fantasy on Points, Noah Rubin, The Roster Report, Locked On, League Winner Sports, Old Man Squad, Adam King). RotoWire: Host is hedging his health with Isaiah Stewart and imagines a 20-game absence at some point; Alex is far more bullish on Edey. NBA Fantasy Bible, Fantasy on Points: Value depends entirely on staying healthy; 60-plus games would make him a potential league winner. Noah Rubin: Named with Ty Jerome as the Grizzlies' two biggest stay-healthy question marks. The Roster Report: Referred to as healthy in the Memphis lineup. Locked On: Barely played last season with a foot/ankle problem as a big man; healthy through college and 66 games as a rookie. League Winner Sports: Played only 11 games last season; projected for 57 games; ankle reported on track for opening night. Old Man Squad: 'Maybe' healthy for day one. Started last season hurt and had a bad fantasy year. Adam King: King loves him but calls Gobert the safer option because of Edey's injuries.

Injury watch: Kawhi Leonard (TOR). 8 creators (Locked On, Number Two Sports, Old Man Squad, RotoWire, NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports, Adam King, SportsEthos). Locked On: Risk player Lloyd will not take inside the top 40. Number Two Sports: Described as one of the most injury-prone players in the league. Old Man Squad: Listed among risky players who are good to go on day one, which makes them draftable under Besbris's rule. RotoWire: Whalen projects 55 to 60 games; 60 would be a win. NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports: D-Mac does not trust his body; James expects Toronto to load-manage him as in 2019 (60 games). Adam King: Called injury prone; King would rather pair first-rounders with players who will play more games. SportsEthos: Dr. A raises the risk of him missing time as in past seasons.

Injury watch: Kristaps Porzingis (GSW). 7 creators (Locked On, Steve St-Pierre, Fantasy on Points, Old Man Squad, Number Two Sports, Adam King, SportsEthos). Locked On: Availability unknown; Lloyd asks whether he will ever appear. Steve St-Pierre, Fantasy on Points: Leo does not expect him back anytime soon; Steve considered him as a last-round stash. Old Man Squad: Referred to as 'cooked'; the Warriors are treating Al Horford as the center. Number Two Sports: Chris is unsure when or whether he is coming back and expects him to miss a massive chunk of games regardless. Adam King: King would be happy with 60 games. SportsEthos: Health is an unknown.

Injury watch: Jalen Suggs (ORL). 7 creators (RotoWire, Old Man Squad, League Winner Sports, FSAN, Locked On, Adam King, Number Two Sports). RotoWire: Expected to miss a ton of time 'as he does every year'. Old Man Squad: Described as 'relatively hurt' as a general profile; Besbris docked him one airplane for games-played risk. League Winner Sports: Played 57 games last season; projected 58. FSAN: Long injury history; seems to miss two to three months every year. Locked On: Injured 'all the time'; Lloyd calls another absence a pretty likely outcome. Adam King: King expects 50 to 55 games because of a reckless playing style that invites injury. Number Two Sports: Has played more than 58 games only once in his career.

Injury watch: Ty Jerome (MEM). 7 creators (Noah Rubin, Locked On, NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports, RotoWire, Number Two Sports, FSAN). Noah Rubin: Health question mark alongside Edey. Locked On: History of injuries that is 'a little concerning'. NBA Fantasy Bible: Only 15 games played last season; has had a healthy preseason. League Winner Sports: Played only 15 games last season; games are the risk, projected 60. RotoWire: Played only 15 games last season; injury history is 'not that great'. Number Two Sports: Played only 15 games last season before getting injured and has dealt with injuries across his last 85 games; the pick is 'health permitting'. FSAN: Described as healthy now; Scotty Pippen Jr. was also out a lot last year.

Injury watch: Tyrese Haliburton (IND). 6 creators (Locked On, Old Man Squad, Noah Rubin, RotoWire, NBA Fantasy Bible, Adam King). Locked On: Missed a preseason game with an ankle injury; Lloyd is not worried about the ankle itself but flags compensation injuries coming back from a torn Achilles. Old Man Squad: Coming back from the Achilles injury; no more risky than Tatum in Dan's view. The Pacers are awful without him. Noah Rubin: Missed last season (the Pacers were 'a disaster without' him); referenced as back and playing with Zubac. RotoWire: Returning from a torn Achilles after missing all of last season. Recovery included setbacks, shingles and weight issues; expect rust, restricted minutes early and possibly sitting back-to-backs. NBA Fantasy Bible: Coming off an Achilles injury and has not played in over a year. Reported fully healthy, but D-Mac expects a slow ramp, managed minutes and rest on some of Indiana's 15 back-to-backs, with a strong finish. Adam King: Coming back after a full 12 months off. King's only risk flags are rest, managed minutes and back-to-backs, mainly in the first month.

Injury watch: Coby White (CHA). 6 creators (RotoWire, NBA Fantasy Bible, The Roster Report, Locked On, Old Man Squad, Number Two Sports). RotoWire: Has a calf injury. NBA Fantasy Bible: Injured at the start of the season. The Roster Report: Injury is more serious than Knueppel's and will definitely linger into the beginning of the season. Locked On: Fourth calf strain in the last 12 months; Lloyd drops him outside the top 90. Old Man Squad: Out; Besbris says he will 'maybe come back at some point'. Number Two Sports: Appeared in a career-low 50 games last season. No current injury mentioned in this video.

Injury watch: Jakob Poeltl (TOR). 6 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, Noah Rubin, Locked On, Old Man Squad, Number Two Sports, SportsEthos). NBA Fantasy Bible: Looking somewhat healthy and solid in preseason. Noah Rubin: Was hurt for most of last year; Rubin hopes he is healthier, and his form affects Murray-Boyles' minutes. Locked On: Back 'is okay for now' and he looks significantly better than last season. Old Man Squad: Looks healthy. Number Two Sports: 'Always battling injuries'; was hurt last season, which opened minutes for Murray-Boyles. SportsEthos: Mark allows that he may be 'a little bit in and out of the lineup'.

Injury watch: Jimmy Butler III (GSW). 6 creators (RotoWire, Steve St-Pierre, Old Man Squad, Number Two Sports, Adam King, SportsEthos). RotoWire: Out. Steve St-Pierre: Out; taken with the last pick as an IL stash in the hope he returns late in the season. Old Man Squad: Hurt, as he was at the end of last season. Number Two Sports: Still working his way back from the major injury he suffered last season. Adam King: Unknown return date ('when does he get back'). SportsEthos: Assumed out until at least 2027; not a factor in the first half of the season.

Injury watch: Mark Williams (PHX). 6 creators (RotoWire, NBA Fantasy Bible, Old Man Squad, FSAN, Number Two Sports, SportsEthos). RotoWire: Injured; Maluach's draft cost has jumped since. NBA Fantasy Bible: Out for a while; may come back later in the season. Old Man Squad: Out for maybe the whole year. FSAN: Out for probably more than half the season after shoulder surgery; Joiner says he will never play consistently. Number Two Sports: Expected to miss several months following shoulder surgery. SportsEthos: Lost for much of the season; Mark says out until at least January or February.

Injury watch: Dejounte Murray (NOP). 6 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports, Number Two Sports, Old Man Squad, SportsEthos, Locked On). NBA Fantasy Bible: Has not been fully healthy over the last few seasons. League Winner Sports: Played only 14 games last season; projected 66. Number Two Sports: Returned last season from a lengthy absence and major injury and looked good with some rust; has now had a full normal offseason for the first time in two years. Old Man Squad: Suffered a catastrophic leg injury 30 games into 2024-25; returned for 14 games at 28 minutes late last season and looked good. Nearly two full years of recovery by opening night; Besbris is not worried. SportsEthos: Was banged up last season, which gave Jeremiah Fears minutes. Locked On: Returned from a torn Achilles last season on limited minutes; Lloyd is not overly concerned and does not expect him to sit back-to-backs.

Injury watch: Dereck Lively II (DAL). 6 creators (Old Man Squad, FSAN, Locked On, RotoWire, League Winner Sports, SportsEthos). Old Man Squad: Possibly out to start the year ('if Dereck Lively is out'), which would lift Daniel Gafford. FSAN: Told Mavericks media he is on the right track and looks in shape; Joiner hopes he starts the season but says 'we'll see'. (RotoWire videos are far more negative on his status.) Locked On: Not healthy. RotoWire: No clue when he will play again; a lot of terrible reports about his recovery from multiple lower-body injuries. League Winner Sports: James says 'hopefully being healthy'. SportsEthos: 'Maybe there, maybe not': reports on his timeline are murky, and Dr. A calls him always banged up.

Injury watch: Kyrie Irving (DAL). 6 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, Steve St-Pierre, Locked On, Old Man Squad, Adam King, RotoWire). NBA Fantasy Bible, Steve St-Pierre: Back after a long time away; scored 14 points in limited preseason minutes and looked smooth. Per-game value is there at pick 46, the question is total games played. Locked On: Made his preseason debut in Macau and looked pretty good. Old Man Squad: Listed among risky players healthy for opening night; the Mavs held him out last season even though he could have returned in March. Adam King, RotoWire: Has been out for a long stretch; Alex still targets him in round 4 to 5.

Injury watch: Joel Embiid (PHI). 6 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, Steve St-Pierre, Hustle Sports, Old Man Squad, RotoWire, Locked On). NBA Fantasy Bible, Steve St-Pierre: Knees 'looked a little bit cooked' in a recent preseason game. Steve is concerned and took him only as a seventh-round upside pick in a mock. Hustle Sports: Value conditional on 'if he could play more'. Old Man Squad: Apparently healthy enough to play on opening night, but Besbris puts his odds of playing a given game two months out (Christmas) at 50/50. RotoWire: Dropped weight and is focused on playing more games, but the Sixers are already talking about managing him. Locked On: 'Embiid will miss some games.'

Injury watch: Kon Knueppel (CHA). 5 creators (RotoWire, NBA Fantasy Bible, The Roster Report, Locked On, Old Man Squad). RotoWire: Also hurt, opening minutes in Charlotte. NBA Fantasy Bible: Hamstring soft-tissue injury; likely to start the regular season injured and miss games. The Roster Report: Hamstring injury likely to linger into the start of the season; not overly serious but expect reduced early production. Locked On: Injured; may not miss time to start the season, but Lloyd says he 'probably' does not begin the season healthy. Went 68, which Lloyd called about right. Old Man Squad: Out probably through the beginning of the season.

Injury watch: Jayson Tatum (BOS). 5 creators (Old Man Squad, NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports, Adam King, Locked On). Old Man Squad: Tatum versus Edwards comes down to games played, roughly 69 versus 72 either way. His steals were good in last year's small sample. NBA Fantasy Bible, League Winner Sports: Returned from his Achilles injury at the back end of last season and is considered healthy; maintenance days expected. Matt calls the quick return an abnormality in a small sample. Adam King: Described as generally pretty healthy. Locked On: Cited as a player who already returned from an Achilles tear and was nowhere near as bad as Lillard's price implies.

Injury watch: Paul George (BOS). 5 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, Locked On, Old Man Squad, Adam King, Number Two Sports). NBA Fantasy Bible: Missed games last season partly due to a suspension; maintenance games expected. Locked On: 'He will probably miss time.' Old Man Squad: A risk; Dan's favorite seventh-rounder anyway. Do not stack with too many other risks. Adam King: King expects 50 to 60 games. Number Two Sports: Has played more than 56 games only once in the past seven seasons; described as 'coming back'.

Injury watch: Walker Kessler (LAL). 5 creators (Hustle Sports, NBA Fantasy Bible, Locked On, FSAN, Adam King). Hustle Sports: Injury history is the only concern; the recommendation assumes he is healthy. NBA Fantasy Bible: Comes into the season with a clean bill of health after a five-game season; has not been healthy in past seasons. Locked On: Played only five games last season; Lloyd is not worried about the injury itself. FSAN: Played only five games last year but had been relatively healthy before that. Adam King: Comes with some risk at pick 25.

Injury watch: Brandon Ingram (LAC). 4 creators (Locked On, NBA Fantasy Bible, Old Man Squad, Number Two Sports). Locked On: Coming off the Achilles; Lloyd will not draft him inside the top 120. NBA Fantasy Bible: Injured to start the season. Old Man Squad: Out for an unknown length of time. Number Two Sports: Dealing with an injury; Chris does not know how much time he will miss.

Injury watch: Keegan Murray (SAC). 4 creators (League Winner Sports, Number Two Sports, Old Man Squad, Locked On). League Winner Sports: Played only 23 games last season; Kings GM said he is healthy entering camp. Number Two Sports: Missed a lot of time with injuries last season. Old Man Squad: Was out for most of last season. Locked On: Injured a lot last season.

Injury watch: Isaiah Hartenstein (OKC). 4 creators (RotoWire, Locked On, Old Man Squad, League Winner Sports). RotoWire: Has struggled to stay healthy. Locked On: Injured a lot last season. Old Man Squad: Did not play in the Thunder preseason game referenced; framed as OKC not playing its centers in preseason. League Winner Sports: Played 47 games last season; projected 67.

Injury watch: Brandon Miller (CHA). 4 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, FSAN, League Winner Sports, Locked On). NBA Fantasy Bible: Missed a preseason game with a shin contusion (minor). Had shoulder surgery in May, reported healed. Played only 30 minutes a game last year while dealing with injuries. FSAN: Clark notes he has really only missed significant time in one season, with 60-plus games in the other two. League Winner Sports: Lingering shoulder injury that was on and off late last season; James says the Hornets have been opaque about it. Locked On: Lloyd is 'somewhat concerned about the shoulder problem' and is waiting on a camp update (as of Sept 17).

Injury watch: Darius Garland (LAC). 4 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, Number Two Sports, Noah Rubin, Locked On). NBA Fantasy Bible: Started last season injured; a struggling Clippers team may rest him toward the back end of the season. Number Two Sports: Battled injuries last season and may carry an injury-prone label; value depends on staying healthy. Noah Rubin: Had a toe issue across multiple seasons; Rubin says he is fully healthy now. Locked On: 'Not always particularly robust.'

Injury watch: Domantas Sabonis (SAC). 4 creators (Noah Rubin, Number Two Sports, Locked On, SportsEthos). Noah Rubin: Played 19 games last season with a knee injury on a tanking Kings team. Described as healthy now; Besbris does not see injury as the concern. Number Two Sports: Described as back and healthy. Locked On: Injured last season; Lloyd does not project a repeat. SportsEthos: Bruski thinks the knee issues are probably okay and that he arrives in great shape.

Injury watch: LaMelo Ball (MIN). 3 creators (Locked On, Old Man Squad, NBA Fantasy Bible). Locked On: Lloyd is not particularly concerned about the ankles; he estimates half the time missed was for tanking. Old Man Squad: Dan does not trust him to stay healthy all season, which is why he is drafting him almost nowhere. NBA Fantasy Bible: Was relatively healthy last season; staying healthy is the only proviso on his value.

Injury watch: Alex Sarr (WAS). 3 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, Locked On, Number Two Sports). NBA Fantasy Bible: Has not been known for staying on the court. Locked On: Back playing after the broken foot. Number Two Sports: Missed time with injury last season.

Injury watch: Max Strus (LAC). 3 creators (RotoWire, NBA Fantasy Bible, Old Man Squad). RotoWire: Dealing with an injury of unknown severity. NBA Fantasy Bible: Also injured. Old Man Squad: Out to start the year.

Injury watch: Trae Young (WAS). 3 creators (Hustle Sports, Adam King, Old Man Squad). Hustle Sports: Mentioned as having an injury history alongside Davis. Adam King: A fairly safe option 'injuries aside'. Old Man Squad: Did not play last year, which sank Trae-plus-Harden teams.

Injury watch: Fred VanVleet (HOU). 3 creators (Locked On, Adam King, Number Two Sports). Locked On: Played his first preseason game; will have days off and limited minutes at times. Adam King: Missed last season; back this year. Number Two Sports: Missed last season with an injury; healthy and back.

Injury watch: Giannis Antetokounmpo (MIA). 3 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, Number Two Sports, SportsEthos). NBA Fantasy Bible: D-Mac has no big health concerns: 'the knees aren't completely cooked'. Number Two Sports: Missed a lot of time last season, which is what opened usage for Kevin Porter Jr. in Milwaukee. SportsEthos: Knee is a stated concern and injuries dragged down last season's value.

Injury watch: Jalen Williams (OKC). 3 creators (Noah Rubin, RotoWire, SportsEthos). Noah Rubin: Wrist injury cost him last offseason, camp and the start of the season; then a hamstring injury, then the other hamstring in the playoffs. Had a full offseason to recover and Sam Presti indicated he looks good. RotoWire: Described as back for the Thunder. SportsEthos: Coming off a major wrist injury that wrecked last season; Bruski is worried about lasting effects on his shooting touch and wants camp and preseason confirmation.

Injury watch: Kevin Durant (HOU). 3 creators (Locked On, Old Man Squad, Adam King). Locked On: Age and health are a mild worry; the Rockets claim a dramatic minutes cut that Lloyd does not believe. Old Man Squad: Played 78 of 82 last year; age is the only worry. Adam King: Surprisingly durable over the last few years.

Injury watch: LeBron James (PHI). 3 creators (Steve St-Pierre, Hustle Sports, RotoWire). Steve St-Pierre: Expected to be in and out of the lineup. Hustle Sports: No injury cited, but age is the flag: year 24, turns 42 in December. RotoWire: Likely to be held out of back-to-backs.

Injury watch: Mikel Brown Jr. (BKN). 3 creators (RotoWire, Noah Rubin, Locked On). RotoWire: Dealing with an ankle injury and has not played in preseason. Noah Rubin: Had not appeared in preseason yet. Locked On: Has not appeared yet; Lloyd suspects he will not be ready to start the season.
Injury watch: Shaedon Sharpe (POR). 2 creators (Locked On, Old Man Squad). Locked On: Out for most of the year; do not draft. Old Man Squad: Out basically for the year; might return at the very end.

Injury watch: Damian Lillard (POR). 2 creators (Old Man Squad, Locked On). Old Man Squad: Listed among players apparently good enough to play on day one. Locked On: Coming back from a torn Achilles at an advanced age; expect a slow ramp in minutes.

Injury watch: Ja Morant (POR). 2 creators (Old Man Squad, NBA Fantasy Bible). Old Man Squad: 'Always hurt'; part of why Besbris will not rank him higher. NBA Fantasy Bible: Played only a handful of games last season; unknown how healthy or committed he and Damian Lillard will be.

Injury watch: Jalen Duren (DET). 2 creators (Locked On, RotoWire). Locked On: Has not played in preseason yet. RotoWire: Not an injury: was holding out over his contract as of Oct 2. (A later RotoWire video, hCZaaWed2EI, refers to a Duren extension being done.)

Injury watch: Jusuf Nurkic (UTA). 2 creators (RotoWire, Locked On). RotoWire: Will miss time to begin the year. Locked On: Not healthy; no idea how long he is out or whether he returns on reduced minutes.

Injury watch: Luka Doncic (LAL). 2 creators (RotoWire, Old Man Squad). RotoWire: Expected to miss games, which boosts Grimes and Sexton. Old Man Squad: Besbris puts the chance he plays on Christmas Day at about 75% as an illustration of game-to-game uncertainty; no specific injury stated.

Injury watch: Tyrese Maxey (PHI). 2 creators (Locked On, Old Man Squad). Locked On: 'He's had some injuries at times', one of several reasons Lloyd is lower on him. Old Man Squad: Okay shot to make it through the year. Has been dinged up and Nick Nurse overplays him (38 minutes a game, 40 early last season).

Injury watch: Austin Reaves (LAL). 2 creators (RotoWire, NBA Fantasy Bible). RotoWire: Does not have the greatest health track record, though not a disaster. NBA Fantasy Bible: Played only 51 games last season.
Injury watch: Cameron Johnson (DEN). 2 creators (RotoWire, Locked On). RotoWire: Expect about 55 games played. Locked On: Injuries plagued him last season.

Injury watch: De'Aaron Fox (SAS). 2 creators (FSAN, SportsEthos). FSAN: Went down with an injury last season, which is how Castle took over at point guard. SportsEthos: Mark says he was probably injured through most of last season's playoffs and trying to gut it out.

Injury watch: Franz Wagner (ORL). 2 creators (League Winner Sports, SportsEthos). League Winner Sports: Matt believes he is healthy; value depends on that holding. SportsEthos: Seriously hurt his ankle playing for Germany, which ruined last season; Bruski expects Orlando to wrap him in bubble wrap and prioritise health.

Injury watch: Jalen Johnson (ATL). 2 creators (RotoWire, Old Man Squad). RotoWire: Has some health concerns, offered as one reason he slid. Old Man Squad: 72 games last year but banged up in his first seasons as a starter; Dan has not seen him look supremely healthy.

Injury watch: Maxime Raynaud (SAC). 2 creators (NBA Fantasy Bible, Locked On). NBA Fantasy Bible: Said on air to look like a long-term injury; an on-screen update after filming says it is not as serious as first thought but he will still miss the start of the regular season. Locked On: Patella subluxation (kneecap slipped out), better than the torn ACL Lloyd feared. Team says at least two weeks; Lloyd guesses three to four.
Injury watch: Nic Claxton (CHI). 2 creators (Locked On, Old Man Squad). Locked On: Injured hamstring; probably does not begin the season healthy. Old Man Squad: On the injured list; do not draft.

Injury watch: Tyler Herro (MIL). 2 creators (RotoWire, Hustle Sports). RotoWire: Health doubts raised: if you do not believe in his health, you should like Brayden Burries more. Hustle Sports: Injuries 'always been his thing'.
Injury watch: Zach LaVine (SAC). 2 creators (Noah Rubin, Number Two Sports). Noah Rubin: Described as healthy this year. Number Two Sports: Battled injuries last season.

Injury watch: Zion Williamson (NOP). 2 creators (Number Two Sports, SportsEthos). Number Two Sports: Pelicans outlook is framed as conditional on Zion being healthy. SportsEthos: Played just enough games last season to qualify for his bonus and was in relatively good shape.
Injury watch: Lauri Markkanen (UTA). 2 creators (Adam King, RotoWire). Adam King, RotoWire: Legitimate injury history on top of tanking-related absences; tends to land at 59 to 63 games.

pairings.build: What following ESPN's category ranks produces (a warning, not a recommendation)
pairings.why: Locked On: Round 1 Adebayo, round 2 Ty Jerome, round 3 Mikal Bridges off ESPN's list: 'Get ready to learn toilet bowl, buddy.'

pairings.build: Guard build tilt (punt FG% and TO), keep FT% strong
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: You want scoring and assists from the second pick because Wemby gives an absurd blocks edge and beats other guard teams in rebounds and blocks. Later bigs should be rebound or block focused. Partners: Trae Young (round 2 (pick 24)): Ideal if he falls, but now ranked 19 so probably gone; LaMelo Ball (round 2): Backup that becomes the first plan; expects 7 to 8.5 assists; punt TO and FG% guard; James Harden (round 2): Interchangeable with LaMelo; Dan prefers him for the less-bad FG%; Devin Booker (round 2): Playable but not optimal; low steals, not a high-assist guard; Stephen Curry (round 2): Playable but risky; Warriors may be in a gap season and he is not a high-assist guy. Avoid with this anchor: Walker Kessler, Donovan Clingan, Evan Mobley, Domantas Sabonis.

pairings.build: No forced punt; optional punt blocks and/or turnovers
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Easiest player to build around. Any second or third-rounder who beats ADP fits except block specialists. A high-turnover guy is fine since Jokic is at 3.7. Partners: Austin Reaves (round 2): Implied: take whoever beats 9-cat ADP near pick 23, and Reaves is the one he thinks does. Avoid with this anchor: Chet Holmgren, Evan Mobley, Domantas Sabonis, Kawhi Leonard, LaMelo Ball, Stephen Curry, Trae Young.

pairings.build: Second-round pick decides the punt
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Luka gives points, threes, 8 rebounds and assists but percentages are a negative, so whatever percentage the second-rounder is bad at, you punt. Partner should be high scoring to protect the points lead. Partners: Trae Young (round 2 (pick 22)): Makes it punt FG% plus punt TO; could make it back to 22; Josh Giddey (round 2): Makes it punt TO and probably punt FT%; Dan is lukewarm because of low scoring. Avoid with this anchor: Chet Holmgren, Domantas Sabonis.

pairings.build: Well-rounded percentages team (preferred)
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Take the player you think has the best year near your pick and do not put a hole in his percentages without a big win elsewhere. Partners: Austin Reaves (round 2 (pick 21)): Favorite pair; doubles down on percentages; Trae Young (round 2): Big win in points, threes and assists justifies the FG% hit; lets you take a bad-FT big later. Avoid with this anchor: LaMelo Ball, Alperen Sengun.

pairings.build: Punt threes
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Shai hits only 1.7 threes, lowest in round one, and moves even higher up the board when you punt them. Partners: Amen Thompson (round 2): 18/8/5 last year, piles on defensive stats, efficient, low turnovers; 17th in punt threes last year; Chet Holmgren (round 3): Great third-round pick in punt threes; Devin Booker (round 2): Not horrible: only about two threes, keeps scoring up, but low defensive numbers; Josh Giddey (round 2): Low-threes option if he gets there, but feels like a double punt.

pairings.build: Punt assists
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Harder to pull off right now than punt threes. Partners: Stephen Curry (round 2): Low-assist guard, but Dan fears his season; Jalen Brunson (round 2): Not a super high assist guard; unenthusiastic; Trey Murphy III (round 3): Probable third-round pick in this build.

pairings.build: Punt points
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Shai's percentage impact on volume is so large that low scorers around him still win FG% and FT%. Partners: Chet Holmgren (round 2 or 3): High-percentages big; sets up rebounds, steals, blocks, both percentages and turnovers.

pairings.build: Guard build: punt FG% and TO
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Cade does not score a ton, so the second-rounder must bring about 25 points (20-plus from a big). This year you can stack three of Cade, Trae, Harden and LaMelo. Add steals by round 5. Partners: Trae Young (round 2 (pick 20)): Best pair; should be there coming back; Karl-Anthony Towns (round 2): Guard-build big: scoring, threes, good FT%, a couple of assists, a steal, no blocks; Austin Reaves (round 2); LaMelo Ball (round 2): One click down; James Harden (round 3): Should be gettable in the third round; Josh Giddey (round 2): Last option; does not score enough. Avoid with this anchor: Amen Thompson, Chet Holmgren, Jamal Murray.

pairings.build: Well-rounded, punt chosen later
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Maxey is at 2.7 steals plus blocks from a guard. Do not surrender that start. Take a big in round 3. Partners: Jamal Murray (round 2): Favorite: points, threes, decent assists, same steals, keeps TO and FG% good; Austin Reaves (round 2): Expected overperformer; Karl-Anthony Towns (round 2): Leans guard build; costs blocks edge but Maxey covers it. Not a favorite; Amen Thompson (round 2): Turns it into a percentages, defensive stats and turnover team at the cost of points and threes. Avoid with this anchor: Trae Young.

pairings.build: Well-rounded, likely punt steals (or assists and steals)
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Tatum's weakness is steals and blocks, his outlier strength is rebounds for his position. Partners: Jamal Murray (round 2): Preferred; helps FG%, keeps points, threes, FT% and turnovers good; Kevin Durant (round 2): Backup; doubles down on scoring, threes, rebounds, FT%; better blocks; Karl-Anthony Towns (round 2): Protects the rebounding edge in a guard-build flavor; Austin Reaves (round 2); Scottie Barnes (round 2): Interesting roto-style pair but will not make it back. Avoid with this anchor: Amen Thompson.

pairings.build: Punt assists lean
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Edwards is at 3.7 assists, weakest of the group, and 2.2 steals plus blocks. Better chance at Murray or Reaves because the pick comes back sooner. Partners: Jamal Murray (round 2): Value is efficiency, not assists; Austin Reaves (round 2); Kevin Durant (round 2): Added live: not a big assist guy; Karl-Anthony Towns (round 2): Backup. Avoid with this anchor: LaMelo Ball, Trae Young, Alperen Sengun, Domantas Sabonis.

pairings.build: Punt FT% (maybe TO too)
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Get outside scoring and assists early because rebounds, blocks and FG% come from cheap punt-FT bigs later. Dan takes Giannis at 6. Partners: Alperen Sengun (round 2): Top choice: a big with steals, 20-plus points and assists; Trae Young (round 2): 23 to 26 points and big assists; Jamal Murray (round 2): Backup; you waste his FG% value; Amen Thompson (round 2): Backup; fit is great but not enough points; Scottie Barnes (round 2): Backup; want more scoring. Avoid with this anchor: Jalen Duren.

pairings.build: Punt blocks if Mitchell is there; otherwise attack blocks or punt points
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Johnson is a worse Jokic in every category, so you must find five categories where a Jokic team is not targeting. Partners: Donovan Mitchell (round 2 (pick 15)): Preferred: rescues scoring, threes, FT%, adds steals. Probably gone; Cooper Flagg (round 2): Upside pick that helps beat Jokic teams in blocks; Amen Thompson (round 2): Leans into punt points; Scottie Barnes (round 2): Same idea: rebounds, assists, steals, blocks, turnovers. Avoid with this anchor: Karl-Anthony Towns, Devin Booker, LaMelo Ball.

pairings.build: Hyper-efficient, assists as a 50/50 category
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Same plan as Maxey but simpler because Mitchell does not block shots. You beat guard-build teams in FG% and turnovers and stay competitive in FT%. Partners: Kevin Durant (round 2 (pick 14 or 15)): Good shot he is there; semi-fixes blocks; Jamal Murray (round 2); Austin Reaves (round 2); Cooper Flagg (round 2): Reasonable, not the favorite. Avoid with this anchor: Scottie Barnes, Chet Holmgren.

pairings.build: Punt points
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Haliburton is far behind in points but has a huge turnover edge and can catch Jokic and Cade teams in assists. Partners: Scottie Barnes (round 2 (pick 13)): Rebounds, assists, steals, blocks, solid percentages, low turnovers; Josh Giddey (round 2): Moved up to an option, but you must add a volume-efficiency player in round 3; Kawhi Leonard (round 3): The volume-efficiency guy, if you accept the games risk; Chet Holmgren (round 3): Hope he falls to the end of the third.

pairings.build: Efficient well-rounded team or low-turnover guard build
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Not a clear punt-points roster but efficient enough to work. Dan worries Indiana babies Haliburton early. Partners: Kevin Durant (round 2): Efficient volume that props up both percentages; Cooper Flagg (round 2): Super well-rounded; Jamal Murray (round 2): Hyper-efficient, light on defensive stats; Austin Reaves (round 2): A bit worse in turnovers; Trae Young (round 2): Two 10-assist guards and you still beat punt-TO teams in turnovers. Avoid with this anchor: LaMelo Ball.

pairings.build: Guard-stats build: win PTS, 3PM, AST, STL, FT%; ignore REB, BLK, FG% and TO (four-category punt)
pairings.why: Adam King: Adam King's actual team, picks in order: R1 Haliburton (12th), R2 Edwards (13th), R3 LaMelo (25th, third-round reversal), R4 Jaylen Brown (48th), R5 Garland (49th), R6 Lillard (72nd), R7 Jerome, R8 Porzingis, R9 Zion (accidental autopick he dislikes), R10 Jalen Green, R11 Melton, R12 Grayson Allen, R13 Fears, R14 Henderson. Haliburton gives every guard stat except big scoring, so round 2 had to be a high-volume scorer (Edwards). Porzingis was the lone center because he fits the build; King would not draft only one center in a normal head-to-head league and is happy with 60 games from him.

pairings.build: Punt 3PM and FT% (assists a swing category)
pairings.why: Adam King/RotoWire: Alex Barutha's actual team in round order: Giannis (round 1, caption reads 'at 18' but context implies 8th), Sengun, Mobley, Sabonis, Banchero, Edey, Fox, Hart, Mitchell, Nurkic, Barrett, DeRozan, Holiday, Gafford. Sengun, Mobley and Sabonis supply the big-man stats and passing. Banchero was a fallback after Dyson Daniels went one pick earlier (54th); Nurkic was a pivot after Cason Wallace was sniped at 107. King's critique: steals are the risk without a Daniels or Wallace, and Rudy Gobert would have been a safer fit than Edey on health. Alex says he could have reached for Daniels in round 4 or Ausar Thompson (went 74th) in round 6 instead of Edey.

pairings.build: Punt points and threes: win defensive stats, rebounds, FG%, with assists still competitive
pairings.why: Adam King: DMac (NBA Fantasy Bible)'s team: Barnes 9th, Johnson 16th, then Holmgren, Murray, Daniels (54th), Thompson (74th), Queta and Gobert later. King says this is the build he usually drafts himself and that Johnson is a fine pairing with Barnes because they share a skill set and leave you strong in assists, rebounds and defense. Barnes gives about 2.5 combined steals and blocks.

pairings.build: Balanced, high-ceiling wing/guard start
pairings.why: Adam King/RotoWire: Analyst 'Point Made' took Tatum in round 1, Kawhi 19th, then Harden and Kyrie. Alex calls Tatum plus Kawhi very synergistic for 9-cat; King says Kawhi's skill set pairs with almost anyone (Tatum, Cooper Flagg, Cade Cunningham) but the games-played risk in round 2 is high, and notes the team leans on older players.

pairings.build: Efficient scoring build (points, threes, percentages)
pairings.why: RotoWire: Analyst 'D-Rock' passed on Jalen Johnson for Durant, took Markkanen at 26 because he would not last until his next pick, and Paul George at 50.
