pairings.anchor: Punt FG% and FT% ('box score' build)
pairings.build: Points-league-style counting-stats team in a 9-cat league, punting percentages
pairings.why: RotoWire: Kirien Sprecher built this kind of team and took Randle at 88; Randle fits because his volume counting stats come with poor efficiency.

pairings.build: Punt 3PM and FT%: recommended fits that Alex missed
pairings.why: Adam King/RotoWire: King and Alex agree these are the pieces a Giannis punt build needs: steals from Daniels, Wallace and Thompson (their threes and FT% do not matter to you) and a safe non-shooting big like Gobert or Queta.

pairings.build: Guard build, punt turnovers (treat as 8-cat)
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: High-turnover, high-assist guards used to all go in round 1; now they are in rounds 2 and 3. Beat Luka and Jokic teams in points, threes, assists, steals and FT%. Cade jumps from 17th to 8th without turnovers. Partners: Trae Young (round 2 (pick 20)): Usually still there at 20; LaMelo Ball (round 2): Still on the board coming back; James Harden (round 2 or 3): Still on the board coming back.

pairings.build: Punt FT%
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: You already know you are punting free throws, so plan which guard categories to add: points first, then steals or assists. Partners: Alperen Sengun (round 2): If you can get him; Trae Young (round early): High-assist guard to add guard categories; Zion Williamson (round later): Punt-FT piece later on.

pairings.anchor: Any first-rounder (especially Maxey, Edwards, Mitchell, Tatum)
pairings.build: Well-rounded, punt decided later
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: These five are well-rounded with upside and pair with everybody. The punt could end up assists, steals (Tatum) or FG%. Partners: Cooper Flagg (round 2 (pick 13)); Kevin Durant (round 2); Jamal Murray (round 2); Scottie Barnes (round 2); Austin Reaves (round 2).

pairings.build: Steve's team from pick 3 in a 9-cat Yahoo mock: guards early, then per-game talent with injury risk, balanced by safe picks and centres
pairings.why: Steve St-Pierre: Rounds 2-4 are three injury dice rolls taken for per-game talent (Curry falling on health and Warriors question marks, Davis the best big on the board, Irving looking smooth in preseason). Okongwu and Anunoby in rounds 5-6 are the safe balance, Embiid in round 7 for upside in a two-centre format, Murray-Boyles and Turner lock up bigs, Dosunmu for SG eligibility, Butler as an IL stash. Steve says only do this with several IL spots.

pairings.build: Leo's team from pick 4: guard-heavy points, assists, threes and free throw build (FG% is the acknowledged weak spot with Young)
pairings.why: Fantasy on Points: Built the guard foundation with Doncic, Ball and Young to lock assists, points, threes and FT. Brown is a floor pick, Buzelis and Jerome are upside picks that fit the build, Edey is the potential league winner at centre, Maluach a talent bet, Jaquez the safe one, then three young prospects and a Lendeborg/Santos Warriors mini handcuff. Leo wanted Austin Reaves in round 2 to pair with Doncic but D-Mac took him.

pairings.build: D-Mac's team from pick 7: balanced 9-cat build that went centre-heavy early, then chased assists and guards
pairings.why: NBA Fantasy Bible: Reaves in round 2, then Holmgren and Clingan to beef up centre. Having gone heavy on centres he targeted assists in round 5 (Murray, a steals guy) and took Herro in round 6 because guards were drying up. George is a mini handcuff with Tatum, Sharpe a breakout centre, Suggs fell, Poeltl looked healthy, Mitchell fell past ADP, Allen for a hot start, Sheppard as a last-round value.

pairings.build: Miami Heat stack by another drafter
pairings.why: NBA Fantasy Bible/Steve St-Pierre: Adebayo was taken at 2.7 by the manager who took Giannis at six; the hosts called it gutsy and too early.

pairings.build: Punt FG%, punt TO, or both
pairings.why: Noah Rubin: High-usage rookie point guard who will score and assist but shoot around 40% with turnovers; a great later-round pick in those builds.

pairings.build: Balanced 9-cat build, no punt, anchored on elite blocks
pairings.why: Hustle Sports: T-Will's template by player type, not a literal roster: (1) Wembanyama for blocks, (2) a playmaking forward for assists (Johnson, Barnes or Sengun), (3) an efficient threes source (Gillespie late; Bane, Knueppel or Porter mid), (4) a steals specialist (Daniels, Herb Jones, Amen or Ausar Thompson), (5) a low-turnover balanced wing (Anunoby, Bridges, McDaniels), (6) an FG% and rebounding big (Clingan, Gobert, Duren, Robinson), (7) a multi-category upside pick (Buzelis, Sarr).

pairings.build: Injury hedge
pairings.why: Number Two Sports: Black is the direct beneficiary whenever Suggs misses time, so he is the target for managers who fade Suggs or want insurance.

pairings.build: Perfect-draft walkthrough with pick 1 (12-team snake, picks 1, 24, 25, 48, 49, 72, 73, 96, 97, 120)
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Not one fixed build: Jokic plus branches. Options are a non-shot-blocking big to punt blocks, or an assists guard with turnovers punted. Honorable mentions are roughly equal to the listed picks. Partner rounds: Austin Reaves R2 (pick 24); Chet Holmgren R3 (pick 25); James Harden R3; Trey Murphy III R3; Lauri Markkanen R3; Stephen Curry R2 or 3; Amen Thompson R2 or 3; Bam Adebayo R3; Jalen Duren R3; Kyrie Irving R4 (pick 48); Anthony Davis R4; Dejounte Murray R5 (pick 49); Onyeka Okongwu R5; Nickeil Alexander-Walker R5; Dyson Daniels R5; Michael Porter Jr. R5; Kel'el Ware R6 (pick 72); Ryan Rollins R6; OG Anunoby R6; Paul George R7 (pick 73); Norman Powell R7; Andrew Wiggins R8 (pick 96); Jalen Suggs R9 (pick 97); Josh Hart R9; Myles Turner R9; Ja Morant R9; Keegan Murray R10 (pick 120); Neemias Queta R10; Reed Sheppard R10; Kevin Porter Jr. R10. Avoid with this anchor: Domantas Sabonis, LaMelo Ball, Devin Booker, Alperen Sengun.

pairings.build: Punt points and/or punt assists
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: If you pair Holmgren with any of the top four it should be Shai. Dan has built a Shai punt-points team before. Partners: Chet Holmgren (round 2 (pick 21 to 24)): Bolsters percentages and defensive stats and adds threes from a center.

pairings.build: Low-scoring build
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Holmgren goes with players taken a bit later who are slightly lower scoring; Jalen Johnson and Cade Cunningham were named as similar fits. Partners: Chet Holmgren (round 2 or 3): Fits best with lower-scoring anchors.

pairings.build: Pairing to avoid
pairings.why: Locked On: Kawhi could be value in round 3 and Davis is a must-draft at 45, but Lloyd 'wouldn't stack the risk players on top of each other'.

pairings.build: ESPN-rank value stack for rounds 2-3
pairings.why: Locked On: On ESPN's ranks Lloyd describes taking a first-rounder, then a player ranked 24 in round 2 and Jamal Murray at 28 in round 3, where 'both guys might be inside the top 14'. The round-2 name is garbled in the captions; his ESPN round-2 must-drafts were Giannis (rank 20) and Cooper Flagg (rank 24).

pairings.build: Guard build, punt turnovers (usually FG% too)
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Guard build lets a Cade team catch Jokic in points and threes and beat him in assists, steals and FT% while conceding turnovers, FG%, rebounds and probably blocks. Partners: Trae Young (round 2): Team becomes good in threes, great in assists, adequate in steals, very good in FT%; Bam Adebayo (round 3): Big who gives points, threes, steals and rebounds; rebounds become the sixth category; Karl-Anthony Towns (round 2): Points, threes and FT% from a big plus rebounds; James Harden (round 2 or 3): Moves up the board in this build; LaMelo Ball (round 2): Moves up the board in this build; Jaren Jackson Jr. (round 4 or 5): Example of a scoring, shot-blocking big who does not rebound.

pairings.build: Punt FT%
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: FG%, rebounds and blocks come later from traditional punt-FT shot-blocking bigs. Partners: Alperen Sengun (round 2): Scoring, assists and steals from a big are what the build lacks early.

pairings.build: Punt points
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Either lock in volume percentages early or pile onto the defensive and rebounding frame. Steals and blocks come later. Partners: Kevin Durant (round 2): Picked in a recent mock: 52/87 on volume locks in both percentages; Scottie Barnes (round 2): Rebounds, assists, steals, blocks, okay percentages.

pairings.build: Punt blocks plus one percentage, or low-scoring pair
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Johnson is a poor man's Jokic, so Dan leans away from him unless the pair changes the shape of the team. Partners: Scottie Barnes (round 2): Helps fix what is wrong with Johnson if you then stop caring about free throws.

pairings.build: Punt steals
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Murray's one weakness is steals, which is also Tatum's. Partners: Jamal Murray (round 2): Called a great pairing.

pairings.build: Punt threes
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Thompson has no obvious punt besides threes or points. Partners: Amen Thompson (round 2): Strong defensive stats, good percentages, low turnovers; costs some scoring.

pairings.build: Weakest four: threes, assists, turnovers, steals. Likely punt steals, assists, turnovers
pairings.why: Adam King: Assists are the obvious punt. Threes from a center matter less now. Partners: Chet Holmgren (round 2 (pick 24)): Perfect start with Wemby; both hit threes so that category can be rebuilt later; Amen Thompson (round 2): Secondary option.

pairings.build: Weakest four: threes, turnovers, blocks, FG% (relative to centers)
pairings.why: Adam King: Blocks are below average for a center. Pairing Jokic with a Jokic-lite (Sabonis, or Sengun as the same type) makes sense. Partners: Josh Giddey (round 2): Out-of-position rebounds, assists, some steals, weak threes, fine FG%; Amen Thompson (round 2); Domantas Sabonis (round 2 (pick 23, a reach)): A Jokic-lite: no blocks, no threes, good FG%, high turnovers.

pairings.build: Punt blocks, FG%, FT%, turnovers; chase points, threes, assists, steals, rebounds
pairings.why: Adam King: Luka's free throws have improved but are not elite, so punting percentages and blocks leaves pure counting stats. Partners: LaMelo Ball (round 2): Points, threes, assists, steals, fine guard rebounds; FG% and streaky FT% ignored; Josh Giddey (round 2): Rebounds and assists; low points offset by Luka.

pairings.build: Weakest four: rebounds, threes, blocks, turnovers
pairings.why: Adam King: Shai is hard to build around because he is good across the board; he hits few threes for a 30-point guard and rebounds little next to Chet and Hartenstein. Partners: Austin Reaves (round 2 (pick 20 or 21)): Similar skill set; Kawhi Leonard (round 2 (pick 20)): Pairs with many anchors but missed-games risk.

pairings.build: Weakest four: rebounds, FG%, FT%, turnovers
pairings.why: Adam King: Cade gives points and assists with few threes and average percentages. Partners: Stephen Curry (round 2): Bumps points and threes; fine assists and steals; his risk is offset by Cade's durability; Josh Giddey (round 2): Assists and some defensive stats, no threes or free throws.

pairings.build: Punt threes, FT%, turnovers (steals are his fourth-weakest but King would not punt them)
pairings.why: Adam King: Easy to build around, but his defensive stats have declined so add them early. Partners: Amen Thompson (round 2): Supplies the steals and blocks Giannis no longer gives; Chet Holmgren (round 2): Named alongside; Walker Kessler (round later): If there; Dyson Daniels (round later); Ausar Thompson (round later).

pairings.build: Guard build: punt rebounds, blocks, FG%, turnovers
pairings.why: Adam King: Easiest four-category punt: points, threes, assists, steals, FT%. Maxey's ADP has moved between 7 and 12 and should settle at 7 to 9. Partners: Trae Young (round 2 (pick 17)): Elite assists, average steals, good FT%; likely available at 17; Tyrese Haliburton (round 2 (pick 17)): About 50/50 to be there; Austin Reaves (round 2).

pairings.build: Punt rebounds, FG%, turnovers, blocks
pairings.why: Adam King: Relatively easy to build around. Partners: Kevin Durant (round 2 (pick 16 or 17)): First-round upside and durable lately; Donovan Mitchell (round 2): Usually goes 14 or 15, so only if lucky.

pairings.build: Weakest four: threes, FG%, turnovers, rebounds
pairings.why: Adam King: Flagg is balanced, so not an easy punt anchor. Partners: Tyrese Haliburton (round 2 (pick 15)): Assists and steals, good FT%; both block well for their positions; Trae Young (round 2): Alternative.

pairings.build: Punt blocks, FG%, turnovers, steals
pairings.why: Adam King: Tatum gives points, threes, assists and rebounds with little defense, so target players whose value is not built on defense. Partners: Stephen Curry (round 2): King leans Curry as the better per-game option; Tatum's health offsets his risk; Trae Young (round 2).

pairings.build: Punt threes, blocks, FG%, turnovers
pairings.why: Adam King: Towns matches Johnson's assists and rebounding profile and shares his weak categories. Partners: Karl-Anthony Towns (round 2): One of King's favorite pairs: rebounds, assists, strong FT%, few blocks, non-elite FG%; Donovan Mitchell (round 2): Lines up well.

pairings.build: Big-man build: punt points, threes, FT%; target rebounds, blocks, FG%, steals, low turnovers
pairings.why: Adam King: Barnes and Amen give rebounds, steals, blocks, fine FG% and good turnovers without using a center slot. King made the playoffs in 10 of 11 leagues with this build last season and won four. Partners: Amen Thompson (round 2 (pick 13)): Favorite pairing; should be there; Walker Kessler (round 3 (pick 25 with third-round reversal)): A bit of a shot at 25; Anthony Davis (round 3 (pick 25 with third-round reversal)): Great fit, higher injury risk than Kessler; Dyson Daniels (round next pick after round 3); Ausar Thompson (round pick after Daniels); Khaman Maluach (round late): Late center target; Jalen Johnson (round 2): Alternative second-round partner.

pairings.build: Triple punt: threes, FT%, turnovers (big-man build plus assists and steals)
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Castle is the guard for a big-man build; in a six-category team that ignores threes, free throws and turnovers he grades top 60 and justifies a seventh-round pick. Giannis build only.

pairings.build: Pick 11, 12-team 9-cat H2H mock with third-round reversal. No punt named. Strengths by Lloyd's read: assists, steals, points, threes, free throws, solid blocks. Weakness: rebounds and bigs. Projected 10th in a tightly bunched room; Lloyd said the team 'is just not coming together well'.
pairings.why: Locked On: R1 (11) Maxey: 'shoehorned' in because he liked Jalen Johnson and Haliburton less. R2 (14) Scottie Barnes: a panic pick off the top of his queue when the clock ran out; he would probably have taken Jamal Murray. R3 (26) Anthony Davis: usually someone he considers there and has looked pretty good in preseason, though he hesitated to put him on a Barnes team. R4 (47) Jaren Jackson Jr.: Jaylen Brown, his intended pick, was taken, and he chose Jackson over Keyonte George. R5 (50) Ryan Rollins: over Matas Buzelis and Cameron Boozer, with the job now secure. R6 (71) Desmond Bane: Michael Porter Jr. and Lillard were both taken just ahead of him, and Bane had fallen. R7 (74) Ty Jerome: wanted him over Dylan Harper. R8 (95) De'Aaron Fox: Day'Ron Sharpe was sniped one pick earlier and Fox was 'way too late' to pass. R9 (98) Brandin Podziemski: over Ja Morant. R10 (119) Darius Acuff Jr.: flyer. R11 (122) Fred VanVleet: fell far past where he normally goes. R12 (143) Kevin Porter Jr.: upside flyer. R13 (146) Isaiah Jackson: flyer on a big. R14 (167) Jalen Smith: needed a big; passed on Jrue Holiday.

pairings.build: What Lloyd says he would have done in round 2 at pick 14
pairings.why: Locked On: Asked himself who he would have taken instead of the Barnes panic pick: 'probably maybe Murray'.

pairings.build: Another drafter's round 1-2 start
pairings.why: Locked On: Lloyd flagged the Giddey half with concern over Giddey's quiet preseason (low rebounds, usage and assists).

pairings.build: Another drafter's late picks on the Jokic team
pairings.why: Locked On: The Jokic drafter took a center the captions render as 'Nemaska' (most likely Neemias Queta) and Jakob Poeltl at the 9/10 turn; Lloyd called it 'two big plodding field goal percentage guys for the Jokic team, interesting combo'. He called the later Mamukelashvili pick good.

pairings.build: Punt blocks, guard build plus rebounds
pairings.why: Noah Rubin: Rubin: take Cade Cunningham, Anthony Edwards or Tyrese Maxey in round one and Towns at about pick 15 to 16, lean into punting blocks, and assists end up strong even without loading up on them early.

pairings.build: Punt blocks, guard build plus rebounds
pairings.why: Noah Rubin: Same Rubin suggestion: first-round guard or wing then Towns in the early second, punting blocks.

pairings.build: Punt blocks, guard build plus rebounds
pairings.why: Noah Rubin: Same Rubin suggestion: first-round guard then Towns in the early second, punting blocks.

pairings.build: Assist-heavy guard build with one big-man category (rebounds)
pairings.why: Noah Rubin: Rubin's example of pairing Towns with a high-assist guard: Towns adds threes and rebounds without sinking FG% the way stacking guards normally does. Besbris frames it as a guard build that still wins rebounds.

pairings.build: Real-life fit note, not a fantasy build
pairings.why: Noah Rubin: Rubin likes Memphis's two-big look: Boozer facilitates and Edey supplies the shot blocking Boozer lacks, with both strong on the glass.

pairings.build: Guard build: points, threes, assists, steals, FT%
pairings.why: Adam King: King's actual draft from pick 12: Haliburton, then Anthony Edwards at 13 to cover the points Haliburton lacks, then Jaylen Brown and Darius Garland for scoring, Zion Williamson (an admitted mistake: points and assists but no threes and poor FT%), and Jalen Green and Jeremiah Fears late. King said the result was fine but he was not thrilled.

pairings.build: Not specified
pairings.why: Adam King: King says that with the first pick, if Amen is still there at 24, the pairing works.

pairings.build: Punt or complement
pairings.why: Adam King: King calls Amen quite a nice pairing with Jokic, either in a punt or as a complement to what Jokic does.

pairings.build: Punt FT% and threes
pairings.why: Adam King: Amen fits the Giannis punt free throw and threes build really well.

pairings.build: Punt points and threes
pairings.why: Adam King: Barnes has a Yahoo ADP of 12, so at the 12/13 turn King pairs him with Amen and goes punt points and threes; he does this a lot.

pairings.build: Punt points, threes, assists, FT%
pairings.why: Adam King: King usually ends up with both brothers: defensive stats, rebounds, FG% and low turnovers. Ausar is 'like a first round player' in this build and King takes him in the 50s or 60s, well ahead of his 89.7 ADP.

pairings.build: Balanced, light on points
pairings.why: Adam King: Holmgren does not hurt FT%, which protects Haliburton's FT%-driven value; the pair is competitive in threes, rebounds, assists, steals, blocks and both percentages, with points the weak spot.

pairings.build: Balanced, light on points
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Besbris suggests Holmgren fits best with the lower-scoring first-rounders such as Haliburton, Jalen Johnson or Cade Cunningham rather than behind Anthony Edwards or Jayson Tatum; King agrees.

pairings.build: Balanced, light on points
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Same Besbris suggestion: Holmgren's low scoring is easier to absorb next to a first-rounder who is not a top scorer.

pairings.build: Counting-stats build (points, assists, threes), accepting weak FG%, turnovers and defensive stats
pairings.why: SportsEthos: If you took Doncic in round one and want more counting stats, Acuff in the early-to-mid 100s gives points, assists and threes even though he grades badly on efficiency and turnovers.

pairings.build: Miami Heat stack
pairings.why: Hustle Sports: T-Will wants at least one of Giannis, Adebayo or Wiggins and would stream Thompson, on the view that Giannis' playmaking with better shooters lifts the whole group.

pairings.build: Injury handcuff
pairings.why: RotoWire: Whalen drafts Stewart late as a hedge in case Edey misses significant time in Memphis.

pairings.build: Punt FT%
pairings.why: RotoWire: Nurkic was about a top-55 player last year excluding FT%; Gobert gives rebounds and blocks with terrible FT% and no threes.

pairings.anchor: Beast mode (FG%, REB, BLK, STL, low TO)
pairings.build: Win FG%, rebounds, blocks, steals and turnovers 5-4 each week; give up the other four
pairings.why: The Roster Report: Bam: points, rebounds, stocks, FG%, fewer turnovers next to Giannis. Hart: rebounds, assists, FG%, low turnovers, few points. White: rebounds for a guard, assists, steals, very low turnovers. Tre Jones: best assist-to-turnover ratio, 55% FG, cheap. Reid and Gobert are the preferred bigs.

pairings.build: Punt FT%
pairings.why: SportsEthos: Dr. A: if you draft Giannis you may as well end up with Gobert, plus Castle and Sengun, since all of them hurt free throw percentage.

pairings.build: Pick 1, 12-team 9-cat H2H mock with third-round reversal. No punt named; balanced build that finished first in projected standings. Self-identified weak spot: threes.
pairings.why: Locked On: R1 (1) Jokic. R2 (24) Anthony Davis: 'I hate it', but Jokic gives a level of security that lets him absorb Davis's risk; alternatives he felt worse about were Kyrie Irving, Brandon Miller, Garland, Sabonis and Bam. R3 (36) Darius Garland: wanted Brandon Miller or Trey Murphy, both sniped; took Garland despite 'Clippers risk worries'. R4 (37) Jaylen Brown: 'a reverse nine cat fluffer' whose category downsides Lloyd thinks are overstated; he had two centers so did not need another, and his next pick was 60. R5 (60) Franz Wagner over Kel'el Ware. R6 (61) Ryan Rollins: thinks he is locked in despite Milwaukee's guard logjam. R7 (84) Brandin Podziemski: expects him to start; Day'Ron Sharpe and Caleb Wilson were sniped. R8 (85) Jarrett Allen: 'a little boring', another center, chosen over Gobert to protect free throws. R9 (108) Zach LaVine: wanted an assist/scoring guard; passed on Poeltl (best projection) and Fears. R10 (109) Egor Demin: flyer at the turn. R11 (132) Cameron Johnson: could be significantly better than last year; his queue targets Grayson Allen and Kevin Porter Jr. were both taken. R12 (133) Sandro Mamukelashvili: see how much the Lakers use him. R13 (156) Nikola Vucevic: beats the price if he gets 23-24 minutes; Ace Bailey and Collin Gillespie were sniped. R14 (157) Jalen Smith: early-season flyer with Claxton hurt.

pairings.build: Round 3 partner Lloyd wanted
pairings.why: Locked On: 'I loved a Banchero pick to go with Jokic' in round 3; another drafter took him before pick 36.

pairings.build: Lloyd's own industry draft, picking 5
pairings.why: Locked On: Lloyd took Giannis at 5 in a concurrent industry league and Amen Thompson came back to him in round 2. He contrasts it with the room's 'classic pairing' of Giannis plus Alperen Sengun, which he says is unnecessary: you do not need another bad free-throw shooter with Giannis, and Sengun does not help threes or steals.

pairings.build: 12/13 turn
pairings.why: Locked On: A Durant at 12 plus Maxey at 13 turn is 'fine', though Lloyd is cool on Maxey.

pairings.build: Punt threes, punt assists or punt points
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: No partners named. Fill with low-scoring players who are okay at percentages. Do not build punt FT% after taking him.

pairings.build: Punt points (the only real catch-up route)
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: No partner named: the second-round pick has to be the optimal punt-points combo player to catch Jokic teams.

pairings.build: Efficiency guard build (low turnovers)
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: High assists like Cade but about two fewer turnovers, so you can stack higher-turnover guards on top and still beat Cade and Jokic teams in turnovers.

pairings.build: Assists anchor at the back of round 2 or in round 3; requires building FG% later
pairings.why: NBA Fantasy Bible: Locking down assists early is smart, but his FG% deficiency has to be repaired with later picks.

pairings.build: FG% repair for rosters with high-volume, poor-shooting scorers
pairings.why: Hustle Sports: His high FG% on inside finishes plus rebounds and blocks 'can help curb' the percentage damage; worth a modest reach.

pairings.build: Punt assists; lean into steals, points, threes
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: No partner named, only a warning: Trae Young ruins FG% and only lifts assists from bad to average. Avoid with this anchor: Trae Young.

pairings.build: No clear punt; efficient low-turnover team
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Second and third-round picks dictate the punt. Avoid with this anchor: Scottie Barnes.

pairings.build: No forced punt
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: If you think punt turnovers you accidentally draft a bunch of guards. Just take the best fantasy players.

pairings.build: Punt FT% or punt FG%
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: A fifth or sixth round Banchero works in punt FT% (protects against his free throws regressing) or punt FG% (where the rest of the roster has enough FT% to cover him), because few players in that range give 22 points, 8 rebounds and 5 assists.

pairings.build: Punt guard stats, or as the steals piece of a guard build
pairings.why: Adam King: King: perfect for a punt guard-stats team; alternatively, if your first three or four picks loaded points, threes and FT%, Daniels can anchor steals for a guard squad.

pairings.build: Punt FG%
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Morant will take and miss a lot of shots in Portland; Besbris says he could be a four-airplane value at 94 only on a team punting FG%.

pairings.build: Punt points or punt FT%
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Late-round starting center who becomes a top 100 option if you are already ignoring points or free throws.

pairings.build: Punt free throws (turnovers conceded)
pairings.why: Locked On: Taken at 5 in H2H categories. Do not punt three categories: punt free throws, ignore turnovers, and get threes, assists and steals from guards taken 'somewhat early', including guards with high free-throw percentages. Do not fill the roster with bad free-throw shooters. No specific partners named in this video.

pairings.build: Punt blocks
pairings.why: RotoWire/NBA Fantasy Bible: Blocks are his only clear weak category, so in a minus-one (punt blocks) context he is a late-first to early-second-round value.

pairings.build: Triple punt: blocks, steals, threes ('punting 3-and-D')
pairings.why: RotoWire: Only in an Adam King-style triple or quadruple punt does Banchero justify a third or fourth-round pick.

pairings.build: Multi-punt
pairings.why: NBA Fantasy Bible: Taking Giannis forces you to punt multiple categories from the start.

pairings.build: Forces a punt build (FT%) from round one
pairings.why: NBA Fantasy Bible/League Winner Sports: He 'forces your hand' and takes more skill to build around; both D-Mac and Matt would rather stay balanced early. No specific partners named.

pairings.build: Punt turnovers (treat as 8-cat)
pairings.why: NBA Fantasy Bible: Elite point guard assists outweigh the turnover hit if you ignore the category.

pairings.build: Fits a build that already tolerates poor FT%
pairings.why: League Winner Sports: James says he is a good pick only once your build has taken a shape that fits his FT% and low stocks.

pairings.build: Narrow three-category punt angle (points, rebounds, assists) in head-to-head
pairings.why: SportsEthos: Bruski says the angle only makes sense if you believe he steps forward and keeps his shots, which he does not; no partners named.

pairings.build: Punt threes, punt points or punt FT%
pairings.why: Old Man Squad: Besbris calls him a 'triple breakout star' in any of those three punts: projected 10 points, 6 rebounds, 4.5 assists, 2.5 steals and 1.3 blocks with no threes and poor FT%.
